# THEATER OF POISONERS AND SORCERERS.

# Concerning Devilish Apparitions, Magicians, and
## Preparers of Poison / Practitioners of the Black Arts / Witches and Monster-folk / many distinguished histories and examples / from proven / credible / old and new writers / regarding what has been disputed and held at all times concerning such people / published with special diligence (the list of whom is to be found on the following page).

->Including the confessions made by several executed witch-women / **Examination**, trial / testimony and punishment / **etc.** Brought together now anew into one **Body of Work** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> / for the sake of many differing questions and opinions which may arise in this matter.<-

->Very useful and profitable for all governors / mayors / officials of the secular sword / **etc.** to know / and by no means to be disregarded.<-

# To the Honorable, Prudent,
### Respectable, and Wise Gentlemen, the Mayors and
### Citizens, as well as the Council of the ancient Free Imperial
### City of Worms, etc., my highly favoring masters
### and especially good friends: Fortune
### and Salvation.

<image-desc>A large ornamental woodcut initial 'E' depicting a figure (possibly a scholar or saint) holding a book and a staff, surrounded by intricate foliage and strapwork.</image-desc>

Honorable, Prudent, Respectable, and Wise Gentlemen, my diligent and entirely willing services are at all times at the disposal of Your Honors, Wisdoms, and Graces <note>The abbreviation "E. E. F. W. vnd G." stands for "Eure Ehrnveſte, Fürſichtige, Weiſe und Gunsten," a formal string of honorifics</note>, my highly favoring masters: In ancient times, one of the Seven Sages of Greece, named Solon—born on the island of Salamis—was asked why he had established no law against those who might kill their fathers or mothers, etc. To this he replied: He did not believe that a person could ever be found who would even dare to take such a cruel deed into their mind, let alone venture to carry it out. This would indeed have been very well said, had Solon not been deceived in his opinion. For truly, it is in itself a very evil deed when one human being (whether a blood relative or not) takes the life of another—something which does not even happen among wild animals of the same name and species. But that one should kill his own biological parents, from whom he himself received life, is indeed a cruel and terrifying crime; yet one learns, alas, that such wicked murder is committed. Thus have the loathsome Satan and the evil, corrupted nature of man gained the upper hand against God's Commandment and the Law of Nature. Indeed, although one might think that no greater crime than this could be committed or devised, the malice of men and the cunning of the Evil Foe are not satisfied with this, but it is

# Preface

it has even come to this: that some people are not only inclined to kill their physical parents or blood relatives, but they would also gladly topple God in Heaven—the Creator and Father of all creatures—from His throne, and set the cursed Satan in His place, if it were possible for them. Thus, no law can now be given so sharp that the malice of men will not exceed it, nor can any punishment ever be set so harsh that the vile world could not deserve it tenfold. Such people are
,, precisely those whom one calls **sorcerers** or **witches** <note>original: "Zauberer oder Zauberinen"</note>, who know-
,, ingly and willfully renounce God their Creator with heart and
,, mouth; they desecrate, blaspheme, and revile Him, and surrender
,, themselves bodily to the loathsome Devil—the arch-enemy of God
,, and all His creatures—as his own property. They recognize him
,, as the true God and worship and honor him in His stead,
so that only through the Devil's help they may carry out all their whims and better pour out their excessive thirst for revenge and malice over other people. This they do because the true, almighty God stands in their way and hinders them with His holy Law and Gospel <note>original: "Gesetz vnd Euangelio"</note>, while the Devil is willing and ready to promote them to the most gruesome sins and vices, and to give them help and counsel for their evil intentions. O Solon, Solon <note>A reference to the ancient Athenian lawmaker; the author suggests Solon's wisdom is needed to address crimes so great they defy legislation.</note>, here it were to be wished that no laws were needed! But it is, alas, far too true; for there are more than enough of such shameful and hideous monstrosities in the world. For if
,, there is one parricide <note>original: "Battermörder" (father-murderer)</note> in the world, one
,, will always find more than a hundred sorcerers to counter him
who cling to the Devil. This is testified by the books of many learned people, histories old and new, daily experience, and it is also testified by the Holy Divine Scripture, both of the Old and New Testaments. Here it is necessary that the authorities <note>original: "Obrigkeit"</note> do not sleep, but keep diligent investigation; and where they find any who have thus fallen away from God, they should spare no wood, coal, straw, nor fire, so that this cruel misfortune may be resisted, God's honor (as much as lies in them) may be rescued, and their own bodies and lives (to say nothing of other people's) may be preserved. Here, not only must the
,, authorities keep watch, but every person must diligently pray to God
,, that he may be protected from the secret, treacherous assaults of the
,, Devil and his servants, the sorcerers.
But people are now far too sluggish; many rulers and judges cast it to the wind and do not believe that
,, such people are to be found—contrary to Divine and worldly testimony—
,, or even if they do believe it, they are still shy of them and fear

# Preface.

<margin>)( iij</margin>

the Devil and his followers much more than God, and would much sooner allow God to be blasphemed and scorned in the worst possible way—and even let their land and people be ruined by sorcerers—than they would ever think to punish them. The common man also regards this lightly; and although nearly all their misfortune (even that which they often cause themselves) is to be attributed to the sorcerers, there are very few among the masses who call upon God for help and assistance against the murderous ways of the sorcerers, until a few are finally made wise through their own great loss. Thus, because of this general negligence, God permits the Devil and his sorcerers all the more power. Therefore, those who expose the malice of the sorcerers act rightly and well. Indeed, extreme necessity requires that examples, foundations, causes, means, and methods—as well as medicines, help, and counsel—be set down in writing, and that their villainy be placed before everyone's eyes. In this way, every person, of whatever station they may be, might be reminded of their calling and how they ought to behave in such cases.

Many learned and experienced people have done this, including the authors listed on the back of the title page, and especially the honorable and well-learned Mr. M. Abraham Saur of Frankenberg <note>Abraham Saur (1545–1593) was a noted jurist and historian</note>, currently the appointed Advocate and Procurator of the Princely Hessian High Court at Marburg. At my request and urging, he has newly brought these works together into a single volume <note>original: "Corpus"</note> and prepared them for printing. These writings briefly encompass everything concerning sorcery that can be proven from Holy Scripture <note>original: "Göttlicher Schrifft"</note> and other certain arguments and examples, as well as what is useful and necessary to know about the subject (mentioning this without intending any slight to other scholars). 

Therefore, since several learned and sensible people have particularly praised these small treatises <note>original: "Tractätlein"</note> and books to me, and I have also seen that they were previously reprinted by me and others—partly in the Latin language and partly in the German language—and were well-received, I have considered it good to produce them together in print for the common good. I hope that I have thereby served all sensible and pious people and provided an incentive to reflect more deeply on these matters and to read these authors more diligently.

To Your Excellencies, Honors, and Graces <note>Abbreviated honorifics: E. E. F. W. vnnd G.</note>, however, I have wished to specifically write and dedicate this Theater <note>original: "Theatrum"; a common Renaissance term for a comprehensive survey or "theater" of knowledge</note>, as my humble and inclined...

# Preface.

To demonstrate my will—especially as you have shown me no small kindnesses in times past—in some measure, which I have indeed been unable to do in any other way than by that which is consistent with my calling <note>The "calling" refers to his profession as a printer and publisher</note> and within my modest ability. And since my inclined will and grateful spirit are much greater than my ability, and better than this work outwardly displays: I hope that Your Noble and Princely Graces <note>original: "E. E. F. W. vnd G." - an abbreviation for "Euer Edel, Fürstlich Wohlgeboren und Gnaden"</note> will accept this labor, along with my further offer to serve should the opportunity arise, with favorable pleasure; and that you will continue to keep me in your favor as you have done until now. Herewith wishing Your Noble and Princely Graces health, long life, and all prosperity. Given at Frankfurt the first of February, in the year after the birth of Christ our Savior, 1586.

# To the Christian Reader.

Many have written of **Sorcery** <note>original: "Zauberey"</note>
In various ways and extensively;
One stirs up this, the other that,
One hits the mark poorly, the other better.
One also finds many loose folk
Who are stark blind in this matter,
And yet wish to be judges,
As if they understood it finely,
And they talk into the **lark-field** <note>A German idiom meaning to speak at random or talk nonsense without knowledge of the facts.</note>
Useless words before all the world;
Yet they have no foundation for it,
Speaking only from the mouths of others,
According to a deceptive delusion,
As a blind man speaks of color.
And from this, in our time,
A great dispute has also arisen,
Whether one should execute **witches** <note>original: "Hexen"</note> and **monsters** <note>original: "Vnhold"; a term for sorcerers or malevolent spirits.</note>
With flaming fire.
The authorities are on one hand too lenient,
On the other hand, they proceed too hastily
With foolish and poor
Women—may God have mercy.
Now, it is truly not a thing
That one should regard as trivial;
It costs both body and soul
If a mistake is committed herein by
Accusers, the accused, the authorities,
And witnesses without distinction.
Therefore, let everyone take heed,
In his station as is proper,
That he does not do too much in the matter
When he wishes to punish the vice.
Do not hurry until one has recognized
The matter itself according to all circumstances;
Do not burden your conscience
With an unreflective judgment,
For **innocently shed blood**
Cries out to God for vengeance;
And when, to someone's misfortune,
A sentence has been carried out—

<summary>A poetic preface warning readers and authorities against hasty or uneducated judgments in witchcraft trials, emphasizing the spiritual danger of shedding innocent blood.</summary>
<keywords>witchcraft, sorcery, judicial caution, innocent blood, legal ethics, social commentary</keywords>

--- Page 8 ---
<meta>The catchword "EPI-" suggests this page serves as an epilogue or introductory poem to a legal or theological treatise on witchcraft.</meta>

Thus, no one can ever restore
That noble life <note>original: "edel Leben"; likely referring to the life of someone wrongfully accused or executed</note> to its former state,
Even if, in such great distress,
You were to grieve yourself to death.
On the other hand, do not be too lenient
When you possess strong evidence;
Instead, proceed correctly and simply,
According to the Law of God and the Emperor.
Be accuser, witness, and judge without fear;
Do everything honestly and with loyalty.
Whoever does not desire God's grace,
Let him bear his own guilt.
It is a wicked kind of mercy
That brings suffering to many people;
He who cannot spare himself <note>meaning: he who persists in his own ruin or sin</note>
Must be abandoned by everyone.
Now, if anyone should wish to know
How he should conduct himself in this matter,
And how he ought to manage it
So that he may remain innocent,
Let him read the good instruction
Provided for him in this book
Concerning sorcery and witchcraft <note>original: "Zauberey vnd Hexenwerck"</note>.
Strengthen your judgment <note>original: "Iudicium"</note> through this;
Do everything with good understanding.
Diligently record in the margin
Whatever concerns the main business itself;
Compare everything with the Scripture,
And proceed only with that
Which is measured against the Word of God.
Yet I must also warn you herewith
That not everything is the truth,
Nor can it stand firm and unshifted,
Among the things printed here together.
The master printer <note>original: "Truckerherr"</note> with all diligence
Has set together black and white,
Evil and good, lies and truth,
Each with its own explanation,
So that from the contrast
One might discover the good treasure,
And understand what it is
That he may surely rely upon.

<summary>A poetic exhortation advising the reader on the gravity of witchcraft trials, urging a balance between strict legal adherence and the careful discernment of truth from falsehood in printed texts.</summary>

# E P I G R A M

->By M. Rudolph Goclenius, Professor of Physics <note>In this era, "Physics" referred to Natural Philosophy or the study of nature.</note> at the University of Marburg, etc.<-

->TO THE READER.<-

Do you wish to see what a woman—and how much a sorceress <note>original: "venefica," implying one who uses potions or poisons.</note>—is capable of?
(Whether she makes rivers flow backward to their sources while the very banks marvel, whether she clears away clouds
or brings them forth, whether she drives away or summons the winds;
whether she moves the forests and commands the mountains to tremble,
the earth to groan, and the spirits of the dead to depart their graves;
whether she draws you down, O Moon; whether, by God’s permission,
she stirs the dire thunders of heaven, or blights the crops, or
bursts the jaws of vipers with her words and incantations;
whether she inserts thin needles, knives, and briars into the liver;
whether the eye of a witch <note>original: "sagae"</note> bewitches the tender lambs;
or whether a Demon becomes an Incubus, and likewise a Succubus <note>Male and female spirits believed to consort with humans.</note>)
Read of this in these books, which the press of
BASSAEUS <note>Nicolaus Bassaeus, a prominent 16th-century Frankfurt printer.</note> has printed anew; Reader, you will find the useful mixed with the sweet.

# H O R A T I U S <note>The Roman poet Horace, from his Epistles.</note>

Dreams, magical terrors, miracles, witches,
Nocturnal ghosts, and Thessalian portents, I meet
With laughter.

### That is:

All that the Devil’s army can do
Is a jest; I would almost laugh at it.

# To the orthodox and well-
### meaning Reader: Grace and peace, through Christ the Son of God, our LORD and Savior.

<margin>1 Peter 5. Satan is God's adversary.</margin>
THE holy Apostle Peter did not without cause or in vain most faithfully and heartily admonish and warn the dear Christians of his time—who were driven and scattered here and there—against the crafty Satan; for according to his malice, he seeks and desires not the salvation of men, but their eternal destruction. Therefore, he always attempts in a deceitful manner to lead the dear Christians away from their true and only Redeemer, Jesus Christ, and to make them apostate. Thus we also experience and see, in these our most poor and embittered times, not only harmful divisions in the holy Christian religion—through which the cursed and damned spirit Belial <note>A biblical term for the devil or a personification of worthlessness and wickedness.</note> most violently troubles, grieves, and even moves and shakes the Christian Church in its very foundation—but also <margin>Belial is godless.</margin> this no small calamity and tribulation: that many persons here and there in Christendom, through the persuasion of the crafty spirit, enter into and involve themselves in gruesome and terrifying idolatry. After renouncing the Christian faith, the holy Sacraments, and especially Holy Baptism, they pledge themselves to him, the Devil, promising and surrendering themselves to him with body and soul. Just as approximately four years ago (as everyone has sufficient report of the same), the loathsome Satan ignited and brought forth a new, <margin>YEAR 1566.</margin> unheard-of, and damned heresy and blasphemy among certain persons here in Schletstadt <note>Modern-day Sélestat in Alsace.</note>: so has he now again—since he is entirely restless and crafty—started a new alarm among us a short time ago. For several of the bewitched female persons were found, after certain examination and experience, to have involved themselves with evil spirits after despising true religion, with shameful, devilish, and cursed obligation. For this reason, they have received their due punishment according to Divine and Secular Law, and have taken their well-deserved reward and value therein.

However, since I have heard that within man's memory, and longer, no person has been judged and executed here in Schletstadt for these reasons, and perhaps (as has happened before due to thoughtlessness) many might think, and even conclude, that one acted improperly and unlawfully with these persons—since various opinions regarding these matters of sorcery arise, are promoted, and are heard here and there—I have seen fit to allow such an Act, together with the entire proceedings, as much as is known to me, to be released in print. This is so that everyone may receive a good report and sufficient information, and may pass a fair judgment on it. May you, favorable reader, understand and take this from me in the best way, and call upon and pray to God the Almighty with me from the heart, that He may grant to all and every dear Christian Authority His Divine grace, help, and assistance, so that the true Christian religion may be promoted, and everything that may be contrary and opposed to the same may be abolished and put away, etc. Dated at Schletstadt, the last day of the Harvest Month <note>September</note>, in the year 1570.

-> Reinhardus Luß of Erythropolis <note>Latinized name for Schletstadt/Sélestat; "Erythropolis" literally means "Red City."</note> <-

<summary>In this preface, Reinhardus Luß justifies the recent execution of several women for witchcraft in Schletstadt, framing their "devilish pacts" as a spiritual threat to the Church. He presents this printed account as a legal and theological defense of the authorities' actions to prevent public misunderstanding.</summary>

# Concerning the Godless Witches/ also
### Heretical and Devilish Women/ who in the
### Imperial City of Sélestat/ in
### Alsace/ were burned, etc.

<margin>Isaiah 45.</margin>
<margin>Throughout Amos.</margin>
<margin>Deuteronomy 28.</margin>
Although from God alone—as the Holy Scripture teaches and testifies here and there—all good things, and likewise all punishments, proceed; yet He commonly employs for the execution of both the service of good and evil angels. Of the service of good angels
<margin>Hebrews 1.</margin>
St. Paul writes to the Hebrews, how they are ministering spirits, sent by God for the salvation of mankind. But of the evil ones,
<margin>Psalm 77.</margin>
David says <note>original: "Psalm 77" - likely referring to Psalm 78:49 in modern numbering</note> that God sent evil angels in His fierce anger, and let them rage and storm, and do harm.

<margin>Psellus on Demons.</margin>
Now, these same spirits are not of one kind, but of many kinds: For some, after they were cast out of Heaven with Lucifer, remain and dwell still near the "Sphere of the Moon" <note>The lunar sphere was considered the lowest heavenly body in medieval cosmology</note>, and because of the fire, are called *Ignei* <note>Fiery ones</note>.
<margin>There are many races of evil spirits; they also have distinct places into which they were first cast at the beginning of their fall.</margin>
Next are the *Terreni* <note>Earthly ones</note>, who by night lead people astray on earth, or otherwise cause much unrest and suffering among them, so that they often cause despondent people to hang themselves, stab themselves, or perish in other ways. Furthermore, the *Aquarii* <note>Watery ones</note>, who like to dwell near
<margin>These things according to Johannes Trithemius.</margin>
puddles or rivers/ and therefore often bring it about that hopeless and sorrowful people drown themselves; and they are called by many "Water-nymphs" or "Mermaids," like the Sirens, because they occasionally show themselves upon the sea and sink ships. When spirits come, they take upon themselves bodies made of air and earth, in whatever form they desire—young or old, human or animal. Yet it is not like a true human, for there is no sentient life, no true soul, nor human formation, neither eyes, belly, nor intestines. Therefore, even if such an evil spirit behaves as if it eats, drinks, sees, etc., it is all a delusion and a deception.

Magical arts can do whatever they do through the powers of the air; yet they have no power unless it is granted from above. And, He alone is the one Creator God, by whose ineffable power it also happens that what Angels (namely the evil ones) could do if they were permitted, they cannot do because they are not permitted.

<margin>
Johannes Trithemius.
Some wished to offer sacrifices to the Devil like these witches, and perhaps confirm the pacts with their own blood.
</margin>
For first and foremost, they renounce their faith in Christ and their Holy Baptism, and surrender themselves body and soul to Satan as his own property and into eternal servitude. Since the Devil—as we ultimately learn from many notable examples in Holy Scripture—is ill-disposed toward all people, he constantly desires to destroy their bodies, lives, and everything they own. He is, however, so powerless and weak if God does not permit him to accomplish anything; thus, as envious, poisonous, and angry as the Devil is against the human race, he can accomplish nothing unless he begs for and obtains authority from God the Lord. This is seen in the case of Job, whom the Devil waylaid and sought to destroy, but

<margin>
See Exodus 1, Job 1, 2, and 10.
</margin>

<column-break/>

<margin>
Revelation 17.
Matthew 8.
</margin>

But why does God the Lord permit the Devil so much, so that he inflicts great damage on the bodies and property of livestock and people? Firstly, so that He may test the pious and God-fearing in their faith, to see if they will remain steadfast in tribulation as well as in prosperity, as seen with Job, Tobias, etc. Secondly, so that He may punish the godless, wicked, and evil people, so they might perhaps recognize their sins, repent, and avoid eternal harm. Also, so that they may be punished as an example here and there, as happened and befell Herod and others.

<margin>

Acts 12.

For the Lord God spoke to the Jewish people: "I am a God who visits the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation, even upon those who hate me," etc. And so that the elders might consider within themselves how harshly the righteous Lord will punish the wicked sinners who do evil out of free will and great presumption—just as Christ said to the women of Jerusalem during his execution: "If this happens to the green wood, what will happen to the dry?"

# ...thus burned at Sélestat.
->A iii<-

revealed and brought to light: but only as an introduction and entrance to the proceedings that have transpired in recent times regarding certain such witches and heretical persons, I have wished to make some mention of this here.

->Theophylactus, Archbishop of Bulgaria.<-
<note>Theophylact of Ohrid (c. 1055–1107), a prominent Byzantine biblical exegete.</note>

Concerning the crippled woman in Luke 13, he writes: this sickness happened and occurred to the woman because of the evil spirit; perhaps for the sake of her sins she was abandoned by God and delivered to Satan for punishment. For Satan inflicts all kinds of evil upon the human body as soon as it is permitted to him by God, etc.

But because these hags seek nothing other, with their devils, than the harm and destruction of other creatures—and they believe nothing else than that they themselves do what the devil does by God's permission—and in addition to this, they renounce their faith in Jesus Christ, all the holy Sacraments, and the entire Christian religion, and after a shameful obligation to the devil, surrender themselves entirely, body and soul, to him: therefore they shall be condemned to death and punished in body and life. For both Divine and Secular Law command and order this, saying: "You shall not allow sorceresses to live." <note>original: "Die Zauberinnen soltu nicht leben lassen." Reference to Exodus 22:18.</note> Likewise, if a man or woman is a soothsayer or an interpreter of signs, they shall die the death, etc.

<margin>Punishment of sorcerers.
Code, Book 9, Title 18. Constitution of Emperor Constantine. Exodus 22. Leviticus 20.</margin>

Furthermore, many make use of sorcerous arts and presume to disturb the elements and to injure and damage innocent people. These, because they are foreign and hostile to nature, shall be judged from life to death like irrational beasts.

But this constitution and statute (says a very learned man, namely, Johannes Trithemius) <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German abbot and polymath who wrote extensively on demonology.</note> concerns and strikes not only witches and "devil-wives," but also necromancers <term>Schwarzkünstler: literally "black-artists" or practitioners of the dark arts</term> and conjurers of devils. For they use all such arts, which are full of cursing, unbelief, and godlessness. To bring the devils into their service, they use and maintain shameful sacrifices and make an explicit pact and alliance with the devil, through which godless superstition they also accomplish great evil, and drag others with them into the pits of the devil and cause them to fall. Therefore, one should nowhere suffer or endure such necromancers any more than the witches, but root them out everywhere from the ground up: as God the Lord has commanded, saying: "You shall not allow sorcerers and witches to live," etc.

<margin>Necromancers, black-artists.</margin>
<margin>Exodus 22</margin>

<column-break/>

Now, just as the damned hags—with the help and assistance of the devils to whom they are surrendered and with whom they practice improper works of carnal lust—damage and destroy cattle, people, etc., they also fall into suspicion because they sometimes display ill-will or resentment toward the people they intend to harm if they are not immediately given everything they desire. From this it follows that such damages are attributed and interpreted as their doing. The like also happened here in Sélestat <note>original: "Schletstadt," a town in Alsace.</note>, where a carpenter's wife frequented her neighbor's house and finally miserably corrupted a young child's little arm, and afterwards partially helped it again with baths, herbs, etc. Following this, the leg of a child belonging to a baker, her godparent, was also injured and so damaged that it was a pitiful sight. When the child's father sought justice from the authorities, she was seized and taken into custody. And when this blasphemous person was questioned under torture <note>original: "peinlich gefragt," a legal euphemism for interrogation involving physical pain</note> regarding the whole matter, she nevertheless refused to confess anything.

Whence this stubbornness of the witches comes, the highly learned Girolamo Cardano <note>original: "Hieronymus Cardanus" (1501–1576), an Italian polymath.</note> indicates, saying: "When one intends to punish these heretical women, devil-worshippers, and murderers, they are so stubborn and so stiff-necked that they cannot be moved by any discretion, nor by the pity of their kin, nor by great torture or fear of death." This comes from the fact that they imagine how their devils—Peterlin, Löblin, Volland, etc.—will protect them from punishment and torture...

<margin>Girolamo Cardano, Book 15, Chapter 80.</margin>

# Concerning the Witches

Whoever takes this to heart and considers it must confess that such actions were an imitation of Cain and Judas <note>Cain and Judas are cited here as the ultimate examples of despair and betrayal</note>, where the one said: "My iniquity is greater than can be forgiven me," etc. And the other: "I have done evil in that I have betrayed innocent blood." He would have gladly turned back, had the Devil not fettered him so tightly. So it is here; although no one should set themselves up as a judge, but rather leave all judgment to the righteous judge ordained by his Heavenly Father, Jesus Christ.

When they arrived at the place with these four women and condemned witches, where the pyre and woodpile had been erected and prepared, the executioners along with their servants and helpers immediately placed them on ladders and bound them, fastening them with chains, and threw them into the ignited fire. They gave no sign of cruel martyrdom, perhaps because gunpowder had been placed before their mouths <note>A common "mercy" in early modern executions to ensure a quicker death via explosion or smoke inhalation</note> and their faces were turned toward the flames; only Amelia let out several screams.

One should rightly speak of how such a great multitude, certainly several thousand people, watched this terrifying and cruel spectacle, having gathered and assembled from many places. And how the executioner's boys were so industrious, diligent, and earnest in carrying straw bundles and stoking the fire, and with other works, so that to many it seemed as if they were seeing the burning and roasting of the hellish Vulcan, of whom the poets write. Afterward, everyone, including the wise lords and both mayors, Valentin Goll and Jacob Ostertag, who were appointed to this, and the well-armed citizens, returned home. So that the judgment would be fully carried out, they did not cease burning until these persons were completely burned to powder and ash.

After all this, it is right that each and every—

<margin>
Vulcan, the blacksmith and metalworker, who is perpetually occupied in fire and smoke, and covered in sparks. Lucian, *On Sacrifices*.
</margin>

<column-break/>

—Christian, but especially the female persons, should always take good care and have great concern, watching and praying, just as Christ very faithfully taught his disciples on the Mount of Olives. They should remember that the cunning Satan tempted, tried, and seduced the first humans through the serpent in Paradise. This was permitted to the evil spirit by GOD so that man might be tested and proven, since he has before him fire and water, good and evil, and by his free will could take one of the two. But by the special providence of GOD, the damned spirit appeared to man to tempt him, not in a friendly or lovely form, but in a terrifying and loathsome shape, so that man might better and more easily perceive and understand the deceit of the loathsome Satan.

Because the Devil has in this way craftily bypassed, deceived, and seduced man, God has set an eternal enmity between the devils and men; therefore, they constantly lie in wait for man in all sorts of measures, ways, and means, as much as they are able.

The holy Apostle Paul well considered and weighed this great danger to mankind within himself. Accordingly, out of special faithfulness and love, desiring to protect all Christian believers from disadvantage and harm, he gave them this teaching and faithful warning: namely, that they should commit themselves to a spiritual struggle and battle against the most hateful enemy, the Devil. Thus, every house is an army that must resist the most harmful enemy at all times. But the enemy is not physical, but a spirit; therefore the struggle and battle must also happen in the spirit or spiritually, and the armor and equipment must be spiritual if one is to resist and thwart this enemy. And because he is quite cunning, he does not come with his open ranks of war and battle, but with secret ambushes and treacherous plots, so that he—

# Concerning Witches

They know God, yet he <note>the Devil</note> approaches with guile and cunning, so that he may find them through greed or lust, or drive those depraved by sin toward death; or, if he profits nothing by guile, he endeavors to cast them down through violence, etc.

<margin>Isidore, *On the Supreme Good*, Book 1. <note>Isidore of Seville (c. 560–636), a scholar whose works were foundational to medieval knowledge.</note></margin>
The Devil is a slippery serpent; if his head—that is, his first suggestion—is not resisted, he glides entirely into the depths of the heart while remaining unnoticed, etc.

<margin>Therefore let us resist him, steadfast in faith. 1 Peter 5.</margin>

### How the Devil can deceive people and beget children.

Doctor Martin Luther said that he himself had heard a story from the Holy John Frederick, Elector of Saxony, that there was a noble lineage in Germany who were born of a *Succubus* <note>original: "Succubo"; a demon in female form</note>. For that is what they are called, just as Melusina of Luxembourg <note>A figure of European folklore, often depicted as a water-spirit or mermaid who marries a nobleman</note> was also such a *Succubus* or devil.

It happened in this way: A nobleman had a beautiful young wife who died and was also buried. Not long afterward, while the master and his servant were lying in a chamber together, the deceased woman came at night and leaned over the master's bed, just as if she were speaking with him. Now when the servant saw that this happened twice in succession, he asked the young lord what it might be, and whether he knew that every night a female figure in white clothing came before his bed. He said no; he slept through the entire night and saw nothing. When night came again, the young lord also paid attention and stayed awake in bed. Then the woman came before the bed again. The lord asked who she was and what she wanted? She answered that she was his wife. He said: "But you are dead and buried." She answered: "Yes, she had to die because of his cursing and for the sake of his sins. But if he wished to have her with him again, she would become his wife once more." He said: "Yes, if only it could be." But she made a condition and warned him that he must not curse—as he had a particular habit of cursing—otherwise she would soon die again. The man promised her

<column-break/>

this. Then the deceased woman remained with him, ruled the household, slept with him, ate and drank with him, and bore children. Now it happened that once the nobleman had guests, and after the meal was finished in the evening, the woman was supposed to fetch a gingerbread for the fruit course out of a chest; and the woman was forgotten <note>likely meaning she was neglected or provoked in the moment</note>, she stooped over, and the woman vanished, and has not been seen since that time. The Devil does this; he can transform himself into the shape of a woman or a man.

Now the question is: Whether these are real women and whether they are real children? Regarding this, my thoughts are that they cannot be real women. Rather, they are devils, and it happens thus: The Devil creates a phantom before their eyes and deceives them, so that the people believe they are sleeping with a real woman, and yet it is nothing. The same happens when it is a man <note>referring to an Incubus</note>. For the Devil is powerful among the children of unbelief, as Saint Paul says.

But how are the children begotten? To this I say: That these sons were also devils, having had such bodies as the mother. It is truly a gruesome, terrifying example that Satan can so plague people that he even begets children. It is the same with the water-sprites <note>original: "Nixen"</note> in the water, who pull people in to them, such as virgins and maidens, with whom he then cohabits and begets devil-children. For otherwise, begetting children is solely a divine work, and there our Lord God must be the Creator. For we always call Him Father, and the conception must happen through established means and through humans in a single moment <note>original: "per constituta media & per homines in einem momento"</note>. For He uses these as a means for the creation of mankind, and through the same...

# and Changelings.
<margin>B</margin>

he worked these things alone and not through the Devil. Therefore, they must be stolen children, for the Devil can indeed steal children—just as one sometimes loses children within six weeks—or they must be *suppositicij* <note>Latin: "substitutes" or "supposititious children"</note>, changelings, which the Saxons call *Kielkröpff* <note>term: "Kielkropf" (plural: Kielkröpfe) — a folklore term for a changeling, literally meaning "narrow-throat" or "funnel-crop," referring to their insatiable hunger.</note>.

### Story of a Changeling in Dessau.

Eight years ago there was one in Dessau which I, Doctor Martin Luther, saw and touched. It was twelve years old and had its eyes and all its senses, so that one thought it was a real child. Yet it did nothing but eat; indeed, it ate as much as any four peasants or threshers. It ate, defecated, and urinated, and when one touched it, it cried out. If things went badly in the house and damage occurred, it laughed and was happy; but if things went well, it wept. It had these two qualities about it. Then I said to the Princes of Anhalt: "If I were Prince or Lord here, I would take this child into the water, into the Mulde <note>original: "Molda"</note> which flows by Dessau, and would risk the charge of homicide <note>original: "Homicidium"</note> upon it." But the Elector of Saxony, who was also in Dessau, and the Princes of Anhalt would not follow me. Then I said: "Then they should have the Christians in the church pray a 'Our Father' that the dear God might take the Devil away." This was done daily in Dessau, and that same changeling died in the second year thereafter. Thus it must be so.

Someone else has written finely of the *Succubis* and *Incubis* <note>Demons believed to have sexual encounters with humans while they sleep.</note>: For it is not rare, and the *Succubi* are women who have dealings with the Devils and satisfy the lust of those old hores and weather-makers <note>term: "Wettermacherin" — a witch believed to control the weather.</note>, just as Melusina in Luxembourg was also such a *Succubus* and Devil.

In the year 1541, Dr. Luther also recalled these stories at the table, and how he had advised the Princes of Anhalt that one should drown the changeling, or the *Kielkropff* (which is so named because it always hurries in its throat <note>A folk etymology suggesting the creature is always swallowing or hungry.</note>). When he was asked why he had advised such a thing, he answered

<column-break/>

to that, that he entirely held it to be the case that such changelings are merely a piece of flesh, a *massa carnis* <note>Latin: "mass of flesh"</note> in which there is no soul. For the Devil can easily make such things, just as he otherwise corrupts people who have reason—indeed, body and soul—because he possesses them physically so that they neither hear, nor see, nor feel anything; he makes them mute, deaf, and blind. Thus the Devil is in such changelings in place of their soul. It is a great power of the Devil that he holds our hearts so captive. And he said: Origen <note>An early Christian scholar (c. 184–253 AD).</note> did not sufficiently understand the power of the Devil when he was of the opinion that on the Last Day the Devils should be redeemed from eternal damnation. "Ah," he said, "it is a great sin of the Devil that he knowingly sets himself against God his Creator."

### Another Story of a Changeling.

In Saxony, near Halberstadt, a man also had a *Kilkropff* who had sucked his mother and five other nurses completely dry, and moreover had eaten much and began to act strangely. People gave this man the advice that he should vow the child to a pilgrimage to Hockelstadt <note>A pilgrimage site dedicated to the Virgin Mary.</note> to the Virgin Mary, and have him weighed there. The peasant followed this and carried him there in a basket. But as he carried him over a water and walked upon the footbridge or bridge, there was a Devil down in the water who called out to him and said: "*Kilkropff, Kilkropff!*" Then the child, who sat in the basket and had never before spoken a word, answered: "Ho, ho!" The peasant was unaccustomed to this and very frightened. Thereupon the Devil in the water asked further: "Where are you going?" The *Kielkropff* said: "I am going to Hockelstadt to Our Dear Lady to let myself be weighed, so that I might thrive."

When the peasant heard this—that the changeling could speak, which he had never before noticed from him—he became angry and immediately threw the child into the water with the basket in which he carried him. Then the two Devils came together, cried "Ho, ho, ha," played with one another, and tumbled about, and vanished together shortly thereafter.

# Concerning Witches and Changelings.

<columns>2</columns>

Such changelings and "kilcrops" <note>German: *Kielkröpffe*; a folklore term for a demonic changeling, often described as having an insatiable appetite.</note> are substituted by Satan in the place of true children, and he plagues the people with them. For Satan has this power: that he exchanges children and lays a devil in the cradle in place of one's own child. Such a creature then does not thrive, but only devours and sucks. However, it is said that such changelings and kilcrops do not live beyond 18 or 19 years of age. This now often happens to women in their six-weeks <note>The traditional period of postpartum recovery and confinement.</note> that their children are exchanged, and the devils lay themselves in their place and behave more foully with their defecating, eating, and screaming than ten other children combined, so that the parents have no rest from such filth, and the mothers are so sucked dry that they can no longer nurse.

<column-break/>

And when Doctor Luther <note>Martin Luther (1483–1546), the German reformer.</note> was asked at the table whether one should also baptize such changelings, he answered: "Yes, for one does not recognize them immediately in the first year, but one knows them only by this: when they thus suck the mothers dry." Doctor Luther said further: "Let us not so despise the Devil; he is truly a master of a thousand arts. See how he overtook the poor boy who fell to his death here in Ambrosius Reuter’s house on the 5th day of December, Anno 1538, who was nonetheless a pious and industrious student. But as he stood upstairs in the house at 4 o'clock in the evening, he suddenly fell down and died." The Devil can show such malice even to pious hearts.

->END of the first little treatise.<-

### The II. Little Treatise.

# A Dialogue on Sorcerers,
### whom in Latin are called *Sortilegos* or *Sortiarios*, <note>original: "Sortilegos oder Sortiarios"; terms for diviners or those who cast lots for magical purposes.</note>
### In which is briefly and thoroughly explained what is disputed regarding this entire business of sorcery; formerly
### published in Latin by Master Lambertus Danæus, <note>Lambert Daneau (c. 1530–1595), a French Reformed theologian.</note> but now newly translated into German and corrected.

->To the kind reader, Lambertus Danæus.<-

<columns>2</columns>

How great a utility this argument contains within itself will, favorable reader, become sufficiently manifest to you hereafter from the dialogue and disputation. However, so that it is not thought to be written more for the curious than for the understanding, I testify with all truth that I was finally—though reluctantly—moved to publish this little book both by the request of good friends and also by many questions regarding this business. No fables or old wives' tales are found herein; if I had wished to collect those, it would have turned into a great work of perhaps 14 books. Therefore, it comprises only what may be witnessed through certain histories or history books, as well as the judgment of pious and learned people, and finally what is to be held concerning this dispute from the Word of God. Also, all those who have read the books of other writers concerning the Devil’s ghosts and delusions must confess to me that this argument is entirely new and has not been explained or treated by anyone before. However that may be, I pray, favorable reader, that you will accept my work, which was done for your best interest, and use it for your benefit and advantage. Herewith, I commend you to God. Given at Orleans, the 1st day of the Hay-month <note>July</note>, in the year 1574.

# A Dialogue concerning the Sorcerers / who are called *Sortiarios* in Latin.

->The persons herein are / Antonius and Theophilus.<-

<margin>Antonius.</margin>

# Concerning the Sorcerers.
## B iij

For such curiosity is a true mother of a frivolous mind and useless industry, which has rightly displeased those who have always been pious people, as Solomon says in the 18th Chapter: <margin>»</margin> A fool has no delight in understanding, <margin>»</margin> but only in what is in his heart. <note>Proverbs 18:2</note> However, I have engaged with you in this question for the reason that I might help many people out of their error, as far as it is possible for me, who do not wish to admit that there are sorcerers, or that anything can be poisoned or enchanted by them. Consequently, they are inclined toward such people and hesitate to condemn and kill them when they fall into their hands, even when they are publicly accused and convicted as sorcerers who have caused manifold harm and misfortune through the devilish art of sorcery. Therefore, if the pressing necessity of these times did not compel me, I would not wish to lose a single word over this matter. For we should do as the ancient Christians did, who in former times excluded all kinds of curious artificiality from their assemblies and schools and burned such useless books, which happened in Asia Minor during the time of St. Paul, in the 19th Chapter of the Acts of the Apostles. And indeed, if we wish to confess the truth, there are many other far more useful questions that better befit a Christian, even if they are not as charming and pleasant to our foolish, curious heads, which commonly wish to climb above the heavens and explore everything that is in Hell and beneath it.

<margin>Antonius.</margin> I see well what you fear, and how cautiously you wish to handle the matter: namely, that the listeners or readers of your conversation might thereafter seek or find more opportunity for frivolity and curiosity than for piety and the fear of God. Such are those who have a delight in hearing such things, yet do not do it so that they may be more strengthened in the fear of God, humble themselves under the mighty hand of God, and acknowledge with due thanksgiving the grace of the most merciful Heavenly Father toward mankind (in that He preserves them against the evil, cunning assaults of the loathsome Devil and his servants, the sorcerers) and praise and glorify Him for it. Instead, they imagine they are given a space in which they may safely wander according to their desires in all kinds of useless questions outside the goal and boundaries of Faith. These people should rightly be counted among those who are always learning and can never come to the knowledge of the truth, in the 2nd [Epistle] to Timothy, the 3rd Chapter.

### Chapter One.
### What the word *Sortiarius* means, and from where it comes.

<margin>Theophil.</margin>
The word *Sortiarius* is undoubtedly drawn from the word *Sortilegus* <note>Latin: "one who gathers or reads lots."</note>, which is more common than the former, and the Latins devised this after the manner of the Greeks. For just as the Greeks call them <term>chresmologous</term> <note>original: "χρησμολόγους" — oracle-mongers or soothsayers.</note>, so the Latins have called them *Sortilegos*. These <term>chresmologoi</term> <note>original: "χρησμολόγοι"</note> and *Sortilegi* are those who, through devilish inspiration, prophesy future things by casting some lot, as was done in former times with small bones or dice; but nowadays, it is done with the hair-sack or the sieve, which is accustomed to turn itself around when certain words are murmured over it. The French, according to the nature of their language, have shortened the word *Sortilegus* and say *Sorcier*. The Hebrews, however, have no similarity at all in terms of the name with the Greeks, Latins, or even with us French. For what the Latins call *Sortiarios*, the Hebrews call *Chobarim* <note>original: "Chobarim" — likely referring to 'Chobar' or 'Chabar,' meaning an enchanter or one who joins spells together.</note>, because they deal in secret cunning and evil pieces of work. But without doubt, the word *Sortiarius* is taken from *Sortilegus*; how this happened, I will briefly explain. First, it is sufficiently obvious that among the many reasons why people associate and link themselves with the devil, this is the single greatest and oldest: namely, so that according to our innate, wicked curiosity, we may know future things beforehand and be able to prophesy to others. For no one is satisfied with his station, but we all wish to intrude into God's mysteries, and it seems to us that we have attained Divine Wisdom and knowledge if we only know beforehand some future things that are unknown to other people. After Satan perceived this levity in the hearts of men at all times, and that they had such a great desire to know future things in advance, he snatched the opportunity to [win] them over with his flattery and

Furthermore, the highly learned Marcus Varro, a very diligent researcher of antiquities, writes that from the beginning of the world there have been many kinds of prophecies which lasted until his own times. <meta>This page continues the classification of diviners and sorcerers by Lambert Daneau, following the first two types mentioned on the previous page.</meta>

# Lambert Daneau

...they, in their prophesying through the stimulation of the hellish spirit, allowed such a dull and confused voice to be heard from their bellies—as if from a jar or a leather bottle—which the Pythia <note>The priestess of Apollo at Delphi</note> at the city of Delphi performed in a shameful and terrifying manner from the tripod (for so the altar or table was named). The remaining six types of the art of divination differ from the previous two in that, although they also occur through the help and deceit of the Devil, Satan does nothing by himself in these six, nor does he speak personally with the diviners (which happens in the first two types); rather, he acts in another's name and through certain means and signs which he nevertheless prescribes and provides to them.

<margin>3.</margin> Thus, the third type is called *Necromancy* <note>original: "Necromantij"</note>, those who wish to know and prophesy future things from dead people through the help of the Devil. This most wicked and foolish type was already in use in the time of Homer, as he mentions it in the eleventh book of the *Odyssey*. Although Satan involves himself in this as well, he does so under a concealed name in the person of another.

<margin>4.</margin> The fourth type is called in Hebrew *Megonin* (from which perhaps the *Magi* are named, though the *Magi* are of a different kind); in Latin they are called *Astrologers* and *Mathematicians* <note>In this period, "mathematicus" often referred specifically to an astrologer or caster of horoscopes</note>, that is, star-gazers. These undertake to prophesy from the heavenly signs, stars, and planets—their rising, setting, positions, oppositions, and courses, etc.—according to their pleasure. Such were the Augurs in Rome in former times; likewise those who prophesied according to a particular division of the air, just as the star-gazers do today.

<margin>5.</margin> The fifth type the Hebrews call *Menachisim*, in Latin *Magi* <note>Sorcerers or magicians</note>, who have also been taught divination by the Devil through special figures, or letters, sketches, or drawings, so that they speak their special words over them; thus they practice their art with such signs as the crafty master-of-a-thousand-arts, the Devil, has taught and prescribed to them.

<column-break/>

Such are the *Hydromancers* <note>original: "Hydromantij"</note>, or water-gazers; and of this kind may well have been the divination with the cup in the first book of Moses <note>Genesis</note>, in the forty-fourth chapter.

<margin>6.</margin> The sixth type of diviners are the *Idegonim* in Hebrew, in Latin *Harioli* <note>Soothsayers or prophets</note>, who prophesy concerning future fortune; these do not devise anything from themselves from which to prophesy, but rather according to the form and manner of certain things they happen to see or hear, which also comes from the school of Satan. To this category belong the interpreters of dreams and the palm-readers <note>original: "hände beseher"</note>, who boast that they can recognize and prophesy a person's good or bad fortune from the lines or crosses of the hands. To this also belong those who in former times prophesied from lightning and thunder; likewise, those who prophesied according to the entrails of sacrifices, and according to the song of birds or their eating; all of whom, indeed, do not wish to be regarded as idolatrous, superstitious people, but rather imagine that their art has a good appearance and foundation upon which something may be built.

<margin>7.</margin> The seventh type the Hebrews call *Mecasephim*, in Latin *Praestigiatores* or *Fascinatores*, that is, eye-dazzlers <note>Illusionists or jugglers</note>, who blind people with sorcery and place many kinds of things before their eyes; but it is vain deceit and nothingness. Such were the sorcerers of Pharaoh, who are also called by the name *Mecasephim* in the second book of Moses <note>Exodus</note> in the seventh chapter.

<margin>8.</margin> The eighth and last type are the *Chobarim*, in the fifth book of Moses <note>Deuteronomy</note> in the 18th chapter, in Latin *Sortilegi* <note>Those who cast lots</note>, who allow themselves to be found with the Devil in special places and practice many kinds of sorcery. # Concerning the Sorcerers.

I went to school where my teacher taught me that *Sortilegi* <note>original: "Sortilegi"; literally "lot-readers"</note> are so named in Latin—not those who do harm with poison, but those who prophesy by means of certain lots, such as beans, dice, and the like, or verses, as when one happens to pick a line from a poet by chance. Such a thing (he says) happened in former times to the Roman Emperor Septimius Severus. For when he wished to take up the government and wanted to learn from Virgil how his undertaking would fare, he happened upon the verse which stands in the 6th book of the *Aeneid*:

->Roman, remember to rule the nations with your power.<-
<note>original Latin: "Tu regere imperio populos Romane memento."</note>
->That is:<-
->O Roman, you shall be the ruler<-
->Over all nations in common.<-

As Lampridius writes of him in his histories. But those whom we call *Sortiarios* <note>original: "Sortiarios"; a medieval Latin term for sorcerers or "lot-casters"</note>—that is, sorcerers—for the most part do not prophesy much, but rather bewitch and kill secretly with poison, and are experienced in the Devil's arts. Even if they occasionally prophesy of future things, they do not do it through special lots, like the ancients, but solely through the pure revelation of the Devil.

<margin>Theophilus.</margin> It is indeed the plain truth, dear Antonius, as you say. For if we wish to speak of it correctly and properly, our *Sortiarij*, of whom we speak, are not to be called *Sortilegi*, but rather devilish sorcerers and poison-murderers.

But because they have learned it thus from Satan and made a covenant with him—just as the *Sortilegi* did—and have also given themselves over to Satan just like them, it follows that the common man has not heeded the distinction of the names. Instead, they have called one class like the other either *Sortilegos* or *Sortiarios*. This includes both those who prophesy according to certain lots by Satan's teaching, and accordingly also those who secretly execute people or cattle with poison, which their aforementioned master gives them himself; for both classes give themselves to him and accomplish their sorcery with his help. Therefore, in common speech, the whole pack of devil-artists is called by the name of only one of those

<column-break/>

classes, *Sortiarius*, and thus one word was derived from another well-known one. One should also hate the whole swarm of devil-artists—especially those called *Sortiarios*—all the more because they first received the name after the Holy Gospel of Christ was revealed to the world. At that time, devilish soothsayers and sorcerous arts were most hated by everyone, as was right. Furthermore, in these names, one cannot strictly follow the purest and best Latin, for the names *Sortilegus* or *Sortiarius* first arose when the Goths invaded Italy and the Latin language had already completely lost its elegance. The Italians were the first to use these words in this way, when it was no longer Latin but "Barbaric Italy." This can be perceived from the title concerning the *Sortilegis* in the *Decretals* <note>A collection of papal law</note>. Although Augustine uses this word in one place in the sense that was customary in his time and in Christendom, one can also clearly see it in the last Canon, in the first Question, where they are commonly called by the barbaric but explicit name *Sortiarij*. Otherwise, it is well known that in Latin *intoxicare*—that is, to do away with by poison—and *incantare*—that is, to bewitch with words or blessings or other unnatural ways, etc.—are two different things. Likewise among the Greeks, *goeteia* <note>original: "γοητεία"; low magic or sorcery</note> and *pharmakeia* <note>original: "φαρμακεία"; poisoning or herbal magic</note> are not one thing, although they both deal with the Devil. In the whole land of Savoy, the sorcerers are called *Eryges*, either from the Greek word *Erinys* <note>original: "Erynnis"; the Furies</note>, which signifies an insane, raging desire to plague mankind; or, as some think, from the word *iunx* <note>original: "ἴυγξ"; the wryneck bird</note>, which in the poet Theocritus is a special bird used for sorcery and love-magic by witches.

<margin>Theophilus.</margin> How then did the ancient Latins call these people in good Latin?

<margin>Antonius.</margin> The men were called *Venefici*, that is, poison-murderers; but the women *Venificae*, female poison-murderers. Also *Sagae* <note>Wise women or witches</note>.

# Lambertus Daneau

Thessalian women, Witches, Vampires, and Screech-owls <note>original: "Thessalæ, Magæ, Lamiæ, Striges" — these are various Latin terms for practitioners of magic and supernatural creatures</note>, all of which names are found in the books of the excellent poet Horace <note>Quintus Horatius Flaccus, a leading Roman lyric poet</note>, who was most experienced in the pure Latin tongue. In the first book of his *Odes*, Ode 27; in the book of *Epodes*, Ode 17; and in the first book of *Satires*, Satire 8. Such a woman existed in the time of Horace named Canidia, about whom he complains. Likewise Circe, whom Homer mentions in the tenth book of the *Odyssey*; also Medea, of whom Ovid writes in the seventh book of the *Metamorphoses*. Finally, there was also such a one mentioned by the poet Lucan in the 6th book of the *Pharsalia*, and many others besides, who are mentioned here and there in various history books. Although these authors just cited are poets, they have nevertheless composed nothing other than things that were well-known and customary in their own time. But to say nothing of the poets, the German maidens are mentioned in such a manner by Julius Caesar in the first book of the *Gallic War*, and Cornelius Tacitus reports in the second book of his *Annals* <note>original: "Jarsgeschichten"</note> of one named Martina, who is said to have taken the life of the Emperor Germanicus with magical poisoning.

For Satan has always been a companion to his own kind, and just as one perceives him nowadays, so has he always been perceived and experienced before, inciting and driving the children of unbelief to avenge themselves against those who have offended them, and to instigate anguish and unjust murder among brothers; for, as John testifies in the 8th chapter, he is a murderer from the beginning. As far as certain experience is concerned, I may say that at all times it has been observed, and proven by deeds, that such people have existed who, through diabolical instigation and art, have bewitched others. Why would one have needed to write laws against them if none had ever existed? Why should punishment be established? For one does not make a law concerning that which does not exist; and in Imperial Law, things that do not exist at all or are unknown are held as one and the same, as the jurists teach. When the wise lawgiver Solon <note>Solon (c. 630–560 BCE) was an Athenian statesman and lawmaker.</note> was asked in Athens why he had made no law against those who murdered their fathers or mothers, he answered: He did not think that such an evil person would ever be found. Therefore, both before and after the birth of Christ, there have been many of the sorcerous rabble here and there. That they existed before Christ's birth is testified by the faithful servant and holy man of God, Moses—a credible witness—who mentions them in so many places and condemns them: In the second book of Moses <note>Exodus</note> in the 22nd chapter, and in the third <note>Leviticus</note> in the 19th chapter, in the fourth book <note>Numbers</note> in the 23rd, and in the fifth <note>Deuteronomy</note> in the 18th. It is also said of Zoroaster of Persia, a famous and wise stargazer <note>astrologer</note>, that he was the very first among all people to practice sorcery and taught others, who, like him, were idolatrous people and worshipers of idols. But that sorcerers also existed after the birth of Christ is sufficiently proven by many histories and other books. It is also testified by the judgments that have often been passed upon them; likewise the laws and punishments imposed upon them in Imperial and Papal laws, where one still reads entire titles and rubrics concerning this misdeed today, as can be seen in the glosses of Gratian <note>referring to the Decretum Gratiani, a collection of Canon Law</note>, in Case 26, questions 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. Furthermore, such poison-murderers have always been known in France, which is confirmed by countless arrests by the Parliament of such people, by many

<margin>Antonius.</margin>
Yes; but can you tell me, Theophilus, why it still happens in this day and age?

# Concerning Sorcerers.
## C ij

->Concerning the arrangement of matters, the philosophers teach further as follows. When a cause of a thing possesses both the understanding and the will for a certain action, and then the power to accomplish it is added, the effect and the work itself must necessarily follow and occur. For example: when someone is hungry and has bread, he eats; if one is thirsty and has wine present, he drinks; if one is freezing and comes to a fire, he warms himself. Because he has the will and is able to do it, it therefore happens. Thus, without doubt, Satan is the cause and instigator of all poisoners and sorcerers; he has the inclined will and also the power to instigate such evil, to persuade people toward sorcery, and to make them his followers (for this is permitted to him by God through His righteous judgment over the ungodly). Therefore, there is no doubt: he does it. To explain this further, dear Antonius, you will, I believe, agree with me that at all times in the world there have been many ungodly people who either did not recognize the right, true God, or if they did recognize Him, nevertheless despised Him.<-

<margin>Antonius.</margin>
I will grant you that, for it is, alas, far too true.

<margin>Theophilus.</margin>
Then you will also not deny me that Satan—after he first abandoned his station and [formerly] was an angel—has at all times diligently striven and, as much as was possible for him, undertaken and brought it about that he turns men away from the knowledge of God and from faith or trust in God and their salvation; also that they reject and despise God Himself and His promise. Likewise, that he has brought them to the point where they surrender themselves to him—namely those whom he has found cold toward the service of God and negligent in grasping His promises with right faith.

<margin>Antonius.</margin>
You speak the truth, for Satan "goes about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour" <note>1 Peter 5:8</note> and make apostate from God, as Peter says in the 1st [Epistle], in the 5th Chapter.

<margin>Theophilus.</margin>
Quite right, dear Antonius, and for that reason he is also called "the old serpent" in the Revelation of John in the 20th Chapter; that is, a common, declared, and sworn enemy of the human race, as Christ witnesses in Matthew 13. He who "has his work in the children of unbelief," as Paul says in Ephesians 2. For the wrath of God comes upon stubborn people. Since it is now clear as day from the cited Scripture that Satan has the will and desire to lead men away from the fear of God and from faith, nothing further remains to be proven but that he also has the power and the ability to do so.

<column-break/>

<margin>Antonius.</margin>
If that is accomplished, then you have done enough, and the matter is proven. But my dear Theophilus, should Satan have such power over men that he could turn them away from God and draw them to himself—they who are after all God’s creatures, created in His image and for His honor more than any other creature on earth?

<margin>Theophilus.</margin>
I confess, Antonius, that Satan would never have had such power if it were not given to him by God the Almighty; who, as a righteous God, thus punishes those who abandon Him out of unthankfulness and malice. Although we may not entirely know or explain the cause of this judgment—why the Lord God delivers one more than another over to Satan and allows them to be led astray—nevertheless, this is God’s righteous will, He who has so decreed it. Yet no one has ever become a sorcerer or a servant of the devil <term>Teuffelsknecht: literally 'devil's servant' or 'thrall'</term> except through his own fault, and who has not first knowingly and willfully renounced God his Creator (from whom he received life and every good thing), abandoned Him, and become faithless toward Him.

<margin>Antonius.</margin>
That must indeed be a strange thing, Theophilus, that a human being should renounce his God and obey Satan—whom he nevertheless knows to be Satan and a villain—to say nothing of making himself his bondservant?

<margin>Theophilus.</margin>
Ah, that is only too true, and all those do it who betake themselves to sorcery. For when Satan once overtakes the people whom he waylays...

For they needed money to support themselves and their household

These two kinds of people despair of the love and help of God, thinking God has forsaken them and does not take up their cross and suffering, or that He will not help them.

Through these ways and means they are led astray by the Devil, especially poor, simple, inexperienced peasants <margin>peasants</margin> who have endured cross, anxiety, and injustice, so that they become sorcerers and servants of the Devil.

One also finds some whom their proud, frivolous spirit drives there, such as those who are not satisfied with human reason and art <term>Art: here meaning skill or branch of knowledge</term>; these become the Devil's bondservants in that they wish to know future things or prophesy of them. Or also those who, out of ambition, desire to accomplish great things with little labor and effort that are impossible for other people. In this way, highly learned and famous people are led astray, as well as noble women and scholars, who are not unjustly punished by God because they despised Him and knowingly swore themselves to Satan.

<margin>Antonius.</margin>
Now I do not doubt, Theophilus, but believe entirely that such servants of the Devil and sorcerers exist, and also that sorcery is performed by them. Dear friend, tell me now also what things they can harm with their poisoning and sorcery.

<margin>Theophilus.</margin>

### The Third Chapter.
#### Which things the sorcerers can harm with their poison.

<margin>Antonius.</margin>
I will also gladly be satisfied with that, for I myself have no desire for such childish and foolish fables. But how is it, Theophilus? Can the sorcerers also bewitch and poison people or cattle? Can they, I ask, also bewitch the air, the water, the herbs, and cool their temper <note>i.e., satisfy their malice</note> on all things, as they themselves publicly confess: that with their devilish art they poison the air far and wide around several cities?

<margin>Theophilus.</margin>
That is easy to consider, Antonius, as you see: if one can strike down a great giant, he can perhaps slay a small, weak boy. So also, whoever can poison and bewitch a human being can do it much sooner and more easily to other things. For man is clever, cunning, prudent, takes heed of himself, and is created in the image of God; whoever can deceive and offend him may well say that he can harm irrational animals, such as horses, sheep, oxen, and cows, which cannot guard and protect themselves from harm like man. Likewise, whoever can poison cattle, why should he not much sooner poison a herb or a tree, the seed, a ring or bolt on the door, a step on the stairs, yes, even the wine, water, or air, which things we can touch at all times? And indeed, the sorcerers can prove their malice on such things; God permits this to them when He wishes to avenge the contempt of His Name through such things and to chastise us for the sake of our sins.

<margin>Antonius.</margin>
So nothing, as I hear, is exempt from sorcery.

<margin>Theophilus.</margin>
Everything on earth that is subject to vanity, mortal, and perishable can be poisoned and bewitched by this devilish, cunning guild of rogues, where it is not preserved and shielded by God. Now, however, there is nothing on earth that is not mortal and perishable. Therefore, we must confess that the sorcerers can do harm to all things on earth,

where God the Lord does not prevent it.

<margin>Antonius.</margin>
But tell me some examples of these things.

<margin>Theophilus.</margin>
That shall certainly be done. Firstly, nothing is more certain than that sorcerers do harm to people, as we see and experience daily. I have seen that the breasts of nursing mothers have completely dried up because they were touched by sorcerers. I have also seen those who have stirred up great tearing, piercing, or cramps in people's bodies, and have also bewitched them with gout <note>original: "Zipperlin"</note>, wasting of the limbs, stroke <note>original: "Schlag," likely referring to paralysis or apoplexy</note>, and other evil diseases, which neither they themselves nor the most experienced doctors could recognize or heal. And the evil kind spares no human being, be it man or woman, old or young, rich or poor, of high or low standing, according as their own wickedness and thirst for revenge drives them to it. What more shall I say? Yes, the bailiffs <note>original: "Meyer"</note> and peasants bewitch their own landlords when they are angered.

The cattle, large and small, they kill with poison in many ways; and they do not only kill them, but when it pleases them, they cause them to swell up or also to become entirely thin, and their roguery and malice has not its equal on earth.

Above all this, they also bewitch the wild game so that it must stand still and allow itself to be felt with the hands. As it stands written in the 58th Psalm: *Their venom is like the venom of a serpent, like a deaf adder that stops her ear, so that she does not hear the voice of the sorcerer, of the charmer who can charm well,* etc. Although Augustine says in the eleventh book of *On the Literal Meaning of Genesis* <note>original: "de Genesi, ad literam"</note>, chapter 28: Satan could all the more easily damage the serpents because human nature was first seduced through the serpent's speech, as a punishment for its harmful service for which it allowed itself to be used. Yet experience itself shows that not only the serpent, but other animals just as well, as they [the sorcerers]...

<margin>Antonius.</margin>

For instance, water becomes warm at one time and cold at another; the air becomes warm, cold, and temperate in a single day, as happens especially in Spring, for in the morning it is cold, at noon warm, and in the evening halved <note>moderate</note>. Because the air is much more subtle and thinner than water, it takes on the foreign nature and properties of those things with which it is mixed all the more quickly and easily.

<margin>Antonius.</margin>

<margin>Theophil.</margin>
I do not deny, Antonius, that God himself—

# Concerning Sorcerers.

Even the First Beginner <note>original: "der erste anfänger"; referring to God as the primary cause who permits evil</note> is the one who, in such a manner and through such people as His instruments, punishes the sins of mankind. But the claim that it is merely a poor delusion in these people—that they are simply deranged and not in their right minds, as some say—is far from the truth. Rather, when sorcerers say they enchant or poison the air, it often happens and is as true as they boast; I can prove this to you. We do not feel what foreign thoughts and fantasies are, nor can they harm our bodies in themselves. Think, for instance, if you had killed me and imagined it as strongly as you liked; as long as you did not put it into action, how would it harm me? Would I have even one hair less because of it? Not a bit. For no one can poison another or make them sick with mere thoughts unless they carry it out in deed. However, we see clearly and experience the truth that sorcerers bring about and cause sickness, cruel pestilence, death, and other such misfortunes in the land, which cannot be denied. Furthermore, they themselves expressly confess it under the agony of the rack <note>original: "auff der Folter"; judicial torture was a standard part of 16th-century legal proceedings</note>, and especially when they are led to their death because of the evil they committed. In short, they all agree; this must surely be nothing other than the truth. If it were nothing but thoughts and fantasy, how could they all speak with one mouth? No, fantasy is varied, but the words and the deed are always found to be consistent and certain. Everyone has their own thoughts, and it is not possible—given how many different people are scattered here and there—that their thoughts and fantasies should agree so exactly that many of them, one like the other, should name the very same place, the same hour, and the same deed, saying: "We were at that place," or "That happened there, on that day, at that hour. This is how it occurred," etc., if it were not as certain as they said.

It is even more marvelous that they "bind" people <note>term: "binden" (binding); a specific type of folk magic or "ligature" intended to cause impotence or prevent the consummation of a marriage</note>, or perform villainy upon them, hindering them in their marital duties so that either both

<column-break/>

of them, or at least one, is rendered unfit and incapable.

<margin>Antonius.</margin>
Oh, Theophilus, what are you saying?

<margin>Theophil.</margin>
It is exactly as I tell you. If they can harm a person's health, take away the strength and vigor of the body, weaken the veins, derange the brain, or withdraw the understanding, and disturb the natural humors <note>original: "natürliche feuchtigkeit"; referring to the four humors of Galenic medicine</note> within us, then it is no wonder if they take away or hinder a man's virility, which depends only on a small member or part of the body in which the natural seed is kept. They do this either by chilling that part through poison or by stirring up great hatred, enmity, and recalcitrance between married couples whom they despise.

Even though this happens with the Devil's help and cunning, it nonetheless results in them stirring up discord and enmity between those who ought to be faithful to one another and hold each other dear. Thus, these godless people are accustomed to taking revenge on those they hate, though often without cause and in an innocent manner. But like their master, Satan, they also take pleasure in sowing weeds among mankind. Matthew 13, John chapter 3.

<margin>Antonius.</margin>
Do you know how to prove this with examples or grounds of reason?

<margin>Theophil.</margin>
Yes, with both. Examples are well known and obvious today, and we also have certain testimonies and proofs. First, Augustine, in the 7th Tractate on John, places "binding" among the evil pieces of sorcery, which includes what we are discussing now. Furthermore, it is proven by the most excellent and learned poet of all who lived in his time, namely Virgil, in his 8th Eclogue, which is taken from common experience, where he says:

> *Necte tribus nodis trinos Amarylli colores,*
> *Necte Amarylli modō: & Veneris dic vincula necto.*

-> That is: <-
> Go, maiden, and take threads of three,
> Let each a different color be.

> I bind, I bind with this my hand,
> That my lover now be in my band. <note>original: "mein Buel gebannt"; "Buel" is an archaic term for a lover or paramour</note>
