# Ludwig Lavater on Ghosts.

completely. In this, it is best that one be cautious, and do neither too much nor too little. <margin>Nothing in excess. <note>original: "Ne quid nimis." A famous classical Greek and Latin proverb advising moderation.</note></margin> That even the Heathens themselves were suspicious of many miracles attributed to their gods—and not without reason—is testified by Valerius Maximus <note>A 1st-century Roman author known for his collection of historical anecdotes.</note> in his first book. True miracles, however, should make us more alert. Just as a noble horse keeps its steady gait, yet if one merely flourishes a small rod, it looks ahead and becomes more attentive; so too should we walk uprightly as long as we live. But when some sign occurs, and it appears as if great things are at hand, we should all the sooner and all the more open our eyes, look before us, and apply ourselves to all that is good. The Heathens, when such warnings from God were presented to them, showed earnestness, holding their supplications and common prayers so that the gods might be merciful to them. Much more should all Lords and authorities, teachers and preachers in our times be diligent in this when great punishment is at hand, so that everyone might turn from their sins toward the good.

Thus we have hitherto sufficiently understood the nature of the appearances of spirits, as well as other wonderful things, and that in former times the world claimed much differently about them than what is found at the root. This has happened with many other things in like manner, as could be proven at length, and as has long since been done by many learned people, as is clearly evident. And so that I may conclude this my report, I wish to have earnestly exhorted and asked all those who shall read it, for the sake of God’s honor, that if they believe there is any error or defect therein, they would kindly point it out to me; but if they find it—as I hope—to be in every way consistent with the Divine Word, then

<column-break/>

they should no longer let themselves be led by the fool’s rope <note>A metaphor for being deceived or led astray like a jester.</note>, but rather give praise and thanks to God the Lord for the great good that He daily delivers them from heavy errors and reveals His truth ever more clearly. And they should not give such rein to their temptations that they no longer seek after the recognized truth. The Cappadocians <note>People of Cappadocia, an ancient region in Asia Minor.</note> (as history testifies), when the royal line among them had died out and the Romans offered them—on account of their faithful service—that they might henceforth be a free people, they would not accept the freedom, but preferred to be servants and bondmen. We should not be so foolish, but rather gladly accept the heartfelt freedom of our souls, which is daily offered to us by God in His word. How many noble nations have fought bravely and chivalrously to obtain or preserve physical freedom? How much more should all Christians fight against the Devil’s cunning, so that the freedom of their souls, which is far more precious, be not suppressed by various superstitions? Let no one on earth hold anything dearer than the freedom of their soul and conscience; let no one, as Paul says, suppress the truth in unrighteousness. Let everyone, whether young or old, consider within themselves that the time God has given us to live is short, and that we must depart from here much sooner than we ourselves believe, and give answer and account to the righteous God for our faith, deeds, and omissions. To the Lord our God be praise and honor in eternity; may He reach out His hand to all those who still stick in error and superstition, and graciously help them out; and to the others, whom He has delivered therefrom, grant His grace that they may be thankful to Him for such benefit, so that they do not fall back into it again, Amen.

# On what he holds regarding Exorcism;
### as true and clear as he intends to answer for it before God his Lord, Creator, and Redeemer on the Last Judgment Day; also here temporally before his Lordship; likewise before a Christian Community and otherwise before all the world, based on truthful grounds, with a free conscience and good intent.

The questions that have been put to me were mostly concerning "impressions" <note>original: "Bedunckungen"</note>, images, visions, beryl-gazing <term>Beryllistica: the practice of scrying or seeing visions in crystals or beryls</term>, familiar spirits <note>original: "Spiritibus familiaribus"</note>, and others of their kind (because these have been presented to people by certain vagabonds as beautiful Divine arts). Concerning these, I conclude extensively as follows:

First, it is to be noted that there are many kinds of impressions, imaginings, visions, or crystal-gazing. But for me, there are three primary types <note>original: "genera"</note>, among which the first and most significant is this: that which is not sought, not desired, nor forced or compelled through ceremonies, but is innate to certain people (of whom some have been found in the past and are still found today). This comes from a special inclination or the influence of a particular celestial or sidereal <note>original: "Syderischer"</note> cooperation and power, imprinted by the upper heavenly bodies, or otherwise brought forth by Divine Order. Thus, they often become partakers of wonderful foreknowledge <note>original: "Præuisiones"</note> and foresight of future things (though they themselves may not know what they signify). Because this does not happen to every person, and especially now in our time (since the world is quite evil and deranged), it is all the more marvelous. However, those who commonly find these examples are those of a particularly pure soul, a subtle spirit, an undefiled sober body, and a simple, not sophisticated understanding—yet possessing a judging reason—and who are otherwise temperate, truthful, withdrawn, God-fearing, and of a mind that overcomes evil desires. Among these, indeed, some pious preachers are to be counted, some of whom are known to me personally, while others are understood through their teaching. Often, in their studies, they do not think of such magnificent phrases, examples, words, and speeches, but these are given to them on the pulpit while preaching and proclaiming God's word through the Holy Spirit (as God promised to Moses in Exodus 4 and Christ to his disciples in Mark 13 and Luke 21). These are spoken and preached by them unexpectedly for the comfort of the human race. All this happens because God wants His omnipotence, holiness, and gifts—which come from Him alone—to be praised, and does not want them attributed to human skill (according to the words of Paul in 1 Corinthians 6: "Your bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit who dwells in you, whom you have from God and not from yourselves"). Now, when something happens to such a person, whether male or female, by chance through Divine inspiration and natural power or cooperation, or a vision or dream appears or comes to them—be it in preaching, in the air, in crystals, or in sleep—and that person, out of sincere simplicity with humble...

If a person asks God their Creator from the bottom of their heart—provided it is not contrary to Divine Omnipotence or harmful to their soul—for understanding and the meaning of a chance occurrence, an appearing vision, dream, speech, or hearing, I consider that such a person (as John speaks in his first Epistle in the third chapter: *Whoever is born of God does not commit sin, for the Son of God remains in him.* <note>original: "Wer auß Gott geboren ist / der thut nicht Sünde / dann der Sohne Gottes bleibet in jhm." Likewise, God appeared to Solomon in a dream (1 Kings 3). <margin>II. Revelation that is corrupted by the Devil with superstition and worldly honor.</margin>
The second species arises from the aforementioned one and is almost to be compared to a <term>changeling</term> <note>A "Wechselbalck" or "Supposititio" refers to a folkloric substitute left by fairies or demons; here it means a false imitation of a true vision.</note>. He tries all his artistic tricks and imagines to the person how they are acceptable and dear to God, and something more than other people. He tries to see if he can bring them to pride, superstition, worldly ambition, or contempt for their neighbor. As soon as he brings the person so far that they, out of curiosity, brood over the meaning of such things, or ask advice from other people who perhaps deal with banishing, conjuring, or other diabolical <term>prestigia</term> <note>Deceptive tricks or illusions.</note>, or

Cyprian also teaches this finely when he says in the book *On the Double Death* that those who practice and use sorcery (but I add and say: also those who believe those who deal with it) deny Christ because they make a pact or covenant with the Devil. Likewise, they become those who teach and preach the vision of their own heart and not from the mouth of the Lord. There is no different judgment for such occurrences than for those who, through their fasting, praying, going on pilgrimages, and other self-chosen works and holiness, think they earn salvation from God, but with ungrateful minds and hearts set aside, dishonor, and despise the merit of Christ, as if His merit were not enough to redeem them.

# Thurneysser’s Considerations

Furthermore, none of such worshippers of demons <note>original: "Cultorum Dæmonũ"</note> ever died a proper natural death, as one has had to see most pitiably in the cases of Emperor Valens, Gonzaga, and Aegidius de Rara.

One has also never heard of anyone who, through his spirit or devil, or even his lying prophecies, did not eventually become a liar and fall into shame, as one reads of Socrates, Nero, and Cornelius Agrippa. Regarding this, Irenaeus says in Book 1, Chapter 9: "You should know that prophecy is not instilled by Marcus the Black-Artist <note>original: "Schwarz-Künstler," referring to a practitioner of the dark arts or necromancy</note>, but God grants the same through His grace; and those who receive it from God speak when God wills, and not when Marcus commands them."

They were all punished before the world, as can be learned from Simon the Sorcerer—who was born in the village of Gitton in Samaria—as well as from Apollonius of Tyana and Manasseh. With body and soul, almost all such necromancers <note>original: "Necromantici"</note>, even if they died here temporally in wretched poverty and misery, were carried away by the devil, as has been sufficiently experienced with Antoninus Heliogabalus, the "Tall Priest" of Salzburg, and a female exorcist in England. If time and opportunity permitted, I could write an entire book full of such examples.

But as for the other question concerning the *familiares* <note>familiar spirits</note>, fiery little men, and other spirits that wander in the Tangutian desert <note>likely referring to the Gobi Desert or regions of Central Asia</note>, as well as in Sicily and the Northern lands—such as Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and other places—all of which are named for the deception of mankind: I hold them all to be devilish phantoms. Even if they occasionally do something "good" for a person (as he might perceive it), they are nevertheless favorable neither to God nor to man, nor to other creatures. To these they are

<column-break/>

highly opposed, being their worst enemies and—as is sensed by the leading astray of ships and their deceitful shouting—their destroyers. Therefore, I believe and know for certain that God has assigned to every human being a holy, rational, pure soul, a Good Spirit dwelling within him—that is, his mind—and a holy angel. Every Christian should be content with these and should alienate, withdraw, and withhold themselves from all other spirits, fleeing their help and never calling upon them. Even if they offer to serve him, he must not let himself be persuaded to use them, speak with them, or command them to do anything, lest he lose all the grace of God and the salvation of his soul. Instead, he should cross himself <note>original: "sich vor jhnen gesegnen"</note> against them, call upon God for His true Holy Spirit and for help and deliverance against them, put forward the merit of Christ, and thus, with firm faith, despise them as null, powerless, lying, and deceptive spirits. He should mock them and spit upon them, hold them in no regard, and (since they are nothing but loose, useless winds without the permission of God) not fear them.

That such sorcery is a heavy sin is found in 1 Samuel and also 2 Kings 17. That God punishes an entire land for the sake of such sin is read in Jeremiah 27. Therefore, according to the judgment of God in Deuteronomy 18 and Exodus 22, I hold nothing of them, but deem them unworthy to live; for it stands in Malachi 3 that they should be rooted out. From all of this (although I have framed the answer to such a high question quite briefly), it can be sufficiently seen what I hold regarding such exorcism <note>original: "Exorciſmo"</note> and also regarding the exorcists.

<margin>One should root out the sorcerers.</margin>

# Master Leonhardi

However, I must confess by my conscience that although I possess a significant portion—indeed, almost the majority—of the books of Paracelsus <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), a famous physician and alchemist.</note> collected together, I have not yet found among his own handwriting any experiments that could be blamed or forbidden by the Christian Church. But because I have diligently collected his writings from all sorts of places at no small expense, I have indeed obtained many written books which are held by sensible people to be Paracelsian, but truly were not his; in these, many such loose fragments are mixed in. I acquired these not because I wished to learn or use them, but solely so that I might experience—and have proof against them—with what vain, worthless, and improper maneuvers the weary Devil leads the poor, miserable human race by a fool's rope.

Therefore, one should distinguish all three species of Magic (although Cicero and Aristotle count only two genera or kinds, namely the artificial and the natural), just as the little word or the noun *Magia* <note>Magic</note> (which is neither Hebrew, Greek, nor Latin, but a Persian word, and a *nomen aequivocum* <note>an equivocal name</note>, meaning that just like *eisch* or *exais* <note>likely referring to Greek terms for "force" or "appearance"</note> it has a twofold meaning) brings such division or partitioning of itself—regardless of the fact that Suidas <note>A 10th-century Greek encyclopedist.</note> opines that the word originated from the *Maguseis*.

Now *Magus* means, in the Persian as well as partly in the Syrian language, just as much as *Nabin* among the Hebrews, *Habim* among the Chaldeans, *sophos* <note>original: "σοφός" - wise</note> among the Greeks, and *sapiens* in the Latin language—in German, "wise." Or even as Vitruvius names them in the preface to Book 8: *Magus*, *Sacerdos*, or wise priests. Thus there are many kinds of wisdom: one is wise unto evil, like Simon Magus <note>A biblical figure often cited as the first heretic and a practitioner of dark arts.</note>, the very worst Magus and most cursed sorcerer. Then another is wise unto good, like the Magi who traveled from the East—not to worship a devil, but to worship and honor the Lord Christ as an enemy of all devils. Therefore, it does not depend on the name or the word that one speaks, but on that which one speaks about; that is, that one judges the understanding of the words from the causes of the speech (so that one does not, as Aristotle says, capture the highest powers of the mind or bind them to the external senses). Whoever considers this can easily understand that from the two significations there is a forbidden magic as well as a permitted, useful Magic. Paracelsus undoubtedly knew the latter, and it is a natural, artistic Magic; it proceeds without conjuration, sacrifice, or the calling upon of spirits. It can and may well be used outside of Divine wrath, without harm to one's neighbor, and without violation of the Christian faith. Its parts are Cabala, Steganography (I am not speaking here of Trithemius's <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), whose "Steganographia" was often accused of being demonic magic.</note>), and Natural Magic, which Joseph, Moses, and Solomon used. Of this, Tertullian speaks in his book *On the Trinity*: it is this, namely the Holy Spirit, who has established and ordained the prophets in the Church, who is the master teacher of all, who governs the tongues (I speak here of true tongues) and performs wonders.

<margin>Natural magic.</margin>

Likewise, He who gives understanding to govern, who shares counsel; as Cyprian also says, He (meaning the Holy Spirit) gave wisdom to Solomon, understanding to Daniel, counsel to Joseph, strength to Samson, knowledge to Moses, fear of God to David, and patience to Job. This is the wisdom which among the Greeks was called *paideia* <note>original: "παιδεία" - education or culture</note> as the highest, most perfect wisdom.

There is also an unnatural Magic, which uses a superstitious Astrology, black art, conjurations, numbers, and characters, which Zoroaster, Artephius, and also Iarchas the Indian King and others practiced. The Greeks call this *goeteian* <note>original: "γοητεία" - sorcery or witchcraft</note>, which is properly an incantation or sorcery, which the Christian Church rightly condemned and erased from the Book of Life. This is the one of which Nicephorus speaks when he says: they have with letters

# Master Leonhard
<meta>Catchword: but</meta>

I have not traveled among the Muscovites <note>People of the Grand Duchy of Moscow/Russia</note>, Egyptians, and Armenians so carelessly that I failed to observe their customs and ceremonies (since I wandered almost entirely for that purpose). Yet, I am not for that reason an Armenian, a Mameluke, nor a Muscovite. What then should prevent me from understanding and recognizing—from the Church Fathers and other teachers—the heresies and errors of the Arians, Eutychians, Nestorians, Antitrinitarians <note>Various historical groups deemed heretical by the mainstream church for their differing views on the nature of the Trinity or Christ</note>, and other fanatics (even if they deal in them quite quietly and subtly so that one does not notice)? I am not, for that reason, an Arian, Eutychian, Nestorian, nor an Antitrinitarian.

Thus I am also, praise be to God, no <margin>mute from birth <note>original Greek: ἐν γενέσει ἄλαλος</note></margin> or born silent, nor am I blind. I have been for so long in wars, on water and land, at court, and otherwise involved in all kinds of affairs, that I can hear, notice, understand, and see the dealings and operations of the world—how spiritual, worldly, high, common, and opposing forces interact. Therefore, by comparing past histories, I can surmise and judge what will become of things in time (just as correctly as Theodotus of Chios and Pothinus <note>Advisors to Ptolemy XIII who predicted the Roman Civil War would follow Pompey to Egypt</note> judged from the state of affairs that if they received Pompey, they would draw the war into Egypt). Therefore, although I am a student of <term>Mathematics</term> <note>In this period, "Mathematics" often included astronomy and astrology</note>, and perhaps in my practice I do not please everyone who <margin>prognostically <note>original Greek: προγνωστικῶς</note></margin> and falsely twists my work or interprets it according to their envious mind—I am not, as such people claim, a heretic, a <term>Necromancer</term> <note>original: Nigromanticus; one who communicates with the dead or practices black magic</note>, or a conjurer of devils. I care nothing at all if all my enemies fight against me and present the Devil, their spirit of lies, as an advocate against me; they will nevertheless be unable to topple this truth but must confess that (as experience brings with it) there are various celestial constitutions and inclinations implanted by Nature which do not only signify and promise good things, but also work such things through Divine permission. Conversely, these same things, together with the temperament of the bodies, also turn and change good into evil; yet

<column-break/>

I speak expressly: they do this not out of their own power, but out of God’s order, will, might, and authority (just as the Devil plagued Job). And every sensible person should believe this. For there are many and various causes which govern all things in quite different ways, all of which causes are governed and ruled by a <term>First Free Cause</term> <note>original Latin: Causa prima libera; referring to God as the ultimate source of all motion and existence</note>, while the others, as subjects and subordinates, must follow the first. Nevertheless, all this happens according to the order established for them by the Creator, and thus proceeds steadily forward. For the <term>Stars</term> <note>original: Gestirn; referring to the planetary bodies and constellations</note> have their operation by Divine command, so that with a certain course come the inclinations or tendencies, and from those the temperaments, and from those come humans, fruit, seeds, and other growths. Likewise, storms and other things surely manifest each in its own time. Therefore, let no one think that I do not know, or that I do not understand and confess, that humans (whatever the stars or their positions may show) should not establish or pronounce the most secret will of God as their own, just like the cunning and intended plots of the Devil. Nor do I believe, write, speak, or confess it to be as absolutely certain as that a human must be born, a fruit must grow, or some other great mutation must happen, as if one were so bound to it that it could not be otherwise. Therefore, I wonder how a mortal man can be persuaded by idle liars to believe that anyone is so "Cyclopean" <note>meaning barbaric or one-sided in vision</note> or senseless as to teach that every event can be so precisely investigated and fathomed in the stars, and the times and moments predicted and shown so infallibly and certainly before they happen, that even what is fathomed must occur exactly so, whether it be pleasing or grieving to God. Indeed, far be it from us that we should treat the true or Christian and permitted way of the actions and effects of the stars as if they...

# Thurneysser’s Reflections

->on the Creator<-

...than the Creator, or for someone to imagine, or otherwise establish and prepare a peculiar or somewhat superstitious <term>Human Philosophy</term> <note>The author uses this to mean a man-made system of thought that ignores divine providence</note> that is contrary to God’s word. Such a philosophy would suggest that one could prevent danger or obtain special utility through one’s own power and ability, outside of God’s Omnipotence, favor, blessing, will, and pleasure. For Sarah became pregnant outside the natural course of things; Elizabeth likewise gave birth to a son; the rain was withheld (1 Samuel 12); the sun was darkened during the suffering of Christ; it stood still in the time of Hezekiah’s sickness; it delayed its course during the storming of the city of Jericho—all according to the nature and will of the Creator, and not at all according to the nature and will of the creature.

Therefore, God has not forbidden the gazing upon the stars, nor has He prohibited the distinguishing and differentiating of their <term>Sympathy and Antipathy</term> <note>The hidden natural attractions or repulsions between celestial bodies and earthly things</note>. Likewise, He has no aversion or dislike toward one considering the observation and investigation of the heavenly bodies. It is not against His will that one, through such diligent considerations, observations, and records, reflects deeply on the nature of future events, and from such inclinations and effects of the <term>Temperaments</term> <note>The four bodily humors/dispositions believed to be influenced by the planets</note>, also predicts or prophesies their outcome. But God has forbidden, and it is contrary to Him, if one does such things out of a superstitious, frivolous mind that is turned away from God and directed only toward the stars, trusting, believing, or esteeming the creature more than the Creator.

Therefore, I continue ever forward in the name of God and remain in my previous manner—without any superstition or false belief—to the praise of God my Lord, Creator, and Redeemer, for the benefit of my neighbor, and to my own credit, to write <term>Calendars</term> <note>Almanacs containing astronomical data and predictions</note> according to my own method. And I admonish the honor-loving reader: where he shall find mention of the danger of fire, let him instruct his household so that they may take better care regarding fire.

<column-break/>

Furthermore, where "homicide" or "bloodshed" etc. is written, let everyone guard themselves against the causes, such as drunkenness, anger, gambling, envy, hatred, adultery, and other causes that bring about homicide, bloodshed, and other such evils.

If he then finds "good times," "fair weather," or "joyful news," let everyone praise the Lord of the stars for such divine gifts and use them with such gratitude that God may be moved through His mercy to allow more of the same to come.

Furthermore, where "famine," "war," "unfortunate deeds," "evil plots or schemes," "storms," and the like are written, let everyone pray to God the Lord for the turning away of such burdensome occurrences.

<margin>
GOD allows His temporal punishment to be turned away through prayer. In Luke 21 it is said: *Pray, that you may be able to escape all these things that are to come.* <note>original: "Orate, vt possitis effugere oĩa hęc, quę ventura sunt."</note> See the example in Jonah 1 & 3, and of King Hezekiah in Isaiah 38.
</margin>

But regarding what is mentioned of treachery, shameful acts, sorrow, death, and the trials of high-ranking, learned, and common persons: no one should believe that I—in this calendar as in all others—intend to lead them away from trusting in God's grace toward any kind of superstition without natural causes, or toward any fear, terror, or despair in the Divine promise (as some falsely accuse me). Rather, I wish much more to point them toward the fear of God, toward prayer, and toward a better life. And all and everyone, of whatever rank or dignity they may be, should know certainly and without doubt that all my <term>practiciren</term> <note>The practice of making astrological predictions</note> proceeds from no other ground or foundation than this alone, from which the prophecy of <term>Cratippus</term> <note>A Peripatetic philosopher and friend of Cicero</note> flowed: When the great Pompey, after the battle in the Pharsalian field, asked him in his garden whether he truly thought that God concerned Himself with human affairs, since he [Pompey] had to suffer defeat in a just cause (as he considered it). Thereupon Cratippus said: that governments, like all other things on Earth, had their appointed course and their set limits and times from God, according to which they must grow and fall, and become good or evil. ## Whether even in this our time among

### Summary Content of this Little Treatise.

<margin>Proposition I.</margin>
The Devil can, neither through himself nor through other persons, inflict any harm on anyone, nor can he violate or blind them, etc.

<column-break/>

<margin>Exception to Proposition I.</margin>
Unless it is permitted to him by God, and that happens:
1. For the punishment of unbelievers and sinners.
2. For the testing of the Pious.
3. For the exercise of faith <note>original Latin: "exercitio fidei"</note>, so that the Majesty of God may be honored and feared all the more diligently.

<margin>Proposition II.</margin>
And although the Devil can inflict harm through God’s permission: yet a limit is set for him: and this is proven by examples:
Job 1. The Lord said to Satan: Behold, all that he has is in your hand; only do not lay your hand upon the man himself.
Also Luke 4. When the Devil had ended every temptation, etc.

<margin>Proposition III.</margin>
The witches or "Devil-women" <note>original: "Teuffelsweiber"</note> can also do no harm: rather, the Devil violates and blinds them with:
1. Deception and the imagination of a thing that is not actually so, such as that they: 1. take on foreign shapes. 2. become invisible. 3. come together over many miles to hold costly banquets and high living. 4. inflict harm. 5. gain knowledge of other people whom they have never seen.

<margin>Proposition IV.</margin>
The witches or monsters <note>original: "Vnholden," a term for demons or sorcerers.</note> also cannot keep their pacts with the Devil. For he is a spirit. And when it happens, he blinds them:
1. Through apparitions.
2. Through children who are stolen and are called changelings <note>term: "Wechselbälge" — folklore figures believed to be fairy or demon offspring substituted for human infants.</note>.

<margin>Proposition V.</margin>
The Devil can, neither for himself nor through his sorcerers and soothsayers, etc., know more than what he perceives and grasps from natural things and forthcoming means, solely as a sharp-witted Physician <note>In the sense of a "natural philosopher" or scientist.</note> and swift spirit: He is thereby often deceived: because God alone can:
1. Change nature.
2. Avert the forthcoming misfortune.
3. Make the good evil and the evil good.

# A Brief, Faithful Warning, Notice, and Instruction:

### Whether even in this our time among
### us Christians, witches, sorcerers, and monsters
### are present, and what they are able
### to accomplish, etc.

->To the Christian Reader.<-

<margin>
Numbers chapters 22 and 23.
Exodus 7.
1 Samuel 28.
Acts 8.
Punishment of sorcerers.
Exodus 22.
Galatians 5.
</margin>
There are, dear Christian reader, many people, even in this our time, who say and believe that among Christian folk, sorcerers and perhaps evil people who keep company with the Devil, etc., must not be present at all. Yet, whoever has read anything in history finds that at all times sorcerers and monsters <note>original: "Vnholden" – a term for fiends, demons, or those in league with them</note> have been found even among the people of God, just as the Holy Scripture of both the Old and New Testaments indicates several sorcerers. For in the Old Testament, the sorcerer Balaam is mentioned; likewise, the black-magicians <note>original: "Schwartzkünstler"</note> who stood before King Pharaoh against Moses, the man of God; likewise the sorceress who let King Saul see and hear the prophet Samuel. In the New Testament, the sorcerer Simon <note>Simon Magus</note>, etc. Experience among us also shows that from day to day such vice has crept in, and through certain circumstances and evidence <note>original: "Indicien" – legal term for clues or signs</note> appears manifest and true. Therefore, they have not unjustly been made hateful and punished at all times. As in Exodus 22, God commands the Israelite people that they should not let the sorceresses live. So also the Holy Spirit in the New Testament excludes such evil people from the Kingdom of God, where it is said: No fornicator, adulterer, sodomite, murderer, drunkard, or sorcerer shall or will inherit the Kingdom of God. Also in the time of the Emperors Constantius and Julian (as is written in the ninth book of the Code under the 6th law), such people, because they are enemies and contrary to nature, were straightway condemned from life to death and executed. But in this our time, they are not unjustly burned with fire, just like heretics, and that requires no proof, for we see such punishment sufficiently before our eyes; from which it is to be concluded that sorcerers have always and in every way been among God's people, and still are.

<column-break/>

<margin>
Power of sorcerers.
Division of this tract on witches, sorcerers, and monsters.

II.
III.
Power of the Devil.

Regarding their power, however, and what they have accomplished or are able to accomplish, etc., I wish to touch upon briefly. And so that this matter may be brought to and taken with better understanding, I will primarily take it upon myself to treat three points and parts. And first, to show whether the Devil and his following, the sorcerers, can inflict harm upon cattle and humans, and to what extent, etc. Secondly, whether sorcerers specifically can do any harm on their own, make weather <note>original: "Wetter machen" – the superstitious belief that witches could conjure storms and hail</note>, and travel in an instant to a gathering and for pleasure over many miles' distance; also whether they can keep carnal company with the Devil. And then finally for the third, whether the Devil and his following could prophesy future things, not yet happened, beforehand, etc. May God grant His grace to treat something useful from these points, through Jesus Christ our Lord and Savior, Amen.

As far as the first point is concerned, regarding the power of the Devil, St. Peter says in his 1st Epistle in the 5th chapter: Be sober and vigilant, for your adversary the Devil walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour. And St. Paul in Ephesians 6: We wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against...

# Master Abraham Saur

The second point: whether sorcerers in particular—that is, those who fall away from God and serve the loathsome Devil—can do harm and create storms through their sorcery, or travel to gatherings and places of pleasure many miles away, etc. This is somewhat complex and hidden from many people, therefore it cannot, shall not, nor may it be decided in brevity. I say, however, as far as I perceive, that such people can do nothing at all on their own; rather, whatever happens is either caused by Nature, or God permits it to Satan. The Devil then carries out his jugglery and <term>mirror-fencing</term><note>original: "Spiegelfechtens" - a term for shadow-boxing or deceptive illusions</note> with the poor people, so that they swear they themselves had done this or that, made this or that storm, allowed themselves to be seen or heard at places of pleasure and dance floors, dallied with the Devil, fathered children, and other such foolishness, etc. For how should these poor, cursed people and sorcerers be able to change the air, make storms, and inflict sickness and other things upon people, when even the Devil, their master, cannot do it by himself?

<margin>
NOTE.
</margin>

And when it does happen, God must permit and allow it to him; otherwise, it is not possible for the Devil to bend a single hair on a person's head, or to shift a single minute of time. If such things stood in the Devil's power, he would truly play the game vehemently and destroy and exterminate mankind, especially the pious. Therefore, St. Chrysostom says in the first book on Matthew: The Devil is not allowed to tempt men as much as he would like, for if it were up to him, he would never cease tempting, which is his foremost and only work; since otherwise he neither eats nor sleeps, nor does anything else but tempt, deceive, and destroy—that is his food. <note>original: "Speise"</note> Thus Chrysostom intends that the Devil cannot tempt as much as he desires, etc. But how does it happen (one might ask) that harm nevertheless occurs, people and cattle are destroyed, and gruesome storms are heard? The causes were heard above in the first point. Furthermore, one might ask: why then do the sorcerers dare to say in their confessions and <term>interrogations</term><note>original: "Urgichten" - formal confessions under torture or legal questioning</note>, and even die upon the claim, that they had made this or that storm or damage?

Words of Chrysostom.

Satan is a master of a thousand arts, a sharp-witted physicist, and a swift spirit in astronomy. Thus they believe they have awakened the storm through their trickery, and they swear an oath that it happened through them and not otherwise. Likewise, when the Devil plagues and punishes people by God's permission (for he is God's executioner), he persuades and deceives the poor people into doing this or that, perhaps even giving them the materials for it; then they swear that the misfortune or accident happened through them. Therefore, Peter Lombard also says in the second book of *Sentences*, distinction 7: Sorcery is performed through the art and power of the Devil, who nevertheless received his power and understanding from God to deceive deceitful people—such as the Egyptians—or the sorcerers themselves. These sorcerers, who are now held in high regard through the cooperation of those spirits, must in the future be damned. This serves either to deceive them or to warn the faithful so that they do not lust after such arts, or to exercise and prove the patience of the righteous. One should also not hold that visible creatures serve the Devil according to his pleasure, but much more God, from whom they also receive this power. If that is so, one might say, why then are people punished so painfully for it? *The punishment should hold its authors.* <note>Latin: "Poena debebat tenere suos autores." **Answer:** That happens likewise through the deception and blinding of the Devil, who in sleep so strongly represents things to them in form through fantasy <note>imagination or mental imagery</note> that they think no differently than that they see the people in person, eat and drink, speak and live physically with them; just as when one lies in a dream, eats and drinks with people, does this and that, and when one wakes up, there is nothing to be built upon it.

> I say to you, son of Aeacus, that you the Romans can conquer.
<note>original Latin: "Aio te Æaciden Romanos vincere posse." This is a famous linguistic riddle. Because of the Latin grammar, it can mean either "You will conquer the Romans" or "The Romans will conquer you."</note>

That is: I tell you, Aeacides, with certainty, that your men of war will overcome the Romans. This was understood in two ways: namely, that your men of war [would overcome] the Romans, or the Romans [would overcome] your men of war. Thus one understands how and when the devils know secrets and can prophesy future things, and that their words—in which nothing but deceit and cunning are to be found—are not to be believed.

### A Brief Examination of this Confession.

->First, she confesses voluntarily<-
->before torture:<-

That Eva became weak, likewise the cows, etc.

This is true by the evidence of the matter. But that the damage came from her, the witch—perhaps through a wish, etc.—that is not true, God unwilling <note>original: "Deo nolente"</note>. For as has often been heard, without God's will, the Devil or his followers cannot bend even the slightest hair on the head of a Christian person, nor inflict any suffering; much less can anyone be

<column-break/>

injured in their body by mere words, wishes, or curses. For if such things were clinging and true, how could one person remain safe from another? She, the witch, also adds—not without reason—the word "perhaps," whereby she gives it to be understood that she does not know it for certain, etc.

->[That her paramour came to her and<-
->had business with her.]<- That the Devil appeared to this person may be true; but that he should also have had carnal business with her is a thing that is not easily believed, since the Devil has neither flesh nor blood and can create nothing, but only defiles and deludes.

->[And advised her to<-
->damage the cattle.]<- This may also be true, for the Devil goes about like a roaring lion, etc. <note>A reference to 1 Peter 5:8</note>, and has been a liar and a murderer from the beginning.

->[The people hold her for a<-
->sorceress, and she is one of those people.]<-
One might say: what further testimony is needed? Her own word and confession are there, etc. Yes, true; but one must know all the circumstances and details, and consider in what manner she practiced sorcery—whether with words or with deeds—and the punishment must be arranged accordingly.

Meanwhile, the Devil may have practiced his jugglery and fantasy with this person, and suggested to her in a dream how she had been at revelries, dance floors, and other far-off places, confusing her senses and holding her therewith. Examples are ready at hand.

# Preface

otherwise brought little use or piety to other high-ranking persons, but rather made them much more confused and doubtful as to whether such evil people are to be found and whether they should be lawfully punished. Because of this, I have been moved to compose and treat the entire matter in a short, summary conceptual framework, as methodically as possible.

But when Your Princely Grace <note>original: "E. F. G." (Euer Fürstlichen Gnaden), a formal address for royalty or high nobility</note> well and piously remembers that a Christian Authority is established by God Himself and girded with the worldly sword, not only to uphold the **Second Table** of God’s Commandments <note>The "Second Table" refers to the laws governing human relationships (murder, theft, etc.)</note> regarding the protection and defense of one's neighbor, but also—because we are all created in the image of God—to rescue the honor of God; thus it is primarily the office of us all, and especially of the Christian Authority, that they should also defend the **First Table** of the Holy Ten Commandments <note>The "First Table" refers to duties toward God, such as avoiding idolatry and blasphemy</note> with all their might and power. Such Christian and noble thoughts as Your Princely Grace has held have, praise and thanks be to God, progressed so far that they have been earnestly put into action; and the blasphemous, apostate, and God-perjuring women and sorceresses have been taken into custody by Your Princely Grace, and according to their testimony and merit, condemned from life to death and burned with fire.

So that Your Princely Grace may have a good conscience, and so that the mouths of other ignorant people—of whom very many are found everywhere, who call evil good and good evil and might find fault with Your Princely Grace—might be stopped, I have herewith most humbly dedicated this small summary treatise to Your Princely Grace. This is not to forestall others, but much more out of Christian, humble love, to defend Your Princely Grace against the aforementioned malevolent critics and mockers <note>original: "Maleuolos vnnd Momos," referring to ill-wishers and Momus, the Greek god of satire and mockery</note>, and also to give others cause to follow Your Princely Grace’s Christian zeal and example in all modesty. I herewith commend Your Princely Grace, along with your beloved spouse and young lordship, into the gracious protection and shield of God, and recommend myself to your acceptable service. Given at Frankfurt, the 1st of March, Anno [15]83.

# Explanation and actual report of this little treatise on several points and questions concerning witchcraft.

<column-break/>

I. It is asked whether there truly be sorcerers or sorceresses.

II. What they can accomplish and do with their witchcraft: Whether, according to their pleasure, or out of their hatred and anger, they can kill, lame, or damage a human being or cattle.

III. Whether the means which they use and apply for such purposes have such a nature or effect that this or that might follow from them.

IV. Since such is not the case, and they can accomplish nothing with all their diligence and effort, whether they should then be punished in their life.

V. What is to be held of this matter when they say: Their paramour, the Devil, transforms himself into human shape and has dealings with them, and that they also sometimes conceive children by him.

### Concerning the First Point.
### Whether there be sorcerers or sorceresses.

<column-break/>

To answer this point, we neither should nor can deny such a thing at all, because Holy Scripture itself testifies to it, as it stands written in the 2nd Book of Moses <note>Exodus</note> in the 22nd Chapter: **Thou shalt not suffer a sorceress to live.** And again, in the 5th Book of Moses <note>Deuteronomy</note> in the 18th Chapter, we read in the 9th, 10th, 11th, and 12th verses, with these words: **When thou art come into the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee, thou shalt not learn to do after the abominations of those nations, that there be not found among you any one that [maketh] his**

->Concerning the second point.<-

<margin>What they accomplish with their sorcery, whether they can lame, damage, and kill humans or livestock, etc.</margin>

Regarding this, one should know in brief words that just as the Devil cannot do everything he would like to do, even so little—and much less—can the witches do. For the Devil is a declared enemy of God and of mankind, and desires and would dearly wish that he might not only deprive man of his salvation and blessedness, but that he might also bring God Himself to nothing and root Him out, so that there were no God at all to punish evil, and that he alone held the government in his hand. The Devil certainly wished and desired that; but it is inconvenient to God the Lord to hand over His government to another; rather, He wishes to keep the sword by the hilt. He wishes to be the helmsman in the ship and hold the rudder, and not the Devil. Therefore, we also confess in the articles of our Christian faith that God alone is Almighty, who has created all things and still governs, and not the Devil; the providence is His, and not the Devil's. In the holy "Our Father" <note>The Lord's Prayer</note> we also pray: Lord, lead us not into temptation; that is, we pray that He would not permit the Devil to have power over us, so that he might tempt us beyond our ability; for His is the kingdom,

<column-break/>

and not the Devil's; His is the power, and not the Devil's.

Therefore, we also see from the Book of Job that the Devil appears before the face of God with the children of God—that is, with the holy angels—to listen to and carry out what God, his strict Lord and Master, would command him. When the Lord then asks him, "From where do you come, Satan? What is my servant Job doing, the likes of whom is not in the land, simple and upright, God-fearing, and avoiding evil?" Satan answers Him, "Yes, Lord, Job has good reason to hope in You; he has good reason to trust You, for You are around him like a circular wall <note>original: "Ringmawer"</note>; but do one thing and stretch out Your hand, and touch him and all that he has; just give him into my claws for once, and You shall see that he will curse You to Your face." And the Lord said: "Behold, all that he has is in your hand; only upon himself do not lay your hand." That is indeed a petition <term>supplication: a formal request or plea</term> of the Devil against the holy Job, in which he confesses that God is always with and around His own, and that he also has no power over them or their goods, unless God the Lord allows him. Thus, afterward, He allows him again at his request to strike Job's body, but to do no harm or injury to his life; he had to comply with this as well, and not reach further than the Lord had commanded and allowed him.

Thus we read in the first book of Kings in the 22nd chapter, when God the Lord wished to punish the godless King Ahab, the wretched Devil also appears before the judgment seat of God; and as God the Lord, the supreme Judge, passes His righteous sentence upon Ahab, that He wishes to punish him, Satan says he should be used as a rod and an executioner over Ahab, and he would go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of his prophets, so that they should lead him astray, and he would thus lose his life. God allows him this, and the judgment of God over Ahab is carried out, which the Devil otherwise would not have dared to do if God the Lord had not first allowed it to him.

# Concerning Witches and Monsters.

The devil does not even have the power to enter into an unclean, desert sow, nor to plague it according to his will; rather, he must first petition <note>original: "Suppliciren"</note> and beg that God might permit it to him. God must pass His judgment upon the sins of mankind in such a way that the devil may do so, as we read in Luke chapter 8, which happened with the swine of the Gadarenes <note>A reference to the biblical story where Jesus casts demons out of a man and into a herd of pigs</note>, where he had to beg the Lord Christ for it while He was still in His state of humiliation: how much more must he do so now, since Christ is exalted to the right hand of God.

From all of this, we see that the devil cannot harm us when he wants, how he wants, or where he wants. Therefore, we should [disregard] the shameful, powerless, cursed devil, who dare not touch a single hair of ours—much less bend or pluck us—who dare not harm a sow without God's will, and who cannot even make a louse, as we see from the second book of Moses <note>Exodus</note> in the eighth chapter. When the sorcerers, with the help of the devil and by God's permission, imitated everything that Moses and Aaron did—they turned water into blood, they brought frogs and toads over the land, they brought forth all kinds of vermin, they brought pestilence, they brought evil black blisters <note>boils</note>, they brought locusts, they brought darkness over the land—then the Lord God finally let the devil and his sorcerers be put to shame, so that he could not imitate even the very least thing, and could not even make a louse without God's permission. Why then should we fear this lousy devil? We should not do the villain so much honor as to be afraid of him. For if we fear and tremble before him, we give it to be understood as if he had power over us and might harm us according to his caprice, when and how he willed. But he cannot and dare not do that, neither in his own person nor through his servants or handmaids, witches or sorcerers, who have no power over us; rather, he must first petition, and the Lord God must allow and permit it to him.

But He permits it to him when we sin, when we are reckless in our office and calling, in our household management, when we do not pray, when we do not raise our children in the fear of God but let them go like dumb cattle, and perhaps even lie down with our children in the devil's name rather than in God's name, and likewise rise again. When people bless <note>ironic use: to curse or invoke</note> what their children, servants, and even cattle eat or drink in the devil's name rather than in God's name. In such cases, God, out of His righteous judgment against sin, permits the devil and evil people to inflict harm upon us, yet no more than He imposes upon them in a measured command. Therefore, let everyone be diligent in prayer, be godly, believe in Jesus Christ, and fear neither devil nor sorcery, and offer them a defiance in true faith.

### Concerning the Third Point.

->Whether witches can do anything—that is, lame, blind, or make one deaf—and do such things through the means they use?<-

To this, the following answer is to be noted: If they are able to come so close to a person that they can give them poison or something else to eat, or blow into their nose at night while the person sleeps, or smear their limbs with [ointments], there is no doubt that they can truly lame, blind, or kill them with such things, just like any other evildoer who is not a sorcerer can inflict harm. Thus, several years ago, the people of Geneva also executed a sorcerer upon whose chest the devil had made a mark to show he was his own. This man confessed, among other things, that he had often waylaid the preachers in Geneva, especially Calvin <note>John Calvin, the Protestant Reformer</note>, but was never able to accomplish anything. He had also smeared the handrail of the pulpit with poison so that when he held onto it while ascending and then perhaps [touched his]...

But as to whether they—using their methods, which are often absurd and entirely ridiculous—could actually accomplish as many wonderful things as they claim, such as hewing an axe or a hatchet into a wall and milking milk out of it: to this I answer roundly and openly that these same methods have absolutely nothing to do with the matter. They themselves accomplish nothing with their methods; rather, the Devil does it. He then persuades the poor "Devil’s whores" <note>A derogatory contemporary term for women accused of witchcraft</note> that they performed it themselves, and that the silly methods he prescribes to them possess such an effect.

But it is nothing other than a Diabolical seduction and delusion. For if such a natural power were present in their methods to perform such wonderful things, then it would surely also happen if I, or someone else who knows nothing of such sorcery, used such methods in the same way. It would follow for me just as well and just as readily as it follows for the witches: that I could milk milk out of a hatchet handle—if the hatchet handle were of such a nature that it could give milk. It would also follow for me, if I mixed water and verbena <note>original: "Verbenam"</note> or *masculathura* <note>likely a corruption of "masculatura" or a specific alchemical/magical ingredient</note> and cast it into the air, that hail and tempests would come from it—if water and verbena possessed such power. It would also follow for me: if I took red willow twigs and beat the morning dew with them so that frost would result—if beating with the little twig had such a power. It would also follow for me: if I blew into someone's eyes so that their sight vanished—if such breathing and blowing had such a natural power and effect. It would also follow for me: that I could break someone's spine if I stroked them with my hand—if such stroking had such an effect. It would also follow for me: if I put water into a bowl and poked

<column-break/>

into it with a finger, and thereby poked out another person's eye—if such finger-peering into the water had such an effect, etc. It would also follow for me: if I made a waxen image <note>A "voodoo doll" style effigy used in sympathetic magic</note> and stabbed it in the chest with a knife, that I could thereby stab the heart in the body of another who is absent—if such stabbing into the waxen image had such a power and effect. It would also follow for me: if I took a waxen candle-wick and measured someone with it, and ignited it afterward so that he must waste away and wither—if such measuring and igniting of the waxen cord had such a power, etc. But now, none of this follows when I or another Christian person does it; therefore, it is to be concluded from this that the methods are entirely foolish means which contribute nothing at all to the matter. Indeed, it is just as if I said: "I drank turnip broth, therefore the weather has become beautiful," or "The club stands behind the door, therefore Duke Alençon <note>Francis, Duke of Anjou and Alençon (1555–1584), who attempted to become sovereign of the Netherlands</note> will remain King in Brabant."

That all such effects nevertheless follow when the witches use their methods does not happen because of the witches (that they do it), nor because of the methods (that such a power resides in them), but the Devil does it. However, he lets his meddlesome Devil-whores bury this or that or arrange things outwardly so that they are not idle, but rather appear to be doing something toward it. And he—by the permission and judgment of God against your sins—kills your cows, your horse, your child, your husband, and your wife. He lets them speak certain words, and he takes a wagon of wood and overturns it, or tears a couple of trees out of the earth by the roots, and afterward persuades them that they accomplished it with their methods and their spoken words. As for example: in Gernsheim (a town situated on the Rhine, belonging to the Bishop of Mainz), they recently drowned a sorceress in the Rhine...

He himself, indeed, can enter into human flesh, skin, and bone by God's permission, for he is a subtle spirit; but a pot-shard, a dish-rag, or a piece of glass—which is something earthly, coarse, perceptible, and thick—that he cannot bring in without injuring the outer skin; rather, if he brings it in, he must open and break the skin. And he can certainly do that through his natural art and speed: not only can he hold a person so fast in sleep while they are slumbering that he may make a rip or wound in their skin and stick something therein, but he can also restore and heal that same inflicted damage most precisely within a few hours, so that the person, when they wake up, knows absolutely nothing of what happened to them, nor sees anything on the outer skin, but only feels the evil filth that sticks inside them.

This is because it is natural, and is also often achieved by many people who, through a drink, can cause one to fall into such a deep sleep that they do not wake for twenty-four hours, and even if a leg were cut from their body, they would feel nothing at all. If humans can bring such things to pass through their art, through drinks, and other herbs that they might apply, [how much more so the Devil?]

It is easily believed to be true, though it is not; how much more can the arch-juggler, Black Caspar <note>A traditional folk name for the Devil</note> himself, do: He can in an instant displace one thing and set another in its place. Thus, when a woman milks milk out of an axe handle, no one should think that the axe handle can give milk; rather, the Devil steals the milk from another cow and lets his hell-whore, the sorceress, tug and milk the axe handle for a while, and he pours the milk so finely into her vessel with strokes as if the milk were in the handle, though it is not in there at all.

But as for the hair and brushes, the sorceress may indeed, by order of her lover <note>The "incubus" or demonic lover</note>, shoot or throw them at a person or horse; but that they can shoot them into the body or belly so powerfully that an animal or person perishes from it—that is nothing. Rather, as soon as it leaves the witch's hand, Satan governs it. He gives it—by the righteous judgment of God—an added force. And because he is, as mentioned above, an experienced artist of nature and a master <term>naturalist: one who understands the hidden laws of the physical world</term>, he can dilate and widen the *poros* or steam-holes <note>pores of the skin</note> so much that he can bring brushes or hair through the pores into the body and stomach of a person or animal without injuring the skin. Or, if not through the pores, then through other open passages and *meatus* <note>Latin: openings or channels in the body</note>, of which there are many in humans and animals, and thus cause sickness and thereafter death. Thus, one must place the Devil's highest and best masterpieces within physics and nature, and not above nature. For the Lord God alone can change nature and work something against its course, and not the Devil, *who works according to nature, and not against nature* <note>original: "qui secundùm naturā, & non contra naturam operatur."</note>.

<margin>NB</margin> But I must ask further: you say, because their means are useless means, and the delusion of the Devil has the greatest place in sorcery, what should I then say of their riding away? Does it happen truly, or is it only a delusion, so that they think they are in this or that place? They eat, they drink, they dance, they revel perhaps in wine barrels or in "hare's cheese" <note>A folk term for a type of fungus or perhaps a hallucinogenic substance</note>—do they do it truly, or is it only a delusion of themselves?

<margin>NB</margin> Answer, short and round: Everything that is natural is also possible for the Devil through the permission and judgment of God. Now, it is natural that the Devil can carry his evil and devoted women here and there in the air. It is natural and possible for him that he can open a cellar and slip inside with his bellows <note>his followers or "wind-bags"</note>, and exercise their wantonness not only over the cream pot and cheese basket, but also at the wine barrel; that is possible and therefore also believable. Meanwhile, however, the evil enemy puts himself in the form of a woman into bed with the husband, and holds him so fast in sleep that he does not wake until it is time for the devil's whore to return.

Thereafter I answer the question: that it does not always truly happen so, but that it is only a delusion, so that they think it happens so, when it does not happen. As for example: There was a nobleman who once captured such a sorcerer, and when he had him questioned under pain <note>torture</note>, he understood from him what he had not expected: namely, that the nobleman's own wife was also a sorceress. Thereupon the nobleman thought briefly, and immediately invited his and his wife's kinsfolk to a banquet. When they had come and everything was prepared and served, he sat himself at the front of the table and his wife at the back of the table in a corner, so that she could not come out. And so they were merry. Meanwhile, the nobleman steps away and takes up other business, telling them all to remain seated and be of good cheer. Together with his captive sorcerer, who had appointed the time when he would discover to him the whole business of sorcery and also show him his wife, they go together—well guarded by the nobleman's servants—to the appointed place. In the same manner, it happened years ago at Rockenhausen, that an <term>official</term><note>original: "Amptmann"; a local administrative or judicial officer</note> there had several times caused many such people to be burned, and yet finally doubted within himself whether they were actually capable of anything; he therefore had several of them in custody again and earnestly questioned them about their trade, whether they could actually accomplish anything, and whether they could show it to him, and whether they could take him along without harm. When they said, "Yes," he placed them together in a room and let them loose, but also had the room well-barred from the outside and ordered his servants to keep watch, so that if the prisoners tried to practice any mischief upon him, they should rush in and come to his aid. Now it happened thus: The official sits with them in the room, has several lights lit, and reads in the Bible; the servants stood before the door and watched with all diligence, wishing to see or hear something new. The prisoners lay down in their straw, snored and slept; none desired to do anything, except that they perhaps stretched themselves and rolled about in their sleep. Now when the hour came which had been appointed, and yet another hour passed beyond that, and still none would wake or be up, the official spoke: "Up, up, up!" and kicked a pair of them with his foot—with your favor be it mentioned—upon their backsides; then they started up, scratched their heads, and said: "Oh, oh, Official, how merry we were! Surely now you believe 

<column-break/>

that there is something to it." And when he reminded them how they had not left the room, she said, "No, no, Official, how dare you say that? You were there yourself with us, here and there, in the meadows; there we danced, and as a true sign, the piper sat upon an apple tree, and the branch broke under him." When the official sent someone to check this sign, it was found to be so: the branch was still freshly broken in two, and under the tree was a trampling of feet. The Devil had done this, and presented to them in sleep such a <term>fantasy</term><note>original: "Phantasey"; here meaning a vivid, devilish hallucination</note>, such a dream and object, as if they had been there; for in truth they had not left the room.

In Strasbourg it also happened at one time that such a suspected woman wanted to go to the Lord's Supper. The <term>parish priest</term><note>original: "Pfarrherr"</note>, however, said so much to her in private absolution and searched so deeply that she confessed it, and he promised her with plausible words that he also wished to learn it and travel with her when she next wished to go; they thus appointed the time (though the priest held her off long enough until he also "knew how"). And when the hour was there, he comes to the woman; she seeks out her oven-fork, gave the priest one as well, took grease out of a little jar, and anointed the fork, telling the priest he should do the same. And as she is thus in earnest with the anointing, she falls backward upon the hearth as if thunder had struck her, and smacks with her mouth no differently than a piglet over the slop-trough. The priest watches her and waits for the end, until about an hour later she comes to herself again; she says, "See, Priest, see, now you believe it; how merry we were, how we ate and drank! Now you have seen it yourself." But the priest rebuked her and said to her: "You poor, seduced creature, you have not moved from the hearth, but have lain there like a beast."

This was a <term>mist-cap</term> of the Devil, who had so possessed the stubborn woman's senses and created such a delusion for her, as if they were carousing bravely, and as if she also saw the priest—

# Concerning Witches and Monsters.

**Pastor’s Wife.** And that is also why, even if they have feasted and drunk the whole night through—as they claim—they are nevertheless as hungry in the morning as hungry hunting dogs, because it is nothing but a delusion.

### Concerning the Fourth Point.

> Since they contribute nothing to it, but rather the Devil does it all alone, and they are merely persuaded and crazed into thinking they did it, why then are they punished, and especially in body and life?

To this I give answer, firstly: that they are to be punished because of the express command of God. Exodus in the 22nd Chapter: *You shall not permit a sorcerer to live.* <note>Exodus 22:18</note> Secondly: it is their total intent, will, and meaning that they wish to do harm, and they also believe they are doing it. Since they then have the will to do harm, the will is taken for the deed and the act in all laws, and they are punished as if they had carried it out themselves. Thirdly: they are perjured, faithless, and apostate people who have fallen away from God and their Redeemer, having denied their Baptism and faith. Therefore, they should also be punished in their lives.

For although other heretics <term>Ketzer: those who deviate from established church doctrine</term> err in many ways regarding God’s essence and will, they do not go so far as to expressly deny God and everything that is of God, as the witches must do when they pay homage and swear oaths to the Devil: where they renounce God, his holy angels, and all his saints, their faith, their baptism, heaven, and the soul’s salvation. To this, our arch-enemy, the loathsome Satan, brings them with sweet and thousand-fold cunning flattering words and great promises of this world's goods, and miserably misleads them; in such a way that during the entire time of their sorcery, they do not become one <term>Bingerheller: a small copper coin from Bingen</term> richer than they would have been otherwise.

### Concerning the Fifth Point.

> Whether the Devil, as their paramour, transforms himself into human shape, has dealings with women, and whether they might conceive children from him, etc.

To this I give this answer: that no one should doubt that the Devil can change and transform himself into human form and shape, and also speak with humans. For if the Devil can transform himself into the shape of an angel, as Paul says, it is also possible for him to take the shape of a human, which has happened many times and is manifest. But whether the Devil may sleep with humans, practice unchastity with them, and also beget children with them from such a mingling—that we must examine somewhat more closely. And indeed, regarding the cohabitation of evil spirits with humans, Augustine testifies in Book 15 of *The City of God*, chapter 23. <note>Latin: "de ciuitate Dei"</note> There is a certain rumor, he says, among those who have experienced and known such things, and have encountered them and heard of them, that there are spirits called *Sylvani* <note>Forest-dwelling spirits or fauns in Roman mythology</note> who have done much harm to women, often desiring to sleep with them and to practice unchaste acts with them. Against this, however, writes Cassian the Teacher, and says: It is not easy to believe that the spiritual nature, such as the Devil is, could practice unchaste acts with women. For if there were anything to it, one would see that at times children would be born from such works of the Devil, which we have never heard of nor seen. Moreover, the devils would practice such filthy lusts much more among themselves than with women, if it were possible.

Now, if I grant that the Devil, by the permission of God, may practice such assumed acts with humans, it is in no way to be believed that he can impregnate a woman, or that she may conceive and bear children from him into the world. For never has any person been found in this world who was conceived without human seed from a spirit and born of a woman, except alone our LORD and Savior Jesus Christ, who was conceived by the Holy Spirit and born of Mary the holy Virgin.

# Paul Frisius

However, Vincent of Beauvais <note>original: "Vincentius"</note> in the 21st book of his *Historical Mirror* <note>original: "Historialis Speculi," a famous medieval encyclopedia</note>, Chapter 30, raises an objection here and says that King Vortigern once undertook to build a mighty tower, but the foundation always collapsed and sank. Finally, he was advised that he should seek a person who was conceived without human seed; such a person would show him how to set and lay the foundation so that it might endure. Thus, one was found in the kingdom named Merlin. He was brought before the King with his mother, and there the mother said how she had conceived this her son Merlin from a spirit and brought him into the world.

Likewise, Erasmus Sarcerius <note>A Lutheran theologian (1501–1559)</note> writes in his *Commonplaces* <note>original: "locis communibus"</note> concerning evil spirits, that in Dresden in Meissen a sorceress was burned who freely and openly confessed that she had conceived and given birth to two daughters by the Devil, who were still alive at that same time, in the year 1546.

To this I answer simply and plainly: that both this Merlin and also the two daughters from Dresden were not conceived by the Devil. For what is born of spirit is spirit, and a pure, earthly human being cannot have his essence from a spirit as a father. Rather, it certainly happened in this way:

After the mother of Merlin and the sorceress of Dresden surrendered themselves to the Devil and consented to him in all his affairs—as all desperate women and witches do who are vowed and promised to the Devil—the Devil, at night in sleep, instilled and cast such a strong imagination with fantasies into their minds. Through this, their senses were so seized and overcome that they believed nothing else than that he had lain with them, because in sleep they felt every appearance of lust. Afterward, when they believed nothing else than that he had been with them, he used his art, his deception, his trickery, and illusion <note>original: "præstigium"</note> to bloat their bodies

<column-break/>

with air and breath, or other things, so that they imagined they were pregnant. And when finally the time of birth arrived, God—on account of their unbelief—permitted and allowed him to cause them pain in the body and start a rumbling within. He drove out the wind and the breath that they had within them, and quickly placed another child there in its stead—one he had perhaps stolen elsewhere beforehand—and secretly laid it under them. This child the mother, with her deceived senses, accepted and thus raised.

That such a thing is true—namely, that the Devil can thus distend and bloat the "whore-sack" <note>A derogatory contemporary term for the womb of a woman perceived as sinful</note> of a witch even if she carries no child—is witnessed by an example which occurred in Constance <note>original: "Costnitz"</note> on Lake Constance. There, a well-bred daughter named Magdalena served, and she surrendered herself to the Devil, who also practiced and exercised unchastity with her. Afterward, however, she was reminded of her gruesome sin by the preachers and other pious people and was brought to true repentance; she renounced the Devil and returned again to her Lord Christ. But the Devil left her no rest by day or night, but caused her pain in her body, so that midwives and other women were frequently sent for in the belief that she was about to give birth. She suffered such compulsion, anguish, and distress without ceasing, but it was only a "witch-cap" <note>original: "Hexelkappen," a deceptive trick or illusion</note> and a fraud of the Devil. For at all times, through such compulsion, she brought forth from her body nails, glass, wood, hair, flax, bone, stone, iron, and similar things; so much came from her that it was beyond counting. All those, young and old, who saw and visited her experienced this—all of which the Devil had put into her and used to torture her.

That the Devil is also accustomed to stealing the children of other people—those who are perhaps reckless and bless their children down into the Devil's name—of that there is also no doubt. For from this come...

# Concerning Witches and Monsters

...men call them **changelings** <note>original: "Wechselkinder"</note>, believing that the Devil has laid himself in the cradle in the form of a child and has taken the true little child away. He, however, lies in the cradle as a wretched child, eating and defecating much—as he is indeed a creature of filth—howling and causing such heartache to the poor parents, who believe it to be their own child. In former times, more was experienced of such phantoms than is now among us, where such things must retreat before the **Holy Gospel**; to God be praise, honor, and thanks.

At **Heßloch** near **Oderheim**, located in the **Gau** <note>A traditional German region or shire</note>, it happened at one time that a cellarer or a farm manager lived there who was secretly betrothed to his cook. Because they could not name themselves publicly—as he was a servant of the clergy <note>Likely referring to the restrictions on marriage for those in minor orders or church service</note>—they intended their cohabitation to be a marriage and wished to behave toward one another in no other way than as a married couple. And when they had a little child together, the Lord God visited them such that He punished them with a **changeling**. It would not grow; it would not gain weight; it howled day and night and ate a great deal.

Finally, the woman decided she would carry her child to **Neuhausen** to the **St. Cyriacus Wagon** <note>A local pilgrimage site where children were weighed against grain or offerings to seek healing</note> to have it weighed, and to give it water to drink from the **St. Cyriacus Spring**, so that it might get better. For at that time, it was a high belief that if one had a child weighed on the great Cyriacus Wagon at Neuhausen that would not thrive, it would certainly change within nine days, either toward life or toward death.

As she came near **Westhofen** into the **Klawer** <note>A local field or forest name</note> with the child—under which she carried it so that she panted and sweated, so heavy had it become for her—she encountered a **wandering scholar** <note>A "Fahrender Schüler," often depicted in folklore as a student of the occult or a clever trickster</note>. He said to her: "Oh, my lady, what kind of filth are you carrying there? It would be no wonder if he throttled you!" She answered that it was her dear child and would not thrive or gain weight, and therefore she wanted to have it weighed at Neuhausen. But he spoke: "It is not your child; rather, it is the **Devil incarnate**. Throw the rogue into the

<column-break/>

brook!" But as she would not, but instead insisted it was her child and kissed it, he spoke further: "Your child stands at home in the parlor chamber behind the chest in a new cradle; this is the Devil. Throw the filth into the brook!" This she did with weeping and howling, and immediately there was such a howling and murmuring under the bridge that goes over the brook there, as if it were a pack of wolves and bears. And when she came home, she found her true little child fresh and healthy in a new cradle. Without doubt, the **Lord God** preserved the little child during the time she suckled the wretched Devil, the changeling.

Three years ago, the following true history occurred: Near **Breslau** <note>Modern-day Wrocław, Poland</note> lived a notable nobleman who had much hay and aftermath <note>The second crop of grass in a season</note> to bring in during the summer. For this, his subjects had to perform forced labor <note>original: "frönen," referring to feudal labor obligations</note>. Among these, a woman who had recently given birth—having been in childbed scarcely eight days—was also called. When she saw that the **Junker** <note>A young nobleman or squire</note> insisted upon it and she could not resist, she took her child out with her, laid it on a little heap of grass, went from it, and attended to the haymaking.

When she had worked for a good while and went to her little child to suckle it, she looked at the child, cried out loudly, struck her hands together over her head, and lamented to everyone that this was not her child. It drew the milk from her so greedily and howled so inhumanly, which she was not used to from her child. Nevertheless, she kept it for several days; it behaved so improperly that it nearly ruined the good woman. She lamented this to the Junker, who said to her: "Woman, if it seems to you that this is not your child, then do this: carry it to the meadow where you laid the previous child, and strike it vigorously with a rod; then you shall see a wonder." The woman followed the Junker, went out, and struck the changeling with the rod so that it shrieked loudly. Then the Devil brought back her stolen child...
