That is: Equity is more than the teaching of all laws. And indeed, the ignorance of the evildoers should excuse them to some extent: because even God, in His judgment, does not punish the ignorant as harshly as those who know, Luke 12.

They were all settled in one village, where there must have been a particular lack of diligence and a carelessness in the disorder of church teaching. For if the parson had instructed his parishioners rightly and faithfully, as he should—firstly in common in the church, having the children recite the <term>Catechism</term> <note>A summary of Christian principles used for instruction.</note> to him there; and thereafter also being observant and investigating whether anyone was involved with sorcery, summoning them to him, warning them against it, and if they were stubborn, the <term>Schultheiß</term> <note>A village mayor or local magistrate.</note> then doing his part as well—then such people would be preserved for God, and so much firewood would be saved. Had the poor widows and orphans been assisted with several measures of corn and other necessities, they might perhaps not have fallen into such misfortune and misery.

But now, whenever such weeds appear, people want to root them out and cite the Law of Moses; but that the field should be so tilled and overseen that such weeds do not grow in it—there, one does not look at what Moses commanded and ordained in the land of the Jews. There was a measure of moderation and discretion in the law regarding the execution of sorcerers. When they behaved impenitently and stubbornly, and no ceasing or improvement was shown, then one proceeded with the punishment.

The ancient teachers of the Church advised the authorities against punishing even the gross heretics with death—those who stripped our Lord Christ of His divinity—who were nevertheless men, learned and witty; much more should one have patience with ignorant, foolish women: who, just as they are more easily led astray than men, are also more easily converted back. Did not Peter sin as grossly and horribly as any "witch" <note>original: "here" (Hexe)</note> who was a man? He was the most intimate and

<column-break/>

foremost disciple of the Lord, by whom he had been taught so long and so much, and had seen so many miracles: who presumed to go with Him into death, and yet denied Him not once, but three times, and with an oath? He was therefore not burned, nor, in my opinion, should he have been burned, even if he had been under a Christian authority. He was converted and became again the foremost Apostle of the Lord. Matters of faith and worldly matters are distinct. Had he become a defector from his sovereign and faithless to him, that would be another matter, and punishable in the body.

Had these women done nothing else, they might have been spared. Catherine was sorry for her sin; she loved her husband so much that she never wanted to do him harm, even though Satan provoked her to it and therefore burdened her all the more. The parson could also have converted the others and set them right again with special counsel and diligence. For once the poor, weak women have involved themselves with the Devil, they fear to abandon him again, lest he terrify them, or do them discomfort, harm, and grief. The oft-mentioned <term>Faust</term> <note>The legendary alchemist and sorcerer Johann Georg Faust.</note> once intended to convert; then the Devil threatened him so harshly, made him so anxious, and terrified him so, that he signed himself over to him anew. Therefore, one must give them courage, arm them well with faith and prayer, so that they may be comforted and undaunted, knowing he will be able to do nothing to them, will eventually grow weary of them, and leave them in peace. In addition, one should also come to their aid in their poverty, because that was a cause of such pitiful misfortune; for this purpose, a general alms should be established by the rulers in market towns and villages: and it should not only be sung in churches, "You shall open your gentle hand to the poor in your land," but it should also happen thus in deed and in work.

That they traveled to the dance on brooms, pitchforks, or little brown horses is a false delusion, both among themselves

those who understand it, as among others who believe it. For how is it believable and possible that they travel and dance in such a way? No broom, no fork flies through the air, no matter how they are greased <note>Refers to "flying ointment," which skeptics like the author believed caused hallucinations rather than actual flight</note>. Wherever one places them, there they remain; they do not move. If the Devil then carries the witches, why would he need the broom or the fork to carry them as well, so that he has an even heavier burden—especially since they are not shaped in such a way that one can sit upon them? Furthermore, if the aforementioned witches traveled in this way by day, while their husbands were in the woods and vineyards, how could it happen that no one in the village, nor out in the field, saw them flying through the air, or saw them traveling or riding on the earth through dry and wet, through thick and thin, as they confess?

The cunning rogue <note>The Devil</note> came to them in their houses in the absence of their husbands to strengthen them in the opinion of traveling away, as if the husbands would otherwise see it: yet they traveled nowhere, but only slept and dreamed at home. Like that musician who, being drunk in the evening, went from the small town of N. to the nearest village and lay down under a tree. From there the Devil took him, as it seemed to him, and led him back into the town to the tavern, where he played the fiddle for the witches to dance for a reward. Afterward, the Devil placed him back under the tree where he had taken him. It was a dream. In taverns, where there are so many servants and guests, where people go to sleep late and rise early, one cannot dance secretly without anyone noticing or waking up from the noise and commotion. The poor wretch was later taken into custody as a sorcerer and confessed under torture that he had also stolen—which was not true—because he would rather be hanged than burned: and he was hanged.

The two witches who went to the bath together saw a witches' dance by the path in the field. How did it happen that other people passing by did not also see it? It was a fantasy and an imagination: just as when a

<column-break/>

sick person lies in a delirium <note>original: "aberwiz"</note> and thinks a tall black man is standing before the bed, and tells people to drive him away, yet others see nothing there and nothing is there. Yes, indeed, dancing! Poor, languishing, hardworking, weary women have no desire to dance: carrying wood out of the forest, carrying manure into the vineyard, and other heavy labor drives away their lust and extravagance and makes them so tired that they must rest and sleep at night; they do not desire to dance even at home on a level threshing floor or paneled floor, let alone out on a watery meadow or an uneven field in the wind, rain, and frost. Good days and plenty make dancers. "Before eating there is no dancing," says the proverb; and, "On a full stomach stands a happy head." Thus, whoever thinks they hold banquets, eating and drinking there, has already been answered: they do not go there. And even if they did go there and sat at a full table, it would still be a fantasy and a ghost: they would travel away as hungry as they had come. Had the judges inspected the dance floors of the witches the very next day after the dances were held, they would have noticed no footprints, nor any little blade of grass trodden down. It is a wonder that there are people who believe this: let alone that even prominent people, judges, and rulers hold it for truth, and pass judgment and punishment based upon it.

Regarding the carnal intercourse <note>original: "Bulschafft"</note> with the Devil, it was said before that it is a deception and a delusion in feeling or touch: or that he sometimes takes a dead body upon himself and joins himself to the woman with it. Therefore it is a cold, unlovely cohabitation, which they have suffered from him without pleasure, out of compulsion.

They did not make the weather: their pot and their cooking <note>Refers to the belief that witches brewed storms in cauldrons</note> contributed nothing to it. The rime and frost that ruined the grain and wine would have come regardless, even if they had not performed their foolish work. What should these powerless women be capable of in such great matters, who could not even bring home a sprig of wood unless they went into the forest themselves to fetch it?

# Heinrich Bullinger

Regarding their confession about bewitching people and livestock to sickness and death, one should have investigated and considered whether it happened through poison, hewing, stabbing, throwing, or striking, as Catharina did to the dog. <note>Referring to a specific case where physical violence was used rather than "magic."</note> Beyond that, nothing was done by them, but rather by the Devil. For words and stroking one's hand over an animal—provided it is not poisoned—does not harm it and it does not die from it. And even if she used herbal salves or powders, intending to cause harm with them, one should consult physicians or others knowledgeable in nature <note>term: Naturkündigern (natural philosophers or scientists)</note> to see whether such things have such power or not. One should take one's time and not hurry to kill people: he who lives can be killed at any time, but he who is dead can never be made living again. Otherwise, witches cannot rightfully be further accused and punished, except for having had the *will* to do such things. If some harm later befalls the animal, the Devil does it, or it otherwise happens according to the common course of nature. When Catharina stroked the horse's back with her hand in the Devil's name, that was not the cause of its death; it would have died without that. When Satan noticed that this would happen, he led her to it, so that she believed she must have done it. And people's livestock die all the more, the more strongly they believe that witches are doing it to them, when it is actually the Devil doing it; and they do not look to God, nor pray to Him, that He might preserve them from misfortune and harm.

Since, then, the will was present without the deed, the authorities are not accustomed to punish it, as mentioned above: before God it counts as much as the deed, for He has reserved such punishment for Himself. If one person wishes death upon another, or throws at, shoots, stabs, or strikes at him and misses—even if he would have killed him had he hit him—he is not condemned as a murderer because of it. Likewise, if someone pursues adultery but does not complete it, he is not punished as an adulterer for it.

Previously, mention was made of two squires in the Emperor's court who were mortal enemies, and one was stabbed in his bed at night, and the other dreamed that he did it. This man

<column-break/>

was not killed as a murderer because of it, but was nevertheless punished to some extent because of his violent will and the coincidence that the deed matched the dream and that his sword was bloody. Thus: they placed him before the court and dug out the earth next to him as far as the shadow of his body extended, and banished him from the land. <note>A symbolic legal punishment where the "shadow" is punished when the physical crime cannot be proven.</note> Just as this man had not stabbed the other, but rather the Devil did, so the fifth witch did not smother her adversary, even though she confessed to it, since she was not present and did not touch him. The courtier's dream was not as strong and vivid as her dream, otherwise he would also have confessed to the deed as she did. Therefore, one should kill the woman as little as him, because she did it just as little—indeed, even less—than he did. The courtier was certainly murdered by the Devil; or, when it happened, he may have otherwise suffocated in his sleep, as happens to many without the Devil's doing and working; and when it happened, the Devil put it into the woman's mind in a dream that she had done it. And even if such a woman kills a horse, child, sheep, or dog, is it then not enough that she pays for it and is otherwise punished for her wantonness and outrage, but not with her life? A human and a beast are an unequal compensation. <note>Bullinger argues that the "eye for an eye" principle shouldn't apply to animal death by execution of a human.</note>

In the imagined and dreamed dances <note>Referring to the Witches' Sabbath</note>, each of them recognizes two or three others, so that one may report and denounce the others when they are imprisoned. Satan is so clever and swift—as much, or even more so—to bring innocent people as well as guilty ones into suffering and to their deaths.

Their madness and insanity can be understood from the fact that they desired to ruin corn and other fruits; yet they already suffered a lack of bread and other necessities. They would have only increased this lack for themselves and their children, which no rational person does. It is the act of an insane person to kill his own sheep because it comes home late: as if a sheep were not a sheep, but a human being.

That the Devil advised and threatened Catharina in prison that she should recant, or he would let a vein in her toe <note>original: "Ader auff der zehe lassen" - likely referring to bloodletting or a ritual mark</note>, otherwise he would strangle her: that happened because

# Reflections on Sorcery

the villain <note>The Devil</note> noticed this in her and feared that, through the exhortation and persistence of the minister, she might turn back to God before the court and during the execution. For if she had opened a vein—for which he undoubtedly brought her a knife or an awl—her blood would have run out until she died. He did the same to a sailor who complained of it to me. When that man had lost his ship and goods at sea and could not sleep at night for worry, someone came before his bed and said: "You have bad blood in you; take the knife and open a vein in your neck, then you will feel better." Had that happened, he would have bled to death from the opened vein; or the murderous spirit would have pressed the knife all the way in and through his throat once he set it there.

Why <margin>b</margin> did he then bring her into prison if he suspected she would fall away from him? Even if he perhaps sensed such a thing in her beforehand, he is sometimes so reckless and hasty to bring people into suffering that he overreaches, and things turn out differently and better than he intended. Then he wishes he had left it alone. Thus he drove Judas to betray and deliver his Master, our LORD and Savior; but soon after, when he saw where it was leading—that the redemption of the human race would result from it—he regretted it and would have liked to set Him free again. He beset Pilate's wife in her sleep at night so that she might influence her husband. He is often an inconstant, contrary spirit, as all evil men are; he sometimes entangles himself in affairs so that he does not know the way out.

As for those among these witches who, as I hear happened, called out to the Devil while in the fire: the liar and murderer had persuaded them and promised them in prison that they should hold fast to him until the fire; when that began, he would be there to rescue them.

Finally, in these testimonies or confessions, it is also to be noted that, as was said at the beginning, the air is everywhere full

<column-break/>

of devils, who found their way to these women in the woods, in the fields, and in the house. When Catharin called to the Devil on the road, he was there immediately.

It has also been commonly said of this trial: when the witches refused to confess their misdeeds under torture, a famous sorcerer <note>term: *Zauberer* - here referring to a professional "cunning man" or male magician hired by the court</note> was summoned from many miles away for a great reward. He supposedly placed a herb in their laps, whereupon they confessed everything willingly and readily. If that is true, then it is a gross and abominable sin before God that one punishes sorcery with sorcery, uses the Devil to carry out the judgment, and honors his servant and bond-slave with money. In the eyes of the world, it is an unjust and perverted business that women—the small, weak witches—are put into the fire, while the man—the great, powerful sorcerer—is not only left unpunished but is also handsomely rewarded. In him dwelt a devil so much more masterful and powerful than in them, that their devils had to obey him or willingly gave way to him. For they play and "shadow-fence" <note>original: *spiegelfechten* - a deceptive or sham fight</note> with one another to the destruction of mankind. The rogue should have been burned first, if it is right for witches to be burned at all. If justice was done to them, then a great injustice was done to him, and the Law of Moses, as well as the Imperial Law, was overlooked here.

The burning of the aforementioned witches caused me to write down these reflections and reminders regarding the business of sorcery and witches; I felt pity for them when I heard from those who were present and had watched the pitiful spectacle. If this compassion seems like foolishness or a rarity to anyone, I leave him to his multifaceted wisdom. But let him see to it "that he is not too wise, just as I am too foolish." I would rather be too merciful than "too harsh, especially in such a confused, erroneous, and incomprehensible matter." Yet many highly intelligent, learned, and unlearned men confirm and reassure me in this opinion of mine; they feel displeasure and horror at these severe "Devil's burnt offerings" <margin>Devil's burnt offerings.</margin> and desire a remedy, and...

### The 12th Little Treatise

# Against the Black Arts,
### Superstitious Blessing, Untruthful Soothsaying, and
### other such arts forbidden by God: a short treatise collected from Holy Scripture and true, good reasons by
### Heinrich Bullinger. <insert>In the year 1571.</insert>

<margin>
Paul's preaching of the Kingdom of God.
</margin>

Against the forbidden and Black Arts, from the 19th chapter of the Acts of the Holy Apostles.

When the Holy Apostle Paul came to Ephesus, he preached about the Kingdom of God, namely how men are redeemed from the kingdom of the Devil and of darkness into the Kingdom of Christ here in time, and after this time may depart into the Kingdom of God through Jesus Christ our Lord; whereby the Kingdom of Christ in Ephesus and all around it increased greatly. For the people abandoned idolatry, clinging alone to the true faith in Christ Jesus, and also desisted from all kinds of vice, and committed themselves to serving God in all righteousness and virtue; for they were greatly moved

<column-break/>

by the great wonders and signs which God worked through the ministry of Paul, so that even those possessed by evil spirits were delivered through the name of Jesus Christ.

<margin>
The Devil's envy and hatred.
</margin>

Such things vexed the Devil greatly, and he undertook to make the wonders and signs that happened through Paul in the name of Jesus Christ suspicious, whereby he might also eventually destroy Paul's preaching and open and maintain his own kingdom; for he stirred up his servants, seven of whom were sons of a prominent priest, Jews and exorcists <note>original: "Teuffels bschworer," literally "devil-swearers" or conjurers</note> who were held in high regard as those who until then had driven out the Devil through black arts and worked all kinds of wonders. These same men also undertook to deliver possessed people in the name of Jesus; had this succeeded, he [the Devil] could easily have made Paul's teaching suspicious, as if it also happened through Black Arts—just as the signs of our Lord Jesus Christ in the Gospel <note>original: "Euangelio"</note> were also slandered.

The devil Matthew 12.
</margin>

# Concerning Witches and Sorcerers.

the Gospel, which the Pharisees gladly would have portrayed as if it were performed through the power of Beelzebub <note>A prince of demons; the Pharisees accused Jesus of using his power in Matthew 12:24</note>; and with similar knavery, Porphyry, Julian, and apostate enemies of the Christian faith slandered the teachings and signs of the Apostles, as if they were empowered and brought about through the black arts.

<margin>The Devil is put to shame.</margin>
But the power of GOD here at Ephesus put to shame not only the practitioners of the black arts, but the Devil himself, through a new and wondrously great sign, and brought all black arts to light, showing that they are vain and accursed. For the Devil was so subdued by God that he himself had to stand against his own friends and servants, defiling them, harming them, and bringing them to great shame before all the world. For when they undertook to release a possessed man, to whom they said: "We adjure you by the Name of Jesus Christ, whom Paul preaches," the Devil within the possessed man contradicted them and spoke: "Jesus I know well, and I know well who Paul is, but who are you?" As if he wished to say: "Why do you lay claim to the Son of God and his holy servant Paul, you who are nothing but desolate rogues and deceivers of the people?"—which is indeed the correct <term>predicate</term> <note>A formal logical term meaning a defining characteristic</note> for such a worthless lot. And herewith he fell upon their heads, tore them down, defiled them harshly, and overpowered them, so that they escaped from the house in which they wished to practice their adventures, naked and wounded; truly naked, for GOD had herewith uncovered and revealed them to all the world, showing that their art was falsehood and knavery. They escaped wounded, for that is the rightful reward—namely harm and ruin, wounding and killing—with which the Devil finally and certainly pays all his servants.

<margin>Forbidden arts rejected.</margin>
And this history indicates to us that the black arts and all forbidden arts displease GOD, and moreover deceive and ruin mankind; therefore everyone should abstain from them. As follows hereafter in the Acts of the Holy Apostles, others at Ephesus who had also dealt with the Devil and forbidden arts brought forth their books of forbidden

<column-break/>

arts and burned them with fire. By this, all the world learns that one should do the same in similar cases, and put away all things related to these arts, so that one not only refrains from using them, but if they are being used or found—whether there are still practitioners of the black arts—no one should go to them, ask them for advice, or make use of their arts. And here it is practical and necessary to speak somewhat more extensively of such forbidden arts. For people are still found who either still deal in them, or else run after those who use them and have faith in them—to see if perhaps these people might be helped, if they are willing to let themselves be advised and aided in another way.

<margin>Why these arts are being discussed.</margin>
The evil enemy brought his art into the world right from the beginning, but in opposition, God has forbidden and rejected them from the beginning, and has always had his servants faithfully report to the world that when a person is in distress, he should nowhere turn to the Devil or his arts, but to God alone, and ask Him for grace, counsel, and help. Likewise, he may seek the counsel and comfort of physicians and other sensible people; but where no help is to be found or expected, one should nevertheless bear the hand of God patiently, and never undertake to tear oneself out of the Cross that God lays upon us through the Devil's help and forbidden arts. For one finds very loose, godless people who are not ashamed to speak openly: "He who is sick would gladly be healthy; if the Devil could help me, why should I care who did it? Why should I reject it?" This is a wicked, gruesome, and abominable—indeed, a devil-possessed—way of speaking, which should never be heard among Christians. There are, however, many kinds of forbidden arts: <term>Magia</term> <note>Magic</note>, <term>Mathematica</term> <note>Here referring to astrology or numerology</note>, and <term>Venefica</term> <note>Sorcery or poisoning</note>, <term>Divinatio</term> <note>Divination</note>, <term>Incantatio</term> <note>Incantations/Spells</note>, <term>Augurium</term> <note>Augury/Omens</note>, <term>Auspicia</term> <note>Auspices/Bird-watching</note>, <term>Geomantia</term> <note>Geomancy/Earth-divination</note>, <term>Necromantia</term> <note>Necromancy/Communicating with the dead</note>, <term>Hydromantia</term> <note>Hydromancy/Water-divination</note>, <term>Pyromantia</term> <note>Pyromancy/Fire-divination</note>, and many more of the Devil's works. I will not speak of all of them here, but only of certain superstitious and forbidden pieces as a warning, as much as God gives grace; and they are all named...

<meta>This page continues Heinrich Bullinger’s discourse on spiritual and social conduct, specifically transitioning into a critique of superstitious practices versus true Christian blessing.</meta>

# Heinrich Bullinger

Black art—that is, art forbidden by God, unrighteous, and the Devil’s art—is that which the "Black Man" <note>A common historical euphemism for the Devil.</note> usually enjoys. Among these arts, one is worse than the other, and yet none of them are good.

<margin>I. Blessing.</margin>
First, common among the world is "blessing" <note>original: "segnen"; here referring to charms or folk-healing spells.</note>, with which some bless people and livestock; sometimes it helps, and sometimes it does not. However, not all blessing is evil or forbidden. For God ordained in His Law, in the 6th chapter of Numbers, that the priests should commonly and publicly speak this blessing or benediction over the people: "The Lord bless you and keep you; the Lord make His face shine upon you and give you peace." To this, God adds that they shall "put my Name upon the children of Israel"—that is, only in my Name, and not under any other names, shall they bless the people, or speak good over them, and wish them health, so that I may bless them. For it is not because of the spoken words—as if the words had a hidden power within them—that the desired and spoken thing shall happen to them; rather, the LORD will bless them. That is, He grants that the words spoken by the priest sound forth and proclaim; for the words themselves can do nothing, nor have they any other power than to proclaim, signify, and indicate that the power and effect belong to GOD alone. In the New Testament, the holy Apostles clearly proclaimed with their words and speech only that which GOD alone grants and gives, and they wrote and spoke: "Grace, peace, and mercy from GOD our Father and the LORD Jesus Christ be with you." This blessing is still spoken rightly and fruitfully by the ministers of the Church at the beginning of sermons in all churches; for that which is spoken there by the ministers is graciously imparted by GOD to the believers, not through the power of the words, but through God’s power.

<margin>Blessing the children.</margin>
And just as there has always been a general church blessing, so too was there a special blessing among the ancient patriarchs who blessed their children, to whom GOD granted the good that was spoken over them by their fathers—not

<column-break/>

through the power of the words, but in the power and out of the grace of God. In the same way, parents should still bless their children—that is, speak good over them and commend them to God, so that He may protect and bless them in soul and body.

<margin>Superstitious blessings.</margin>
However, it is an open error when you say to your children or others, "Now may GOD protect you" (for every Christian person may commend another to blessing and departing grace, that is, the grace of GOD) "and the holy Cross." If you then understand the Cross not as the wood, but as Paul does in the first chapter of 1 Corinthians—the death and suffering of Christ—then that is right. But it is wrong when you say: "Now may God and Our Dear Lady <note>A reference to the Virgin Mary, which Bullinger, as a Protestant Reformer, views as superstitious when placed on par with God.</note> protect you." For thus it is written in the twenty-eighth chapter of Isaiah: whoever blesses himself on earth (in Christendom) shall bless himself in the true GOD, and whoever swears on earth shall swear by the true GOD. But it is very evil when parents give their children to the Devil or curse them, or when one person does so to another—though there is no room to speak further of that here—and when they say that the blessing of people and livestock (such as is used for blessing wounds and eyes, or blessing "the worm" <note>A historical term for various internal parasites or localized infections believed to be caused by "worms."</note> and other diseases) is righteous; it is unrighteous and serves among the forbidden arts. Likewise, writing blessings on scraps of paper and hanging them around the neck—I am not speaking now of herbs and spices, nor of natural medicine. But where one uses specific words, strange and barbaric words, crosses oneself, or makes and paints little crosses, uses characters <note>term: characters <gloss>occult symbols or sigils</gloss></note>, and then attributes to the spoken blessing, words, and characters that health will be given for their sake—that is idolatry and the Devil’s work, and belongs among the Black Arts. For the argument made here—that the "blesser" uses prayer for it—is a falsehood and a deception. You can understand this by asking: "If I otherwise pray to GOD without such customs and blessings, does the prayer still help?" They answer: "No." For you must have the blessing over you, along with that which—

Nor is this blessing right simply because it sometimes helps, or heals people and livestock, of which more will follow hereafter.

<margin>II. Conjuring.</margin>
Accordingly, there are also Conjurers <term>Exorcistæ; those who attempt to expel spirits through ritual commands</term>, of whom much is still found among the ancients regarding exorcisms, about which others have written—such as Peter Martyr in the 8th chapter of the 1st book of Kings, folio 72b—and others have disputed. Indeed, there was a gift and grace in the ancient Church whereby evil enemies were driven out of the possessed; however, these, like the gift of tongues and other graces, have ceased. Christ himself drove out the evil enemy with a command and order, as the rightful Lord, and the Apostles and first believers also drove them out, but in the name of Jesus Christ; they neither used nor left behind any "Exorcisms" <note>ritual formulas</note> for us to use. Therefore, everything that the Papists <note>a derogatory term for Roman Catholics</note> do with their conjuring of the possessed at Luffen by St. Anstett and elsewhere is without foundation in God's Word and belongs under superstition and forbidden arts. It is also in itself so ridiculous and absurd that the foolish custom of conjuring refutes itself. For what is it but this: that they place the possessed person naked in a bath of cold water, choke him with the stole <note>a liturgical vestment</note>, sprinkle him with holy water, lash him with rods, cover or clothe him with the chasuble or mass-garment, and use many other buffooneries, of which I will say no more here.

<margin>How one may and should deal with deaf or possessed people.</margin>
But to those who ask: "What if my people are so raging that it is in doubt whether they are deaf or possessed? May I then not have them conjured?" To them, the Truth answers: No, and not at all. "What shall I do then?" Do that which you have learned in the Gospel: those who had possessed people hurried to Christ, led them to Him, and asked Him for help. Do that also. "Yes, but He is no longer on Earth, therefore I can no longer come to Him?" Answer: He is, however, in His Church; go to it and desire the common prayer (of the Church to Christ), use medicine, guard the sick person well so that he may harm neither himself nor other people, and thus wait for the grace of GOD. Yet there is another kind of devil-conjuring where he is not driven out, but rather binds himself to the conjurer. For the thousand-fold Devil allows himself to be forced and bound by the conjurer with high-sounding delusions and strange words and incantations, so that he stands ready to serve the devil-conjurer's hand and will, and to carry out what he is commanded. And while the conjurer thinks and imagines he has the Devil in his service and power, the Devil blinds his conjurer for a time—whom he rules far more than he is ruled—since he has him according to his will, fenced off in his kingdom away from the Kingdom of GOD, and finally leads him into the abyss of Hell. Such serving spirits, however, they are accustomed to call <term>paredros</term> <note>Greek: "sitting beside"; assistant spirits</note> and <term>familiares spiritus</term> <note>Latin: "familiar spirits"</note>; some call them the "devil in the glass" or in the vial, also <term>Pythonem</term> <note>a spirit of divination</note> and a soothsaying spirit, as follows hereafter. All this is dearly forbidden by GOD as the Devil's work and a loathsome, great sin, which should also be punished in a person's life, as will also follow to some extent hereafter.

<column-break/>

<margin>III. Planetary powers.</margin>
Furthermore, there are many <term>Magi mathematici</term> <note>astrologers or "mathematical magicians"</note>, stargazers, planet-preachers, and day-choosers, who undertake not only to predict future things from the stars and the course of the stars, but also to subject man—with body and soul and all his goods—to the stars in such a way that they work powerfully within them. For those born under the planet Venus must be lechers; those under Mars must quarrel and wage war; those under Saturn must steal. They also say that certain days are rejected, and that this and that is...

By this, people are led astray into superstition and anxiety, forgetting God’s governance and His ordering of all things, and directing all their actions and omissions toward the stars, the signs, and the planets, dealing in sheer idolatry and paganism. There are also many who wish to excuse their sins and shame in a shameful and unchristian manner by saying: "I must surely whore and commit adultery, for I am a child of Venus." <note>A reference to the astrological belief that being born under the planet Venus compels one toward lust.</note> Indeed, you are much more a child of the Devil, blinded by the forbidden art of star-judging. God has not given such power to the stars; the astrologers lie and deceive regarding them. For the Scripture reads thus: *That they may distinguish between day and night, and be for signs and set times, for days and years.* <note>original: "Ut distinguant inter diem & noctem, sintque in signa & stata tempora, in dies & annos." A translation of Genesis 1:14.</note> The same Scripture also witnesses that Esau and Jacob were born under one planet, and many thousands of people are still born under one horoscope who nevertheless have different natures. And although in the waxing and waning month, in the ebbing and increasing moon, one sows different things that should grow downward or upward, and fells wood at a specific time, the planets or the stars do not work upon the soul, honor, body, or property of man. Believing people know that they are subject to the ordinance of God; they look to God in all their actions and omissions, and not at all to the signs and astrologers, which are clearly and entirely rejected in the word of God. Isaiah 47, Jeremiah 10, Micah 5, and elsewhere. Thus, the ancient teachers also unanimously rejected astrology <term>Astrologiam: the practice of predicting the future via stars</term>, even though they did recognize astronomy <term>Astronomiam: the scientific study of celestial bodies</term> to some extent.

<margin>IV. Questioning the souls of the deceased.</margin>
Among the forbidden arts, it must especially be counted that some raise the deceased—as they imagine—from the dead, and then ask them about their concerns or desire information. As Saul, the King of Israel, commanded the witch at Endor to wake Samuel. But that is a pure deception of the Devil, who can transform himself into the form of an angel, as Paul says—not to mention into the form of a human and the deceased. But our true faith never permits that souls, after their departure from the body, may be dragged here and there by the Devil from those places where they are judged by God. *The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God* <note>original: "Iustorum animæ sunt in manu DEI." From Wisdom of Solomon 3:1.</note>, as the Scripture says; the damned souls are not allowed back out to us, as the Lord Himself witnesses in Luke 16. And upon such a "pretty" foundation many have based their fables—the Papists with their apparitions and revelations of souls—clearly against the Word of God, which plainly commands that we should not search for or ask the truth from spirits or the deceased.

<column-break/>

<margin>V. Soothsaying.</margin>
Likewise is *Divinatio* or *Spiritus Pythonis* <note>original: "Spiritus Pythonis" refers to a spirit of divination or a "pythonic spirit," referencing the Oracle of Delphi.</note>, soothsaying and the revealing of secrets, also a species of the Black Art, where the "Lauchßner" <note>An archaic term for a diviner or one who listens/spies out secrets.</note> or soothsayer undertakes to open hidden things through a crystal or other devilish inspirations and instruments. For instance, if someone has lost something that was stolen from him, he visits the conjurer and asks who the thief might be. The practitioner of the Black Art, through his art and the revelation of the Devil, either depicts the thief with signs so that one may suspect who he is, or says the stolen item will soon be returned—where it sometimes happens by chance, but on the other hand, it fails many times, grossly and frequently. Thus the Devil sets people against one another, and it has often been found that he has accused honorable and innocent people. And it is indeed a great abomination and a conscious insanity that a human is so blinded that he seeks the truth from him of whom the Mouth of Truth speaks, saying he was a liar from the beginning, the father and author of all lies. You would not believe any man who has the reputation of being a liar, yet you believe the Devil, who is the lie itself. And when he occasionally tells a truth, he tells it so that he may lead you astray in other ways all the better and more grossly with lies and all kinds of deceit, and keep you in his kingdom.

# Concerning Witches and Sorcerers

<margin>VI. Sorcerers and Witches.</margin>
Now follow the *Malefici* and *Maleficæ* <note>Latin: malevolent practitioners or evildoers</note>, the true master black-magicians, whom people call sorcerers and sorceresses or witches. Sorcerers are those who are equal to witches in the main business, for they are also called "master-lords" and make alliances and understandings with the Devil, signing themselves over to him, withdrawing from God and the true faith, so that through the help of the Devil they may work wonders, help, and cause harm. Of this kind were those of whom the Scripture speaks here and there, calling them *Magos* <note>Latin: Magi or magicians</note>, such as the *Magi Pharaonis* <note>Latin: Pharaoh’s magicians</note>, Simon Magus, and others of that sort; and in our own times, Faustus the black-magician was such a one. These are also for the most part *divini* <note>Latin: diviners</note> or soothsayers, and are defiled and stinking with other such "devil’s-dung." Those among women who are like this are called sorceresses and witches, like the one at Endor, and many like her, whom King Saul—while he was still of right mind—ordered to be judged and put to death. They also deny God and the true faith, pledge themselves to the Devil, and after the denial of Holy Baptism, receive a bite or a mark on their body from the Devil, who plays wondrous games here with them, marries them, holds weddings, feasts, and dances, sleeps with them, and carries out many abominations too gruesome to mention. They also, through his help, damage the fruits in the field, as well as people and livestock. This is found to be true manifold in deed and experience. It is found, however, for the most part, that witches are caused and driven to such a gruesome alliance with the Devil—as they themselves confess—through poverty, envy and hatred, or a desire for revenge, whereby they give the Devil the occasion to tempt and acknowledge them. For he appears to them in a magnificent form and holds out the hope that if they surrender to him, he will let them lack for nothing and give them great power for revenge; so that they believe him, as Eve believed the serpent, he catches them: but afterward he keeps nothing of his word. For they are always poor and miserable. And even when he occasionally gives them something, it is nothing at all, and vanishes again from under their hands. Likewise, he cannot help them with revenge at all times as they desire.

<column-break/>

<margin>Whether sorcerers possess any power.</margin>
Here, however, it is asked whether sorcerers, black-magicians, and witches possess any power over the things that are thought to be done by them? For many wish to consider it a delusion, a vain imagination and fantasy, and that they have power neither over the weather, nor over people and livestock. Against this, however, experience and Holy Scripture testify that they have an effect on the things they do, and everyone sees and finds that it is not a delusion, but truly happens, what they do: concerning this, see the 2nd Book of Moses <note>Exodus</note> in the 7th Chapter. How the magicians of Pharaoh worked many signs in deed, which Moses and Aaron had previously done through God's power. Yet they were always put to shame by the Divine signs. For the serpent of Moses ate up the serpents of the magicians. See also the 28th Chapter of 1 Samuel, where you will be informed how the witch awakened Samuel for Saul. And although that which was awakened by the witch was not the true and Holy Samuel, it was nevertheless a visible, substantial form of Samuel, so that the godless Saul thought no differently than that it was the true Samuel; just as even now, through black arts, the deceased are called and conjured for conversation, who truly are not the deceased, yet also not a delusion, but a being like the deceased, and a deception of the Devil. See further in the Acts of the Apostles in the 8th Chapter, and you will find how Simon the Sorcerer for a long time bewitched the citizens of the city of Samaria, that is, fooled and deceived them with sorcery, who was also driven away by Divine truth, and his art of sorcery was revealed and put to shame.

<margin>From whence comes the power of sorcerers.</margin>
Here one asks again, however, from whom and from whence comes the power with which sorcerers and sorceresses work? Answer: From the Devil and from

from the Devil’s cunning. Yet not all of it comes from him, as if he possessed such power of his own accord, but rather from the providence and permission of God, who allows such things for certain reasons and out of His righteous Judgment, using the Devil as His executioner or the fulfiller of His decrees. The Devil, however, employs for this purpose those who are of his household: sorcerers, witches, and other godless, abominable, desperate, and cursed people.

You may see all of this as if in a mirror in the history of Job, whom God wished to test; for this reason, He permitted the Devil to harm him in his house, children, and goods, though he was not to touch or harm his body. Therefore, the Devil went forth and stirred up a terrible storm, with which he overturned the house where Job’s children were, killing them all. He also moved the warriors of the Chaldeans, who made a raid, slew Job’s servants, and moreover robbed and drove away all his cattle and possessions. Now, when you compare all of this to the works of sorcerers and witches—how they harm people and livestock—you see and understand how it comes to pass.

<margin>Why God permits this.</margin> But if you ask in turn: why does God permit so much to the Devil and, through him, to evil people? And why does He allow them to work such things? Answer: The judgments of God are true and righteous, but also unsearchable <note>original: "vnersorschlich" - beyond human comprehension</note>. Yet He also informs us of several reasons for this permission, or His allowing and letting happen, that they may do such things. Firstly, He wishes thereby to test His own people, to see whether—when they witness such things—they will stand firm in God, His Word, and Faith, and allow themselves to be turned away from Him by nothing. For thus it is written in Deuteronomy, in the thirteenth chapter: "If a prophet or a dreamer <note>Bullinger adds: understand by this all sorts of charlatans and Devil’s-spawn</note> arises among you and gives a sign or a wonder, and the sign or wonder of which he spoke comes to pass, and he says: 'Let us follow other gods,' then you shall not listen to the words of such a dreamer. For the Lord your God is testing you, to find out whether you love Him with all your heart," etc. Look up that place yourself in the indicated thirteenth chapter. Furthermore, since God has given us a perfect teaching—that we should serve God alone and trust fully that He can and will protect us from all evil, for which reason we should call upon Him—and has given us enough signs in His Word to witness and confirm this to us; yet people are found who do not seek God and are superstitious. God punishes them and their unbelief through false-believing people of the Devil. For thus it is written: that the Devil has influence with all kinds of lying powers, signs, and wonders, and with all kinds of deceptions, etc. So that all those may be judged who did not love the truth nor believe it, but took pleasure in unrighteousness. See for yourself the words of Paul in 2 Thessalonians, chapter 2.

<column-break/>

But if you say that enchantment <note>term: "verzauberung" - refers to being bewitched or under a magical spell</note> also happens to pious, God-fearing people, then I say to that: it happens to them as it did to Job, for their testing; he was miserably injured by the Devil, by God’s permission, not only in his goods but also in his body.

<margin>Believing people are also enchanted.</margin>

<margin>Young children enchanted.</margin> But what, you ask, have the little children been accused of, that they are enchanted and ruined for their parents? Why does God permit such a thing? Answer: The same God who had the power to take away the dear children of His beloved servant Job, and to let them be destroyed by the violent storm stirred up by the Devil, still has power over all the children of this world. He may well take them away as He wills and through whom He wills; and He can also give them that which is better and deliver them from evil, so that no injustice or violence is done to them, and we have no cause to complain against God. Moreover, when parents see great need, misery, and wretchedness in their children, they learn through the contemplation of their sins how they might be visited by God with all kinds of punishments. For here it is necessary to judge—

<margin>The true basis of this matter.</margin>
In summary, GOD our God and Father is the LORD, the Sovereign and Ruler of all affairs, visible and invisible. He guides and sustains mankind in His Almighty government, providence, and ordinance. Here, the Devil has no power at all over mankind, nor can he inflict any harm—whether to soul, honor, body, or property—unless he first has permission from God. As seen in the Holy Gospel, without permission he has no power even over the unclean Gadarene swine. How much more glorious and worthy is man before GOD, for whose sake He created Heaven and Earth and all that is therein! When GOD allows the Devil and his crew <note>original: "Gesind" — meaning his followers or demonic attendants.</note> some leeway, He does so for certain reasons: for the good of the believers and for the punishment of the unbelievers. He does not allow the Devil and his crew everything they desire. For God rules them and holds them back with His bridle, as is seen in the story of Job. These monsters <note>original: "Unholden" — a term for witches or malevolent spirits.</note> often intend to harm people but are unable to do so; if the Devil could do what he liked, he would destroy the whole world. But he is capable of nothing. Therefore, let each of you surrender your body, soul, honor, property, and all that is yours to this, our true, living, Almighty God, who can, may, and will protect us all from all evil, including witches and all sorcery. You should not fear these things, but rather curse them with true faith. And if anyone should encounter such things, let him run to GOD for counsel and help with true faith; He will forsake no one, but will help and comfort. To Him be praise, honor, and glory from eternity to eternity.

<margin>God rejects these arts with His Law.</margin>
In conclusion, we wish to hear what GOD has established in His Law regarding these arts, and what other laws and rights have judged concerning them. I will mention only a few words: let everyone go to God’s Law and the legal statutes and read it all properly for themselves.

In the eighteenth chapter of Deuteronomy: *You shall not learn to do the abominations of those nations to which you come. Let there not be found among you anyone who makes his son or daughter pass through the fire, or a soothsayer, or a chooser of days <note>original: "Tagwehler" — one who practices superstition regarding "lucky" or "unlucky" days.</note>, or one who heeds the cries of birds, or a sorcerer, or a charmer, or a medium, or an interpreter of signs, or one who consults the dead. In the twentieth chapter of Leviticus: *When a soul turns to mediums and interpreters of signs (understand by this all those who deal in forbidden arts) to go whoring after them (note here what a "honorable" name is given to those who run after mediums), I will set my face against that soul and will root them out from their people.* Likewise: *When a man or woman is a medium or an interpreter of signs, they shall surely die; they shall be stoned, their blood shall be upon them.* And

In the twenty-second chapter of Exodus: *You shall not allow a sorceress to live.*

The Imperial Laws <note>The "Constitutio Criminalis Carolina," the legal code of the Holy Roman Empire.</note> also command them to be killed, just as the Divine Law does. Therefore, let those who dispute against these laws watch what they say when they conclude that witches who only deal in "fantasies" should not be burned or killed.

Concerning evildoers and astrologers, Book 9, Title 18: *Let no one consult an astrologer; let the magi attempt nothing. Let the curiosity for divining be silenced forever. For he who is disobedient shall suffer capital punishment, struck down by the avenging sword.* <note>original Latin: "De maleficis & mathematicis... ### The XIII. Little Treatise

# True Discovery and Expla-
### nation of all the most prominent articles of Sorcery; concerning sorcerers, monsters <note>original: "Vnholden" - demons or monstrous beings</note>, hags <note>original: "Hängsten" - an archaic term for a type of malevolent spirit or witch</note>, nightmares, "shots" <note>term: "Schüssen" - refers to 'elf-shot' or sudden supernatural pains believed to be inflicted by magic</note>, as well as the affairs, nature, deeds, omissions, essence, love-affairs, and medicines of witches, from whence they grow, and all their machinations: Likewise what changelings are, the "Furious Host" <note>note: The Wild Hunt or "Wüttens heer," a folklore motif of a ghostly procession</note>, what is to be held of them, etc. As experienced from their imprisonment by the Well-Born Lord, Lord Jacob, Baron of Liechtenberg, etc. Published by:

### Doctor Jacob Wecker.

**General Declaration concerning Sorcerers, Hags, Witches, and their Machinations, and what is to be held of them.**

Although it is with danger and sorrow that one must write and speak of sorcerers, hags, and witches—indeed, one should remain entirely silent before the simple-minded, since not everyone (even those who wish to be highly learned) is willing to conceive of the true understanding and report—nevertheless, it would not be fitting to proceed without a report. This is because so much depends upon it, and so much is spoken and dealt with regarding it. Since high and low estates speak and act so childishly concerning this matter, and few have written or taught on this material based on experience, I will describe as much as is necessary from Holy Scripture, proven histories, and daily experience.

**Whether Sorcery truly exists?**
**First, it is necessary to prove:**

<column-break/>

that sorcery and witchcraft truly exist, and by whom they were first invented and practiced. For many, both learned and unlearned, teach against this, crying out that it is a fable and that there is nothing to it; it is to them like a fable and a laughing matter. This is because they have no knowledge or experience of Holy or natural writings, nor of meteorological or mineral influences and impressions. Regarding this, you may consult Jacob Sprenger <note>note: Co-author of the Malleus Maleficarum</note> in Part 1, last Chapter, as to who first invented and practiced sorcery. You should also read Polydore <note>note: Polydore Vergil, author of "On Discovery"</note> in Books 22 and 23 of *On the Inventors of Things* <note>original: "de inuentoribus rerum"</note>, though it would be far too long to write here. But that sorcery and witchcraft truly exist lies so openly in the light of day that he who does not reject Holy Scripture and does not deny natural influences (neither of which a learned man rejects, since Holy Scripture and Nature affirm them) must believe in these effects and actions. For this has been proven and experienced in many ways in Scripture, Nature, and History.

Did not Aod <note>note: Likely referring to a figure from apocryphal traditions</note> practice great sorcery among the Jews? As Philo the Jew <note>original: "Philon Iudæus"</note> writes in the book *Biblical Antiquities* <note>original: "Antiquitatum Biblicarum"</note>.

# Discovery of all the most prominent articles of Sorcery

Likewise, the sorcerers of Pharaoh, as the Book of Exodus 7 shows. Similarly, Simon the Sorcerer <note>Simon Magus, mentioned in Acts 8</note> deceived the people. As Luke in the Histories <note>The Acts of the Apostles</note> describes, and as Cornelius Tacitus has well described regarding the Germanic people in his golden second book <note>referring to Tacitus's *Germania* or *Histories*</note>.

->Of two kinds of Sorcery.<-

In our time, we have two kinds of sorcery: that of the right hand and that of the left hand. On the right side are those who wish to be Christians but offend GOD with sorcery, believing that through blessings, consecrations, confirmations, the priest's holy water, bells, churches, herb-cakes <note>traditional blessed pastries</note>, Easter-baptism, and such child's play, they can forgive sin and drive out the Devil with his phantom sorcery and hags. This is no less a sorcery than that on the left side. For it is like taking an apple from the Creator and placing it upon Moloch <note>an ancient idol associated with sacrifice</note>; it is a turning away from GOD toward created things.

The Spirit of God does not allow itself to be conjured here and there, up and down, in and out, according to the thoughts of every fool, bishop, or priest—as if He could be conjured in and out of stone, wood, ore, wax, herbs, or oil—since He is otherwise present in all things according to His measure. Man (says Solomon) has no power over the Spirit to restrain or compel it. What GOD has once blessed remains blessed for eternity. Therefore, all blessing by priests or laypeople is a wasted, useless, and truly sorcerous blessing and consecration.

How much sorcery and witchcraft is practiced by Jews, heathens, and evil or weak Christians through blessings, prayers, crossings, characters <note>magical symbols or sigils</note>, pilgrimages, and writings is well known to all true Christians. Through these, countless people have been seduced and deceived, as will be testified hereafter.

That sorcery and witchcraft are also practiced on the left side by those who hold GOD and Christ in little regard and make use of the Devil and created things, we have proven in many ways through Holy Scripture and history. Where Moses, by God's power, turned the staff into snakes and water into blood, the sorcerers soon accomplished similar wonders out of nature through the Devil's help, whose power is greater than any man's.

And such things are found in many and various places, which will be proven and described bit by bit in the process. Namely: Genesis 41, Exodus 7, 8, 9, 22, Numbers 23, Leviticus 19, 20, Deuteronomy 18, 1 Kings 28, 4 Kings 1, 21, 23, 1 Chronicles 11, 2 Chronicles 33, Psalm 58, Isaiah 2, 8, 44, 47, Jeremiah 10, 27, Daniel 2, 4, 5, Micah 5, Nahum 3, Zechariah 12, Wisdom 12, Ecclesiasticus 34, Acts 8, 13, 16, 19. No less has the Pope also written of sorceries. Namely: 26. Question 2. 4. 5. 7. 88. Distinction 33. Question 1. chapter *Si per fortiarias* <note>Latin: "If by means of sorceresses"</note>. Likewise throughout the *Extra de sortilegiis* <note>Latin: Decretals concerning fortune-tellers</note> and Thomas <note>Aquinas</note> *Secunda Secundae*, question 95.

Just as the Scripture speaks in general and in specific terms, so also are sorcerers named in many and various places; and as many sorceries as there are, so many names may they bear. They are sometimes called: *Magi* <note>Magicians</note>, *arioli* <note>soothsayers</note>, *augures* <note>augurs</note>, *omen servantes* <note>observers of omens</note>, *Malefici* <note>evildoers/witches</note>, *Somniatores* <note>dreamers</note>, *Pythones* <note>spirit-mediums</note>, *Incantatores* <note>enchanters</note>, *Aruspices* <note>diviners using entrails</note>, *Divinatores* <note>diviners</note>, *Necromantici* <note>necromancers</note>, *Geomantici* <note>earth-diviners</note>, *Hydromantici* <note>water-diviners</note>, *Pyromantici* <note>fire-diviners</note>, etc. Regarding these, one should consult Augustine, *On Christian Doctrine* book 2, and Polydore <note>Vergil</note> *On the Discovery of Things* book 1, chapter 22.

The magical art has this nature: that sorcerers, through the Devil, haunt the elements, trouble the minds of men, and poison hearts through harmful potions, whereby they also undertake to make people sick, to kill, to make the sick healthy again, and to revive the dead.

**Scapulamantici:** Those who, by looking at the shoulder blades and limbs, wish to describe the nature of men.

**Sortilegij:** Those who, with strange figures and characters, undertake to bring about wonderful things. As in 26. question 1. chapter *Sortilegij*.

**Arioli:** These are those who practice through slips of paper blessed on altars and similar phantoms and blessings for good and evil.

**Augures:** Those who give their ears to the song of birds so that they may take future things from it. Some from the flight, others from the song.

**Malefici:** Those who do evil to creatures through the Devil and direct cruel phantoms against their neighbor.

->Three things belong to Sorcery.<-

Furthermore, it is to be known that three things are necessary for sorcery. Namely, the **permission of God** as the first and principal part. The second is the **human sorcerer**. The third is the **Devil**, Satan <term>ascending and descending</term> <note>referring to the direction from which spirits appear</note>, the <term>Incubus and Succubus</term> <note>demons believed to have sexual relations with sleeping humans</note>, etc. The permission of GOD is a cause of all sorcery and the work of the devil, as well as of the sorcerer. Without it, neither the devil nor the sorcerer has any power or ability. Therefore, the sorcerers could not create lice nor interpret Pharaoh's dream where God did not permit it. The devil can never create, as was proven in the case of Job.

But GOD permits this and allows it for both the good and the evil: for the good as a trial, and for the evil as a punishment. For the good, such as Job and Tobit; for the evil, such as Simon Magus. And this happens (says Augustine in *The City of God*, book 23, and in the *Sentences*, Distinction 7 & 8) to de-

<column-break/>

->From whence Sorcery grows.<-

Sorcery and witchcraft <note>original: "Zauberey uñ Hexenwerck"</note> grow from many kinds of causes, as Pliny writes in Book 30, chapters 1 and 2. Sometimes from evil company, playmates, pride, greed, envy, hatred, carnal wantonness, sadness, or poverty. When, for these reasons (as described hereafter), people bind themselves to the devil, keep fellowship with him, and enter into a contract and <term>Homage</term> <note>original: "Omaginierent," meaning to swear fealty as a vassal</note>—that is, they pledge themselves to him. There they deny GOD and their Creator JESUS Christ and all believers; they also wish to defile all creatures and surrender themselves body and soul to the devil, offering to him, and thereafter whoring with him. Sometimes they sign the covenant with blood.

This happens with men and women, but more so with women than with men; the reason is that they are of a weaker nature than men, as Aristotle says in the fifth book of *On Animals*. It is also accomplished in two ways: in general and in particular. In particular, the "Ascending" devil approaches the person and presents his suit to them. If they then consent, they come to an agreement until it comes before the general assembly. It is just as when someone takes a woman "by words of the present" <note>original: "in verbo de præsenti," a legal term for a binding marriage contract made through a simple declaration</note> and only afterwards is it confirmed before the community or church. Generally, it is confirmed in this way: when the devil, through his beadles, calls a General Council of all witches from all places, or of a specific nation of the world, then the novices are presented, as is their custom, and counted in the assembly. Also, as with the others, the mark is embodied and attached to them, as will be described hereafter.

It is not hidden from us that the Ascendants, Descendants, spirits of the stars, and the influence of the stars of heaven—just as we plant the earth—also fulfill their office on earth afterward, as do the spirits created for vengeance. Indeed, as soon as the child is born, he attempts his...

These spirits—Ascendants and Descendants—have among them strange and divided natures. One draws toward sorcery. Another toward harlotry. The third toward stealing. Now, where children of this nature are not raised well by father and mother, nor surrendered to God and Christ by calling upon Him with prayer, fasting, and persistence, the child is raised in ruin and finally damned in this vice.

Therefore, you parents, hold fast with care and discipline, so that children are raised in the fear of God and are rescued and protected from these vices.

When these spirits and sins have taken root in children from youth upward and they are not drawn away from them, then a false nature will build its dwelling therein, which afterwards does not easily fall. It grows up in malice, added to the fact that man has a corrupt nature in himself. By nature, he is envious, hateful, proud, greedy, and desirous of fleshly lust. Then, when he finds the innate envy, hate, greedy heart, and fleshly desire to be serviceable to him—a fit instrument—he hunts them down with envy, hate, pride, greed, and fleshly desire, according to the nature of the person, until he succeeds and thrusts the spear into their hand.

When the spirit finds this, he incites them further to pride, greed, envy, hate, and fleshly lust, according to how he finds the person's disposition. Is he envious? He moves the man to revenge. Is he

The good ones as **Tobias** and **Luke** describe. The evil ones as happened with **Eve**, **Job**, **Christ**, etc. In a dream, he proposes how he should do or leave this or that. He prescribes **Ceremonies** for them, which actually contribute nothing to the result (as will be said hereafter), but are used so that he may conveniently come to pride, riches, stealing, whoring, etc.

Likewise, he appears visibly in an assumed body, which he takes to himself from the air and the earth. He forms it however he wishes to have it: in a young or old, human or animal shape. Yet it is not like a human, for there is no sensitive life, true soul, **physical organ** <note>original: "Organum physicum"</note>, nor human informing spirit, as **Aristotle** writes in **book 2 of *On the Soul*** <note>original: "2. de anima"</note>. It has no natural eyes, belly, intestines, etc., although it is so shaped that it may see, drink, eat, or digest from it like another human. He drives the body as a master drives a wheel, or a pilot a ship. Therefore, several philosophers, such as **Apuleius** and **Africanus**, were deceived when they said that devils are "animals, bodily, rational, immortal, and of a subtle body." Even if he behaves as if he eats, drinks, or sees, it is all an illusion. He sees by himself in the spirit. He keeps the food hidden until he can cast it out, so that he may deceive the world. With such a body, he often comes to men and women. He speaks to them friendly, promises them land and people, goods and money, but he performs little for them, as he did to Christ. Thereafter, he makes **Covenants**, desperate contracts, and establishes alliances and tokens of obligation. He prescribes ceremonies. He points out and teaches them how to satisfy pride, greed, fleshly lust, envy, and hate. He decks out the proud with beautiful jewels, commits harlotry with the fleshly, makes the poor rich, and fulfills the lust of the greedy, as will be further related hereafter.

### On the making of Thunder / Hail / Snow / Rain and Frost.

He also teaches them, according to their delusion, how they should make, enchant, and cast spells for thunder, hail, frost, snow, storms, and the air. Likewise, how to transform into cats, beasts, wolves, goats, donkeys, geese, and birds; how to ride upon sticks and forks; how to travel from one place to another; and how to lame people and make them <note>The original term "Mütischer" likely refers to being "mutisch" or "mütisch," meaning dejected, silenced, or perhaps physically stunted/crippled.</note> broken in spirit.

Once they understand and have been taught this, they break out into deeds according to the nature of their spirit or <term>Ascendant</term> <note>In this context, the author uses "Ascendant" to refer to a guiding spirit or a specific astrological influence that governs the sorcerer's power.</note>; they undertake to use ceremonies to satisfy their envy, hatred, pride, and fleshly desires, just as the Devil teaches them. He shows them strange works, such as making a scepter with four knobs, each for a direction of the world: West, East, North, and North-Wind <note>original: "Occident, Orient, Septentrion und Aquilon"</note>, and placing it in the location where they wish to act, striking it with a small hammer. Then the Devil travels to that same region and works upon <term>Nature</term>—which he is able to bring together—whereby it hails, frosts, snows, or storms, as <margin>Jacobus Sprenger wrote in part two, chapter fifteen.</margin> Jacobus Sprenger <note>Sprenger was the co-author of the *Malleus Maleficarum*, the infamous witch-hunting manual.</note> wrote in part two, chapter fifteen.

Now, when GOD permits the Ascendant and the sorcerer, the spirit may bring about everything that Nature is capable of. Therefore, the sorcerer, through the help of the Ascendants, can bring summer fruit—such as cherries, strawberries, and apples—in the winter; indeed, quite naturally, not phantom fruits. For the regions of the earth are unequal according to their influence. When it is summer with us, it is winter among the <term>Antipodes</term> <note>People living on the opposite side of the globe.</note>. Our horizon or climate may have fruit that the African or Indian cannot. And when it is autumn with us, it is the lower spring <note>original: "Nideren Glenz"</note>; when it is night with us, it is day for those below. As is clearly shown on the Globe. There, one finds every day summer, spring, winter, autumn, etc. Thus, time continually provides cherries, strawberries, and apples every day; it is always autumn and harvest somewhere, so that all is Natural. Although to the ignorant man it

<column-break/>

is strange and breeds wonder, the <term>Magus</term> <note>A practitioner of high magic or a learned sorcerer.</note> or sorcerer can bring such things about quickly through his Ascendants. Thus it has often happened that the sorcerer, through his Ascendant, has taken his food from the kitchen in the East <note>original: "Orient"</note> and brought it to another in the West. All this, if GOD permits it, happens Naturally, for the spirit can travel from place to place swiftly and soon, as the Scripture reports of Habakkuk <note>A reference to the apocryphal story of Habakkuk being carried by an angel to feed Daniel in the lions' den.</note>.

Furthermore, where the sorcerers and witches wish to accomplish their works—making hail or frost—they employ certain ceremonies and thereby call upon the Devil. He then travels to where storms are naturally present in the air and drives them to the place and town where they wish to carry out their envy and hatred with revenge. For this, the Devil is always prepared. He can retain the materials with which he makes thunder, hail, and snow as long as the hour is convenient for him to use them.

To this end, he sometimes wants a sign from the witch, especially her hair, which he then mixes into the hailstones and coats them with ice—just as the apothecary coats coriander with sugar, or as the minter strikes the mark upon the silver. For just as man can work in metals, so the Ascendant can work in the influence of the heavens. For Nature is subjected to him by GOD’S permission.

Now, wherever the sorcerer or witch wishes to pour out their envy, the Devil directs the storm there, just as the archer directs his arrow to the target; he drives the clouds with power, so that they move faster than a bullet from a gun. This should be understood for hail, as well as for frost, snow, wind, freezing, and cloudbursts.

This does not happen against Nature, but rather with Nature; for there are many arts on earth that compare themselves with <term>Meteorological</term> impressions <note>Atmospheric phenomena or "meteors" in the Aristotelian sense.</note> and how the heavenly generations occur. ### Concerning the Medicine of the Sorcerers and Witches.

Furthermore, it is to be known that the sorcerers, wizards, and witches also perform many wonders with medicine through the Devil, making many healthy. Indeed, they only heal those whom they have previously injured, poisoned, or made infirm through the Devil, and then cease to afflict them; through this, they acquire a great following and reputation, as Augustine in *On Christian Doctrine* and *On the Divination of Demons* <note>original: "Augustinus de Doctr. Christia. de diuinatione Dæmon."</note>, as well as Lactantius in *The Divine Institutes*, Book 2, Chapter 6 <note>original: "Lactantius, de erroris origine lib. 2. cap. 6."</note>, describe.

### Concerning Night-Afflictions and the "Shots" of Witches.

In this way, they injure many people and cattle, even unto death. All this occurs by God's favor or permission, primarily in that they shoot things under the skin into the body: straw, hog bristles, wood splinters, leather, scraps, thread, <term>Fürbatten</term> <note>likely small bundles or charms used in folk magic</note>, spindle-tips, fish bones, intestines, and countless others. The Devil performs this so masterfully that the skin is not injured by it. He opens the *pores* (sweat-holes), reaches inside, and leaves the object lying in the flesh; then the pores close up again, just as when someone places a stone in the water, pulls their hand back out, and leaves the stone lying there. Then no one sees how the stone got into the water. Thus it also happens naturally at times that a lightning bolt strikes through a scabbard without damaging it, but melts the iron within; it makes the scabbard *porous* (full of holes). The same happens with this phantom-work, which is more evil than other blows and wounds.

### How Witches Enchant Men and Take Their Strength and Limbs.

No less does such an intrusion happen to men, whereby their manly strength is taken from them. As Ham did to his father Noah, as Berosus writes, and more examples are written by Jacobus Sprenger in Part 2, Chapters 6 and 7 <note>referring to the *Malleus Maleficarum*, a famous 15th-century treatise on hunting witches</note>.

Likewise, if the witches bear a grudge against certain men or women, they prepare the *ascendants* by the power of their pact; they may use many kinds of ceremonies, roots, stones, herbs, and ointments, but these do nothing. Only the intrusion of the Devil is the cause. Here he does not thrust anything inside, but he applies a poison there so that he lames him in the kidneys, just as a fisherman reaches into the water and squeezes the fish so that it spoils or dies. Thus the Devil reaches into the loins and lames the source, after which other illnesses follow. Such intrusions happen to the old and young, not only in the manner described, but also affecting the liver, lungs, spleen, kidneys, and brain. Thus he makes them liver-sick, ill, insane, or brain-frenzied. Then people say she has eaten "cat brains," which is a superstition and a folly, for all this must happen through the *ascendants*. Much more unbelief is practiced here by poor women with the members of men, which they take from them—if God permits it and the Devil proves his art—which sit in nests like birds. Although some do not understand this so literally, as if the limbs were entirely and substantially torn or cut from the body (since a person could hardly live through that), and they sometimes return or are sent back without pain. This indicates that it happens solely by a *prestigious art* <note>original: "præstigiosa arte"; meaning an art of illusion or trickery that deceives the senses</note>, with the eyes blinded and hardened through sorcery.

Then it often happens that he makes the witches pregnant and gives birth through the child. Therefore the children are called *Camphiones* or *Wechselkindt* <term>Changelings: folklore beings substituted for real children</term>, as William of Auvergne says in *On the Universe*, last part <note>original: "Guilielmus Parisiensis de vniuerso"</note>. These children are deformed, with large bellies, small limbs, and large heads; they have the devil's members, and five women are not enough to suckle or nourish one.

Yes, even sometimes the *Incubus* devil deceives virgins who have never known a man and makes them pregnant, as is written in the Histories of Merlin, who was born of a nun, enclosed, without any man. As is described in Hartmann Schedel’s *Sixth Age* in his life <note>referring to the Nuremberg Chronicle</note>, and likewise in Nauclerus, Volume 2, Genesis 15.

Likewise, the *Incubus Ascendant* transforms himself into an animal—a goat, donkey, or dog; or rather, he creeps into such an animal and speaks out of it. He forms it before our eyes as he wishes: above like a human, below like a goat, dog, or donkey. From this comes the proverb: "The devil has the feet of a donkey, dog, or goat." And by the power of that same animal, he accomplishes his work. Therefore, among the young witches, animal-like and terrifying figures—like donkeys, goats, and dogs—are born. He also sometimes beds these children on the hayloft, under linden leaves, or in secret places, so that they are not shamed before the world; for he protects them, not for their sake but for his own good, from vice and shame, so that he may longer deceive and harm the world with them.

### Concerning the Wild Hunt.

Since we have understood what it means to ride on forks, sticks, and animals, and how that may happen: now let us declare what the <term>Wüttisheer</term> <note>The Wild Hunt or "Wotan's Host," a folkloric procession of spirits or witches</note> is. It is a gathering of all or many lords, monsters, stallions, and sorcerers who come together in a council to conduct their business. They carry out what they cannot achieve in their own houses: to legislate, to instruct, to conspire, to teach, to agree, to enroll, to mark, to pay homage, to give vows, and to establish what their covenant contains; to command one another what mischief they wish to stir up, and also what each one has to accomplish for themselves, and thus complete their vice and witchcraft.

Furthermore, it is to be understood that since the sorcerers and witches have dealings with <term>Incubi</term> and <term>Succubi</term> <note>demons believed to have sexual intercourse with sleeping humans</note>, both higher and lower spirits, some also become pregnant. Now, if it happens that they cannot carry out their business in their houses as necessity demands, they devise this (like a maiden who is pregnant and wishes to hide her birth, who goes to a bath until the matter is finished) with the Wild Hunt. They all come together from all nations; the Devil leads them over bush and stone, villages, cities, lands, people, mountains, and valleys with gruesome crying and terrifying horror. The leading Devil flies before and after them until they come to the place they have appointed; there they are delivered of their children, hold their confinements, and carry out all their dealings.
