### How Witches Transform into Animals.

Now follows a wonder known through witches: that the hags and witches are transformed into animals—cats, wolves, bucks, goats, dogs, geese, and birds. For this, they again have ceremonies, ointments, and blessings, as if it must happen through their art. They have a special drink, ointment, and blessing for every animal, wherein they are subsequently deceived, for the <term>Ascendentes</term> <note>plural of Ascendent; the spirits</note> must do this without any other means. Just as a potter may make a jug, a tile, or other vessel out of clay, and break it again, and make it differently again—so it is with the spirit and the witch. The spirit is the master, the witch is the clay, and in such a way a cat, wolf, or goat is made out of the witch. In this, nothing is taken away from the person, nor is anything added, but like the clay, it is possible and known to the spirits. This also happens so that the witches become unknown to the people, whereby they may do more harm to the world; for cats climb upon the roof, creep into houses, and may enter rooms and chambers without suspicion, there to steal, perform sorcery, and injure children. Wolves do striking damage to the livestock, for no one pays attention to the possibility that these might be witches. And when a witch-hag is transformed into such an animal, she also has that animal's nature, strength, and power—and even more besides, because the <term>Ascendent</term> assists her in it. If they are struck while in these forms, as often happens, those same blows and wounds are found on the witch's body when she returns to her old being, just as she received them. Dei libr. decimooctauo, capite decimoseptimo & decimoctauo"</note> Although I will set down no final declaration or conclusion on this question, leaving the judgment to the reader, I find two opinions debated here. Macarius released this woman from witchcraft through his prayer. Likewise, God also turned King Nebuchadnezzar into a beast, as Daniel has written.

# Discovery of all the most noble articles of Sorcery.

Regarding the second point, it has been argued often and at length whether an essential transformation <note>original: *essentialiter*</note> can truly occur, because Nature is capable of it, and everything is possible for the Devil, provided that God permits it.

Now, Nature is capable over a long period of time of turning one body into another; therefore, there is a continual alteration in every body, both of humans and of cattle. In this way, a human always takes on the character of the food they consume. If one always eats fish, their nature becomes cold, just as the fish is. Likewise, if one always eats coarse pork, their nature and coarse character will become pig-like; this is experienced among the peasants, which is why they belch so much and are pig-like. Conversely, those who make use of pure, subtle, noble food become noble, subtle, of high understanding, and great reason. Therefore, Aristotle also says: "We say those of soft flesh are apt of mind" <note>original: *Molles carne aptos mente dicimus*</note>, meaning those of a pure nature are gifted in spirit. Likewise, if one consumes poison, their nature and everything becomes poison, as Aristotle writes in the third book of *Physics* and in the treatise written to Alexander the Great; and where one nature is consumed, another soon grows in its place; the "birth of one is the corruption of another" <note>original: *generatio vnius, corruptio alterius*</note> from the second book of *Metaphysics*.

Now, there is also one matter for all elements and their same conjunction <note>original: *primo de generatione & corruptione*</note>: that one may become out of the other through the order of Nature and the course of time, as Pliny writes in Book 7, Chapter 4 of his *Natural History*, that a man was once born from a woman, etc. Now, what Nature is capable of through a long time and its course, Satan is capable of in a short time, for he can accelerate Nature so that the business is soon completed; hence he soon (like Moses through God's power) brought forth truly natural frogs. Here some admit that the Devil may only make "creeping dust-animals" <note>original: *Animalia reptilia puluerina*</note>, which do not always grow from proper seed but from "decay" <note>original: *ex putredine*</note> or filth, such as all vermin and worms; and that he cannot transform such animals [higher beings], which no one can or wants to dispute. For Aristotle says, "Let the al-

<column-break/>

chemists rejoice, since they cannot transmute the species of things" <note>original: *Gaudeant Alchimistæ, quoniam species rerum transmutare non possunt*</note>, etc. Neither the Devil nor sorcerers can ever alter the specific forms of species, such that a human is no longer a human and loses human character, reason, and nature; the same applies to other animals born from "perfect seed" <note>original: *perfecto semine*</note>. However, Nature, which is a matter under one form, is capable of this: that the same matter is now "in potential" <note>original: *in potentia*</note> for another form, where Nature does not err, even if one form follows another. See also *On Generation and Corruption*, book 1, etc.

Though the matter of "creeping animals" remains as it is, the sorcerers have nonetheless turned water into blood and the staff into snakes; from this, it is concluded that they change forms "by means of matter" <note>original: *mediante materia*</note>. Based on this, it is argued that they may also alter humans and animals, while the "human species remains" <note>original: *manente specie humana*</note>; the human remains a human even though he is organized and shaped differently. **EXAMPLE:** Sometimes it happens that Nature errs in conception, so that a shape is born of a strange form: perhaps one that does not see, another that does not hear or speak, with four feet, two heads, etc. Yet it is still a human, even if it has less of the human shape or form. In the same way, Satan can change the body of a human into another form. Thus Helena gave the child another form, as Herodotus writes in book 6. Yet the soul and matter always remain uninjured in their value; the human is "composed of a rational soul and a body" <note>original: *compositum ex anima rationali & corpore*</note>, so that even the transmuted one remains; it is not essential that he be "two-legged" <note>original: *bipes*</note>, it "suffices to have a body and a soul" <note>original: *sufficit habere corpus & animam*</note>, etc.

How all this happens, I wish to make known to the natural philosopher <term>physico: a student of the physical world and nature</term> and the reader, and briefly recount what has been described of such things. Diodorus Siculus writes in book 2 that Proteus, King in Egypt, had the art to change himself into another form—now an animal, fire, a tree, etc.

Likewise, several gods changed themselves into animals, birds, and dogs, as Nauclerus claims in Volume 1, Genesis 24, etc. Similarly, the goddess Circe changed countless [men] into animals.

->On the stealing of milk by witches.<-

So that you may also recognize the strength of the "ascendants" <note>term: Ascendenten; here referring to rising spirits or demonic influences that govern certain physical effects</note>, know herewith that witches appear to milk cows from distaffs, axe-handles, nails, etc. It is not that the milk actually comes out of the distaff, handle, or nail. It must come from the fact that it is naturally from the cow, although the devil sometimes brings it or offers water instead of milk. From this it follows that the spirits steal the milk from the cows in the stall, and sometimes even from nursing women. You should understand it thus: the witches do not have the power to do it themselves, but by the pact they have with the spirits, the spirits milk the cows, carrying and leading the milk through the air to the place where the witch wants it. Then, as she strokes the distaff, handle, or nail, the Devil pours the milk into the tub or vessel. Though it all happens invisibly, the sorceress believes the milk flows out through the distaff or nail. The Devil may also hide the milk so it is not seen, clouding or veiling the vessel just as we cover a thing so it cannot be seen. This work is not actually "milking," but rather "pouring out." Jacob Sprenger <note>Co-author of the *Malleus Maleficarum* (The Hammer of Witches)</note> mentions this in the second part, chapter fourteen; you may look it up there.

As Origen testifies in his 7th Homily on Isaiah, Chapter 8.

# Discovery of All the Most Notable Articles of Sorcery

That witches, sorcerers, and magicians tell the truth and predict the future through the Devil—as happened in the case of Saul <note>Referring to King Saul seeking the Witch of Endor in 1 Samuel 28</note>—is no wonder. For the Devil often transforms himself into an Angel of Light; he speaks of the future and the truth, but not for the sake of truth, rather for his own benefit. Just as when he said: "Christ was the Son of GOD," he did so only so that he would not be tormented by Him (Matthew 8, Mark 5, Luke 4). Likewise, the priests of Pharaoh spoke the truth regarding Moses, as Josephus writes in the second book, ninth chapter of *Antiquities*.

The Devil speaks the truth at various times so that those who refuse to believe the truth might offend GOD even more, and so that his own profit might be increased. He also draws many away from the truth through false miracles so that the world might be deceived. This happened to Pope Leo X, as it is said of him: he spoke to the Devil within a possessed person, saying, "If I am the true Vicar of Christ <note>Latin: *Vicarius Christi*; the Pope's title as earthly representative of Christ</note>, then depart, you Devil!" Immediately the Devil departed, so that he might deceive the Pope and his household into believing he truly was the Vicar of Christ, which is not the case.

The magician Manius deceived Tarquinius Priscus when he cut a stone as if it were wood, so that he might lead him into the error of augury <note><term>Augury</term>: The practice of predicting the future by observing the flight of birds</note>. (Livy, Book 1; Valerius, Book 1, Chapter 4).

Now, when the Devil speaks of the future with magicians, sorcerers, and witches, it has no other basis than this: he is experienced in all the natural arts, from which he can deduce what is likely to happen in the future based on what has occurred before. Just as an astronomer predicts the course of the heavens, or a physician predicts a person's future health, so too did he have good knowledge regarding Saul. Since he saw that David had been anointed King, that the great army of the Philistines was camped in the field against Saul, and saw the disobedient disorder among Saul's people, Satan could easily recount and prophesy Saul's destruction (because of his disobedience). Without these means, he would not have been able to know the future on his own. Yet there is no profound substance there; there is always a deception within it, as Eusebius says in Book 5, Chapters 16 and 17: "The idol in Antioch prophesied much, but it was all lies." Likewise in Book 9, Chapter 3: Whenever the Devil spoke of the future through oracles, he always deceived therein and never gave a definitive report. As Cicero says regarding the Delphic Oracle in Book 2 of *On Divination*: "I say the Romans shall conquer the Trojans" <note>original: "Aio te, Aeacida, Romanos vincere posse" - a famous grammatical ambiguity where either side could be the victor</note>. That was an answer that pointed from one question to another, showing nothing certain, because the opposite could also be found within it. If he says, "I saw the Trojans conquer the Romans," one is to be understood just as the other. Such false oracular prophecy was received by Croesus, King of the Persians, from the idol, as written by Herodotus, Plutarch in many places, Diodorus Siculus, the *Tripartite History*, and Nauclerus. How all this is done and accomplished is nothing, as Lactantius says in *The Origin of Error*, except that the Devil wishes to deceive or be deceived therein. He also wishes to keep the fallen in their error because they rejected the love of truth, as happened to Saul. Therefore, we should in no way believe the Devil and his followers, for he is a Father of Lies and wishes to deceive us with them, just as happened to Eve.

<column-break/>

In this, one should consider well and distinguish between works, so that we may test prophecies properly and rightly. For GOD often speaks of the future through men, such as Eldad and Medad; likewise the Sibyls <note>Ancient prophetesses believed by some early Christians to have predicted Christ</note> spoke, and no less was prophesied through Caiaphas. Therefore, not all prophets are children of GOD; GOD uses them as an instrument, like Saul, Balaam, etc. Baptist Fulgosus wrote of such things in Book 8, Chapter 11. It is certain and true that no one can tell the future except GOD alone, and those to whom He commits His Spirit. If they chatter about the future now, it is all a deception, even if they happen to guess correctly, for it all happens through the Devil, who ultimately tells no truth except where he might benefit from it. It often happens that those who are sick or have lost something run to the sorcerers to seek help and counsel from them, wherein they be— <note>The text cuts off mid-word "befinden" or "betrogen," matching the catchword "sie be-" from the previous page's metadata.</note>

I have experienced this myself; indeed, the sorcerer, etc., has accused pious, honorable people who were afterwards found innocent before God and the world, all of which happened out of envy and hatred.

->Expelling magic with magic.<-

How well you judges must guard yourselves, so that no one is condemned out of innocence, envy, or hatred! You should investigate the matter with earnestness and not believe every rumor and invented slander. Suspicion must be entirely transparent; test whether it arises from truth, lies, envy, hatred, etc. It is better to let ten guilty people go free than to torture one innocent person.

And if it should be found true that someone is a witch, sorcerer, wizard, etc., guilty in this city and rightfully condemned to death: then desist from the foolish, superstitious articles of questioning once they are captured. Do not insist on not letting them touch the ground, throwing them into tubs, shaving off their hair, carrying them to court on carts, and whatever other superstitions there are—all of which I have seen and experienced myself. Indeed, for the sake of superstition you kill them, yet you uphold the same superstition yourselves! These people are such "clever" courts, just as Saul did; you may by no means defend injustice with injustice. Dirt cannot be cleaned with dirt; the pile only grows larger because of it. Thus, magic cannot be Christianly expelled with magic. We should do nothing evil so that good may follow; act as becomes Christian rulers, and then the Devil will not harm you. But if you persist and remain in this mistrust, you will encounter in your flight that which you fled from; for the Devil has the opportunity and power to pay deceit with deceit, so that he might snatch the witches from your hands and carry them into the air, rescuing them from your hand—all of which is caused by the unbelief you hold in this matter.

<column-break/>

The executioner <note>original: "Henker/ Nachrichter"</note> is also entirely foolish here, imagining he can force the poor people to confess with his phantoms and "blessings." He pours Easter-baptism water and St. John’s blessing <note>note: A ritual drink or sacramental used superstitiously to compel truth</note> into the person, etc. Let the authorities look to this, for certainly the people in this business have neither conscience nor knowledge; thus all their actions and omissions are inclined only toward torture.

As soon as you—says Dr. Johannes Nider <note>note: A 15th-century theologian and author of the 'Formicarius', an early work on witchcraft</note>—fall under the power of the regular authorities, which is from GOD the LORD, all the witches' power falls from them. But if you do not stand firm in GOD, but doubt and fear in this work, and fail to keep watch over your faith in GOD, it will happen to you as in the example he gives: A judge sent his servants to arrest a sorcerer; the man emitted such an unbearable stench that they could not grab him. This made their hearts unbelieving and despondent. Then the judge rebuked his servants and said: "You of little heart, go forth as servants of Justice, which is meant to punish the wicked." Soon the servants caught the poor man.

### Driving away Witchcraft with Blessings.

There are many others who wish to drive away witchcraft with blessings, holy water, salt, herbs, words, signs, the ringing of bells, and other ceremonies. They attribute a special power to these things so that they might prevail over the others, also using natural powers like herbs and stones, such as mouse-ear, <unclear>sar</unclear>, vervain, elderberry, rue, <unclear>buggeln</unclear>, coral, etc. They cite as a reason that every herb and stone is given a particular *Ascendant* which will not and cannot suffer any witchcraft, and which is stronger than the *Ascendant* of the witches. There are many more experiments which are not worth writing down because of their folly. Tobias drove away the spirit from Sarah with the liver upon the embers, concerning which you may consult the physician Petrus de Largelata <note>Pietro d'Argelata</note> in his book on the bewitched, Book 5, Tract 8, Chapter 8.

Likewise, some look at figures which, when made upon bricks and directed against the weather, drive the storm back; and when placed upon the afflicted area, the harm is healed. The reason given is that a strong *Ascendant* signifies the figure and is present to drive away the other. In this way, witches who have transformed into cats, wolves, or goats are also struck, captured, and killed. No less does the foolish common folk undertake to drive away storms, hail, and frost with crosses stuck upon the roads. Likewise,

### How one shall recognize witches; how witches are identified.

We recognize sorcerers, witches, and <term>Hengst</term> <note>literally "stallions," here referring to male witches or warlocks</note> by their works, life, and conduct. These people direct all their actions toward their own profit and toward creating unrest and discord, for their *Ascendant* is an enemy of peace and love. They cast their eyes down into the corners; the women flee from men, and the boys from girls, etc. For the <term>incubi</term> and <term>succubi</term> <note>demons believed to have sexual intercourse with sleeping humans</note> will not tolerate it, just as there is an innate jealousy that no one suffers their beloved to be shared with another. Thus, the *incubus* or *succubus* is even less willing to suffer it; and even if the women are married to men, their love does not come from the heart. They throw the men "over the saddle" <note>an idiom for rejecting or unseating them</note>, and are envious and intolerable toward their husbands and all people. And the more chaste, quiet, and secluded they are kept, the sooner they fall into witchcraft; therefore, it is to be feared that many of these vermin are in the cloisters, both of men and women. Likewise, they are unfaithful toward their own children, unfriendly and unsociable with the household servants. The Devil also prepares them so that they become misshapen, deformed, and reckless, so that they may endure their husbands. He sometimes marks their mouths, ears, hands, feet, foreheads, etc., as if he were cutting out the <term>chrism</term> <note>the holy anointing oil from baptism, which the devil was said to try to remove</note>, or otherwise makes them lame, crooked, or injures their eyes. Indeed, not only they, but their children are marked, so that one may recognize the mothers by the children.

### By what means witchcraft is to be prevented and whom it may harm.

Now, whatever the nature of witchcraft or sorcery may be, whether great or small, it can do no harm to one who is founded, fixed, or strengthened in faith. For in everything that happens through witchcraft and the Devil, unbelief alone is the cause; God permits this as a punishment. # Lord Jacob, Baron of Liechtenberg.

<note>original: "Adversus gentes"</note> Against the Heathen, chapter 23; Athanasius in his *Various Questions*, question 13; likewise you may consult Jacob Sprenger <note>Co-author of the Malleus Maleficarum</note> in part 2 regarding those who are exempt.

Therefore, to prevent, ward off, and root out such sorcery, we must seek God and Jesus Christ in earnest and pray for faith, so that neither ghosts, the Devil, armies, hail, wind, snow, frost, etc., nor anything else may harm us. Let us first seek the kingdom of God, then all things shall be added unto us, and thereafter let us cultivate the love that God desires from us. For this reason, men should love their wives, and in turn, wives should love their husbands and be obedient to them, as this is the greatest medicine against this work of witches. These two should raise their children in the fear of God, believe the Holy Scriptures, and teach them to love and to work. Do not let them go idle, especially where they are <term>Melancholy</term> <note>In this period, "melancholy" or "black bile" was believed to be a physical imbalance that made people vulnerable to demonic despair or hallucinations.</note>, for idleness invites these vices. Likewise, keep children honorable through discipline, assisting them in all their needs; do not be grim or shameful toward them, nor overstretch the bow. Allow them reasonable joy, such as wrestling, jumping, singing, and modest dancing. Let them engage in comedies and the playing of music and stringed instruments—just as this drove the Devil away from Saul, and as the smoke drove the ghost away from Sarah <note>A reference to the Book of Tobit</note>—and pursue similar joys, all with discipline and propriety. This is so they are not driven into such fantasies. For it is better to do this than to fall into such wickedness and evil. Aristotle says that such joyful play is unnecessary for man in Book 4 and 8 of the *Politics*. Thus, one must also choose the lesser of two evils, as in Book 5 of the *Ethics*. Although all these things, when carried out in moderation, may be done with God and honor, I do not wish to establish unseemly rattling or vicious carousing, etc., but rather let propriety be the judge; only take away the sadness from these melancholy people, which is not the least cause of this vice. For sadness also brings death and the ruin of body and life; just as the moth harms the garment, so sadness harms the heart.

Sometimes people also cannot bear to be restrained and locked away from joy; where joy is denied them, worse things come of it. The Lord also does not refuse reasonable joy, as He says: "I will build you up again, O Virgin Israel; you shall take up your tambourines, string the instruments, and go forth to the dances and pastimes." There, joy is a blessing and mourning is a punishment. The wisest of wise men speaks thus: wise speech is found in their instruction; they have pursued the sweetness and loveliness of music and brought forth lovely poems, etc. This sufficiently testifies that the wise also engage in joyful play so that sadness may be taken from them.

Parents should also not withhold their children from marriage for too long, lest fleshly lust draw the children into this vice.

You must earnestly guard your children from evil company, especially from slandered men and women, so that they may be honorably protected and raised. Just as some are drawn into these vices out of sadness and despondency, others are deceived through poverty. Therefore, an authority should keep a faithful eye on the poor, troubled hearts, helping them abundantly, speaking to them kindly, and standing by other people in faithful love, so that these people are preserved from this misery and wretchedness and also set free. Much misfortune grows out of poverty, for Hegesippus says in Book 5, chapter 18: poverty strips away all propriety and establishes shame. We should provide for the poor and not defy or grieve them, as we have described regarding Agrippa in Josephus, Book 18, chapter 2 of the *Antiquities*, and Fulgosus, Book 4, chapter 4.

Likewise, others are defiled with sorcery for the sake of pride, fleshly lust, and greed, desiring great goods, wealth, power, and worldly honors. When they cannot attain wealth, honor, and power, etc., by themselves, they make an agreement with Satan, who then helps them to wealth and power. However, it does not last long; the Devil soon lets them fall. Thus Satan also tempted Christ and said: "I will give you this world if you worship me," etc. The Devil did the same with Eve and subsequently with all the world on earth.

# Discovery of all the most prominent articles of Sorcery.

## Ee ij

To increase, diminish, or make God's work large or small, and also to preserve and protect it from all evil—regardless of the fact that God has blessed and spoken well of all things from eternity—is impossible. For what God has once blessed remains blessed for eternity; it cannot be further blessed or improved by any creature. Likewise, everything blessed by God cannot be slandered by men. God's Spirit does not allow itself to be constrained by men (says the wise man) in stone, wood, ore, herb, wax, etc., such that man has power over the Spirit, to resist or compel the Spirit. God's Spirit desires to dwell only in the heart of man. Regarding this, the Lord says: *I will turn your blessing into a curse* <note>Malachi 2:2</note> because you do not dwell and walk according to my heart; and conversely, for the good, he turns the curse into a blessing.

For a greater understanding of this declaration of the little word "blessing," we should understand that the word "to bless" is used and taken in three ways: First, to make good, righteous, and holy. Second, to speak well, to praise, and to pray to God for others. As when Melchizedek blessed Abraham, he spoke well of him and prayed to God for him, that he might be blessed in all his life.

Likewise, Jacob blessed all his sons and grandchildren; he prayed to the Lord that they would be made great and blessed by Him.

Thirdly, "to bless" is sometimes used for "to curse," as it is written of Naboth, that he was said to have "blessed" <note>meaning blasphemed</note> God and the King.

Likewise, Satan said to Christ the Lord and God: *Touch all that Job possesses, his belongings and goods, and he will bless you to your face*—that is, he will curse you.

The first kind of blessing belongs to God alone and to no creature. He alone blesses us, makes us great, and gives us His benediction <note>original: "benediction"</note>, to which all power is subject, and He alone can and will sustain us. Thus God blessed the world, saying: *Be fruitful and multiply*, etc. Likewise, David says: *May God bless us so that we come into your knowledge; the Lord will*

<column-break/>

*bless us*, and says further, *give His blessing*, etc.

Now, whoever wishes to increase or diminish creatures, or to bless them in such a way, must be God and no man or creature. For making a thing larger than it was created by God Himself does not rest in the hand and power of the creation, but of the Creator. Also, the blesser must always be greater than the blessed. He alone is the one who blesses, sanctifies, makes great, and sustains everything under His power, and no creature does. Whatever is now blessed must and shall be blessed, sanctified, and sustained by Him who is able and capable of blessing; otherwise, it is all in vain and lost.

The second kind of blessing is a work of faith and the love of God, as when we pray for the right understanding and welfare of our neighbor, as Jacob did, that God would protect him and keep him in His shelter. Not that we are capable of such things through our own strength and power, stretching our words so high that they wish to grasp at God's power and glory; rather, we only wait upon, pray to, and desire from God the Lord that His grace and power may hover over us, etc.

The third kind of blessing is to hold God and one's neighbor as nothing, to sit upon His throne, power, and glory. These desperate, poor people "bless" God—that is, they curse and scold God, bearing impatience toward His Cross, and seating themselves in His place, wishing through their own wit and power to be more capable than God. These speak useless things (says David), saying: *Our tongue shall prevail; it is our right to speak; who is our Lord? Who will master us? What we speak and do is righteous and good; it must all be valid; no one shall contradict it.*

These are the people who, out of their own presumption, undertake to bless and enchant <note>original: "incantiren"</note> creatures; indeed, they truly awaken the curse rather than the blessing upon them. God will also give them the curse instead of the blessing. How could they bless, do good, or speak well, while they are evil and do not walk in the faith of God? Indeed, their dealings are nothing but lies and evil-speaking, imagining that if they bless certain words with invented, strange...

speak certain characters <note>magical signs or sigils</note> over people and livestock, as well as other creatures; soon they are to be helped or the Devil with his phantom is to be driven away by it. In this, however, they are more deceived, for the Devil does not retreat for the sake of the blessing or the word, nor does he allow himself to be so easily overwhelmed. We have an example of this in the sons of Sceva <note>referencing Acts 19:13-16</note>, who undertook to cast out devils in the name of Jesus, as Paul had done, and yet had no faith. To them the Devil spoke thus: "Jesus I know, and Paul I know well, but who are you?" And the evil spirit leaped upon them, mastered them, and threw them under him, so that they escaped from him naked and wounded. Therefore, guard yourselves well, you miserable blessers; desist from this abomination and phantom, if you wish not to be banished by God and not to be deceived by the Devil.

Here we have two kinds of blessers or sorcerers. Some are on the right side, who wish to have acted well and Christianly thereby; they are not ashamed of their error and wish to be held in high regard for it, despite those who punish them for it—as the monks, nuns, and priests do. They imagine that with their good words and works, though with a deceived delusion, they can make a god out of creatures, blessing Christ out of bread, wine, etc.

Likewise, to bless or consecrate salt, water, herbs, wax, bells, temples, ore, churchyards, etc., and wherever these are used, all phantoms in the air, water, and on earth must retreat. This is a right folly, for the Devil does not flee these things; indeed, he has more cause to deceive you therein.

The other blessing is on the left side, where some use all kinds of good and evil words, with understanding and without understanding, using characters, crosses, "tau" signs <note>the T-shaped cross</note>, etc., thereby intending to protect and transform creatures.

Such as those who bless and conjure their own and others' swords and weapons, so that they may not be hurt or damaged by them; as has often happened, that one has danced upon them with a bare body. The cause was the herb called *mala fides* <note>Latin: "bad faith" or "treachery"</note>.

Others conjure and bless their artillery, not only so that they are not hurt by it, but so that they may hurt and damage other people without fail. What blessings, sorcery, etc., they use for this, I will not reveal at this time, so that others do not take occasion from this sorcery.

In addition, one also finds certain desperate people who, in the Devil's name, lie down on Saint Andrew's night and bless themselves for it, because their spouse is supposed to appear to them on that same night. This then often happens through the Devil's cunning, so that they may be confirmed in their idolatry.

Many are also found who have blessings and characters of a wondrous kind written on virgin parchment <note>parchment made from the skin of a stillborn animal, often used in magic</note>, and sometimes hang the Gospel of St. John around their neck. They have the words *Adonay* <note>Hebrew: "Lord"</note>, *Ananizapta* <note>a magical word used against epilepsy or plague</note>, *tetragrammaton* <note>Greek: the four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>, etc., engraved on gold or silver; this is then supposed to be good against sudden death, pestilence, and other afflictions, as if God's power were contained in these writings. But this is a withdrawal from God and right folly before Christians.

Furthermore, the godless blesser should never be spared, who shamelessly and publicly, with great blindness, dares to bless wounds, stabs, blood, "limb-water" <note>synovial fluid or lymph</note>, etc., with foolish words. Soon the wound or stab is to be healed and the blood or water stilled; they forget thereby all natural types and means through which the affliction could otherwise be helped.

Here I cannot remain silent about the story of a foolish woman who once came in haste to a schoolboy, exhorted him with all diligence and earnestness that he should quickly trace and copy the slip of paper she showed in her hand, so that she might be delivered from her dripping, running eyes by hanging the slip around her neck. But the boy could not read the slip because of its fadedness—as they all are—so the boy quickly wrote these words: "May the devil tear this old woman's eyes out." He gave the slip to the woman to hang around her neck; soon the woman became healthy. The slip did as much as her hanging it on her neck; all of which the devil did so that the superstition in the woman would be strengthened.

# Discovery of all the most prominent articles of Sorcery.

I have seen a great "Hansen"—as they call a charlatan—named Lösch, performing incantations and blessings. He employed this error: he took the sick person, set them immediately upon the hearth, and bound a slip of paper upon them filled with desperate letters and characters <note>magical symbols or sigils</note>. I later read this slip, in which nothing was written but pure devils: Lucifer, Satan, Beelzebub, Oriens, Belial, Pargiman, Maman, Bubloss, Coap, Abiger, Barbaras, Narthim, Oleasat, Bilech, Curson, etc. What kind of "blessing" that was, every Christian can well understand. God preserve us from this malediction <note>original: "Malediction," meaning a curse</note>, where God was never called upon, but only the Devil. Nor was that person helped; the evil faith they both shared saw to that. Furthermore, there are many of the poor folk who, in desperate faith, bless and enchant their livestock—oxen, pigs, sheep, dogs, etc.—so that these are not eaten or torn apart by wolves, bears, and other beasts. They put so much of their faith into this that they are occasionally helped; however, this is not through the power of the blessing, but through the Devil's help. Experience shows this: a "blesser" commended his and other people's cattle to luck through his blessing; soon the Devil took charge of the cattle and protected them after his fashion, so that they remained unharmed by wild animals, whereby the human was once again deceived.

Another thing we see in daily practice among the common rabble: if someone has been bitten by a rabid dog, horse, ox, pig, sheep, etc., they abandon all natural means and the art <note>medical skill</note> by which they might be helped. They fall back on blessings and other sorcery and idolatry to be helped. They bless and cauterize the damaged livestock without any method or reason; they make use of phantoms, characters, or "keys" and other tomfoolery, such as Saint Rupert’s, Saint Eligius’s <note>original: "Sanct Logij," likely St. Eligius, patron of horses and smiths</note>, and others. Wherever these are used, the livestock is supposed to be helped immediately. But this is a folly; indeed, they sometimes cauterize an animal on the forehead when it has been bitten on the hindquarters, believing some Divine power to be hidden in the keys, though they differ in no way from any other iron. No one wishes to dispute the use of cauterization and other natural means to help the livestock; indeed, where the animal is bitten or injured, it should be cauterized with iron and anointed at the wound or bite, so that the poison may be drawn out by the fire or ointment and the animal helped.

<column-break/>

Not only do these blinded people make use of external idolatry and works, but out of deliberate deceit, they create characters and "childbed crosses" <note>protective amulets for women in labor</note> over the door. They write letters with strange, invented script that no one understands—not even they themselves know what it is—which is supposed to be good against hail, wind, fire, mice, and rats, as I have seen myself. Likewise, they give letters to humans and animals to eat, which is supposed to be good for madness or "deaf-sickness" <note>likely epilepsy or vertigo</note>; in this, however, nothing but a deception is driven by the Devil. May God have mercy on them. In addition to this, I have seen several more who presumed to bless the weather, as if God must be obedient to miserable humans regarding His firmament, and that whatever they wish must happen immediately. This is true jugglery before God and Christians, for truly God and Nature do not wish to be mastered by man in such a way, especially while they possess such presumption without faith or love.

Much could be written of the blessings of St. John, St. Quirinus, and St. Stephen, for great idolatry and witchcraft are practiced with them. They believe they can discover and heal all "revenge" or "penance" <note>referring to magical afflictions or "witches' shots"</note> by these means. They lay stones in the fire; if the stone then hisses or swells, the penance or revenge is judged accordingly. All of this is the work of the Devil and true witches.

Likewise, another folly follows these poor people, which I have often seen: when a beast, sheep, dog, etc., has broken a leg, they immediately bind a chair leg with cloths and leave the animal or beast unbound. Then the animal is supposed to be helped by this. That this has often happened was done by the Devil, so that the human is deceived and confirmed in idolatry. This is once again an abomination; for as soon as the animal is not helped by nature, herbs, medicine, etc., the Devil then becomes the apothecary or physician.

He who now, despite this report, still wishes to bless, takes the creature he intends to bless out of God's hands and places it into the Devil's protection and power—of which he actually has none—making himself into a god as Lucifer did, wishing to be equal and similar to God, because he believes protection and power rest more in his own hands than in God's hands and power.

These are indeed desperate people who do not hold God for God; they trust the Devil more than God the Lord. Why should the pious, faithful God pay the price, that one does not believe or trust Him as much or more than the creature, which can do nothing without God and must have everything from Him? God alone can and will bless, from whom we also have all comfort, blessing, benediction, help, and faith; may God give us this out of grace, Amen.

Now the things belonging to the <term>Theory and Practice</term><note>Latin: "Theorica vnd Practica" - the intellectual framework and the actual performance of magic</note> are ended. Further, it is to be noted what is required regarding the imprisonment and death of witches and sorcerers: as soon as they are captured, their <term>Ascendant</term><note>In this context, the author refers to a familiar spirit or a personal demon that "ascends" to influence the person</note> comes and comforts them at times, telling them how he will

<column-break/>

release them, so that they may be and remain steadfast in unbelief, since he still needs them for his abomination. He speaks to them in a friendly manner, although he deceives them many times, for often God will not have it so, so that the abomination may be abolished. Yet the Devil does not leave them, so that they might not be converted to God; therefore he sometimes wrings their necks when he cannot help them. Yes, he sometimes does not leave them even at the court or on the way to it, which is why there is such a monstrous haunting of ghosts about them. For this reason, it is necessary that one takes good care and heed of them, comforting them intensely with God's word—for teaching does not return without fruit—and proclaiming the mercy of God through Jesus Christ: that God does not desire the death of the sinner, but rather that he be converted. The mercy of God is greater than the sins of the world (Genesis 3, 4; Chronicles 22; Lamentations 2; Micah 7, etc.). Now the Ascendant will abandon them, for he cannot endure that, since there is no fellowship between God and the Devil; in the hope that she will be considered with grace by God and rescued from the Devil.

No more shall be written at this time of the abomination and the earnest haunting and vermin of sorcery, <term>stallions</term><note>Likely a reference to "Hengsten" as a term for male practitioners or a specific type of familiar</note>, witches, etc., since their actions are sufficiently recognized. Nothing is lacking therein except to act earnestly, which I wish to commend entirely to the Authorities. With an earnest warning: do not easily undertake anything in this matter without a special, great cause, so that no one is so harshly tortured in innocence; yet also do not let it pass by while sleeping where there might be cause to deal with these poor people, so that the abomination may be uprooted and dried up before God and men.

Let all this rest for the time being, as it is not my office at this moment. But where there is need, I will hereafter describe as much for improvement from proven writings.

-> End of the Thirteenth Little Treatise. <-

## Preface

<margin>Various opinions of those who have written about witches.</margin>
Many learned men before and during our time have written about witches—who are commonly called sorceresses, or in Low Saxon *Töuerschen*—and indeed, have made great books: wherein they diligently and extensively treat not only of their nature, power, deeds, and art (if one should call their fantasy and devilish jugglery an "art") but also of the signs or marks by which they are to be recognized, and the punishment with which to chastise them. However, they are not all entirely of one opinion. For the greatest part follows custom and old usage. Some, while wishing to punish the disagreements and errors of others, devise new errors themselves and obscure the matter more and more the longer they go on. Many of them also attribute more to witches, and some less, than is proper.

So too, regarding the signs and testimony, they are likewise not of one opinion: because one party completely rejects and considers as deceptive the signs which the opposing side holds as right and certain.

<column-break/>

Conversely, there are also some who claim that such witches as we have were not present in former times, and therefore should not be subject to the punishment that was customary among the ancients. Thus, some want them to be punished either because of the misdeeds attributed to them, or on the other hand, because they have shamefully fallen away from God and denied Him. In summary, there is no measure or end to the differing opinions in this matter. From this, not only the common man but also the rulers often pass unequal judgments; out of harmful prejudices, they sometimes commit grave errors. This happens (as said) because of the manifold opinions of the writers, who do not speak with one voice on the same subject. This occurs not only in this business—which in itself is always dark (as it flows from the Father of Darkness, of error, and of all destruction)—but also in matters of religion and the interpretation of Holy Scripture, where in the same way men are miserably disturbed, led astray, and divided <margin>Discord of Religion.</margin> by

# Preface.

...because of such unevenness of opinions. Since one person holds as right that which another recognizes as wrong, and one praises what another despises, nothing other than a miserable condition and the ruin of the Church of God has arisen. In some places, the authorities proceed with terrible tyranny and violence, while the subjects are shaken and destroyed by despondency, fear, hatred, envy, rebellion, and discord among one another.

Therefore, everyone can easily perceive what a difficult matter I have now undertaken, of which the beautiful saying or aphorism of the old Hippocrates may rightly be said: *the experiment is dangerous, the judgment difficult.* <note>original: "das versuchen ist gefährlich/ das urtheil schwerlich." A translation of the famous Latin "Ars longa, vita brevis, occasio praeceps, experimentum periculosum, iudicium difficile."</note> For one cannot easily hit the exact point where the true ground of truth resides amidst so many different and unequal opinions, or at least find a middle path upon which one may walk safely, doing harm neither to the truth nor to the common peace—that is, neither grieving the innocent nor strengthening the guilty in their malice. Since this is difficult for a lover of Justice and the Fear of God to achieve (would to God I could rightly boast of these two virtues), I carry the certain hope that the pious reader will not take it ill of me if I should perhaps follow the opinion of him who says: in doubtful matters, one should agree with the most equitable opinion; or that other saying, that it is better to leave a guilty person unpunished than to punish an innocent one. For I do this by no means with the intention of defending sin, but rather so that no injustice occurs, and so that all kinds of causes for the manifold disaster, which I mentioned shortly before, might be prevented.

<margin>
1. aph. 1. <note>Reference to Hippocrates' Aphorisms, Section 1.</note>
</margin>

<margin>
Digest on the Rules of Law, law "factum cuiq; suum." Digest on penalties. Also law "omnib. quidem" in the same. <note>Citations to the Corpus Iuris Civilis, the body of Roman Law used in early modern legal arguments.</note>
</margin>

Also, the authorities will rightly grant me the favor of using that same freedom which others before me have likewise used: namely, that I may publicly declare my opinion on common matters. This is especially so because these things belong, to a certain extent, to the Doctors of Medicine, and physicians are often not a little troubled by them. Furthermore, I do not do this as if I, like a new lawmaker, wished to prescribe a certain rule for the authorities which they must always follow. Rather, I wish to give guidance to all who read this my reflection, so that by comparing the manifold opinions, they may recognize for themselves which is best, and not accept or follow something they do not rightly understand. And when it comes to the Judgment, they should proceed and act in such a way that they do not later have cause for regret, and find by experience the truth of what the Poet said:

> If you judge the verdict wrongly,
> Then God will punish you rightly.

I intend, however, to handle the matter in this order: first, I shall speak of the nature, power, works, and deeds of witches; second, of the signs or marks by which they are to be recognized; third and finally, of the punishment of which they are rightly guilty. For in these three parts, which are the most necessary, we wish to encompass the entire matter. Not that I wish to treat these parts exhaustively (for what would it profit to do again what has already been well performed by others? Or how could I encompass a vast sea in a narrow brook?), but rather that I only run through the summary of these things, intending this time to explain more what injustice occurs therein than what ought rightly to happen (though both will nonetheless be indicated to some extent).

# Concerning Witches by Doctor Johann Ewich.

<margin>The many names for witches.</margin> Just as the Greek and Hebrew names are quite diverse, so too are the Latin: namely, *Saga* <note>a wise-woman or female diviner</note>, *Lamia* <note>a man-eating monster or night-witch</note>, *Striges* <note>screech-owls or hags</note>, *Venefica* <note>poisoner or sorceress</note>, *Malefica* <note>evildoer</note>, *incantatrix* <note>enchantress</note>, *Maga* <note>magician</note>, *Præstigiatrix* <note>illusionist</note>, *Pithonica* <note>pythoness or spirit-medium</note>, *Sortilega* <note>fortune-teller</note>, *pharmakis* <note>original Greek: φαρμακὶς; a dealer in drugs or spells</note>, *pharmakeutria* <note>original Greek: φαρμακεύτρια; a female sorceress</note>, *goēteis* <note>original Greek: γοητεὶς; charlatans or sorcerers</note>, *epōdoi* <note>original Greek: ἐπωδοὶ; chanters of incantations</note>, *Chobarim* <note>original Hebrew: חֹבֵר; charmers or those who tie knots</note>, etc. And all of these have their own particular meanings, as is well known to those experienced in languages. In German they are called *Hexen* <note>witches</note>, *Vnholden* <note>monsters or demons</note>, *Zauberinnen* <note>sorceresses</note>; in Lower Saxony, *Töuerschen*, etc. I have not undertaken to provide a further interpretation of these names at this time; rather, he who desires such and can understand it may seek them out from others who have written extensively on this. For I intend only to give a brief report on the aforementioned matters, which are the most useful and necessary. And for my part, everyone is free to use whatever words they wish, provided that through misunderstanding or the mixing of terms, the things understood by those words and names are not also mixed up and misinterpreted. For strictly speaking, the foreign words and our German words do not mean exactly the same thing; for example, the Latin words *Venefica* <note>poisoner</note> and *incantatrix* <note>enchantress</note>, or *Maga* <note>magician</note>. Likewise the German *Hexen* <note>witches</note> and *Zauberin* <note>sorceress</note>. This arises from the fact that the people burdened with this "devil-sickness" are not all of one kind, nor do they commit the same works. For it happens for the most part that just as there is a kinship among the virtues, so too among the vices, sins, and crimes there is a relationship whereby one is related to another—especially in the vices, to which the path <margin>In *Works and Days*.</margin> (as Hesiod says) is nearer, and which are easily obtained, indeed in great heaps. And it would be only fair that a distinction be maintained, and that the same guilt and punishment not be imposed on all the accused merely for the sake of the names (because they are so misused), unless they were sufficiently convicted and found guilty of each misdeed in particular. There are many among the witches who have never given poison to anyone, and yet they are called *Veneficæ*, that is, poisoners, and are held and punished as such. Just as if one wanted to hold and punish all thieves and murderers, and all heretics, as willful, cunning deceivers because perhaps theft is mixed with murder, and intentional deception is perceived in some heresy—what sensible person would be able to praise or justify that? But this belongs to the third part.

As to what witches actually are, of whom we are to treat, the <margin>What witches are; three descriptions.</margin> three following descriptions shall clearly show us. The first is taken almost word-for-word from Ulrich Molitor, who was once a Professor of Canon Law and counselor to Archduke Sigismund of Austria: Witches are accursed women who, although they can accomplish nothing in reality, nevertheless, through the incitement of Satan—on account of poverty, mistrust, conceived hatred, or other temptations of the Devil to which they did not offer resistance as they rightly should have—depart from the good God and, as it were, sacrifice themselves to Satan, and thus attach themselves to an oversized heresy, that is, the society of devils.

The second description was provided by <margin>1st Part of the Disputations against Paracelsus, chapter 8, etc.</margin> the excellent physician of the German nation, Dr. Thomas Erastus, with the following words: A *Saga* or witch is a sorceress, or a juggler, or by whatever name one wishes to call her, who, after she has renounced God and the true religion, gives herself over to Satan through a public covenant, so that—besides many other promises and hopes—she learns from him to disturb the elements by the conjuration of herbs and other things harmless by their nature, to create storms, to inflict harm upon people, cattle, and grain, and to do many other wonderful things impossible to nature.

To this description, although it is complete and not easily improved upon, I have nevertheless wished to add my own, which is almost identical to the previous ones, and it reads thus: Witches are human beings, mostly of the female sex, who deny the true God and renounce Him: through the seduction, cunning, counsel, and incitement of Satan, to whom they also, through a superstitious...

# On Witches

...make a covenant as their own, and with his help, they undertake to do many improper and unbelievable things, mostly to the ruin of other people, with foolish ceremonies and gestures, or at least with terrible wishes and curses. This description encompasses almost the entire nature and kind of witches of whom we speak, and it is therefore useful that we explain the same further and in an orderly fashion. For the question of whether witches actually exist, I consider unnecessary, since (alas) there are all too many of them in this latter age of the world. But whether they also existed in former times or not, I do not wish to dispute at this time, since it is certain that they either existed, or others of the same kind existed—at least as far as guilt and criminal law are concerned—as shall be further indicated hereafter.

<margin>Whether witches actually exist.</margin>

<margin>Witches are human beings, unchanged in their human essence.</margin>

Thus, first in our description, it is said that witches are human beings. Indeed, no sensible person can deny this <insert>or substance</insert>. That such is the case is evident not only from the external appearance and shape of the human being, but also from the internal form, and all the natural powers, words, and works that arise from the same. For the "form"—as the natural philosophers <note>original: "Naturkündiger"</note> say—gives to every thing its essence, from which things then commonly take their names; so much so that the experienced logicians <note>original: "Dialectici"</note> are accustomed to call names "unexplained descriptions," and conversely, descriptions "expanded, explained names." Therefore, if a creature is deprived of the aforementioned form, it no longer remains the same creature it was before, even if it keeps the same name—just as a dead man or a dead lion, or a counterfeit of the same which never had such an internal form, are called by the same names in a figurative way, because one has no more convenient names, or for the sake of their previous state when they were still unchanged, or also because of the likeness and external shape. But if the internal form—which, as mentioned, was called by Aristotle a "perfection" and "soul"—

<margin>Form.</margin>

<margin>Entelechy <note>original Greek: "Εντελέχεια" – a term used by Aristotle to describe the realization or complete expression of a thing's potential.</note></margin>

<column-break/>

is entirely changed or taken away, then one says that the creature is dead, come to nothing, and become carrion, or has turned into another thing, and henceforth is no longer what it was before, nor is it properly called so anymore.

Since this is the case, as reported, many people are rightly amazed that a new writer a short time ago—when he wanted to state the reason why witches, when they are thrown into the water and thus tested, do not sink downward but float on top just like pumice stone—wrote: That they have lost the state of their previous form (for thus his words sound in Latin) from the time they made a covenant with Satan, and are no longer the humans they were before as far as the internal form is concerned. Indeed, he claims they have taken on an entirely new form or nature, so that they may be called humans who have become partakers of the Devil's essence by which they are possessed. And so that he might bring to light not only unheard-of and newly-invented wondrous talk, but also his own incompetence in philosophy and his reckless theology, he adds such a foundation to this wondrous fable of his: For the evil spirit (he says), a spirit and prince of the air who is the cause and origin of all sin, has so taken possession of the hearts and other limbs of the evil women that he is entirely and essentially poured out and mixed into their whole substance and every part of the same (O terrible words!), in such a way that as long as they have done no true repentance and improved themselves, he cannot be absent or depart from any part of their body; and that for this reason, witches can neither think nor do anything good, but strive at all times for misfortune and to cause harm to other creatures, etc. As he then describes this there with more words, and finally concludes in confirmation of his opinion that no one should doubt that the powers and abilities of the entire body of witches are completely changed, and their previous...

<summary>The author argues that witches remain fundamentally human in essence and "form," rejecting a contemporary theory that claims their physical substance is literally replaced by the Devil's essence during the water test (ordeal by water).</summary>

# Doctor Johann Etwich.

...form entirely lost, etc. These are almost the words of this new writer, though translated here from the Latin.

<margin>Refutation of the previous opinion.</margin>
But what should one say about this wondrous speech and godless fiction? Nothing else, in my opinion, than what the matter itself reveals: namely, that this fiction is not only inconsistent and self-contradictory, but that it is also against Nature and against Theology, and wanders astray in many ways, falling far short of the truth.

For first, it is certain that by these words (the state of their previous form) he understands either the natural powers—insofar as the soul acts through the service of the body, and the body through the help of the soul—or else the internal form itself, which (as is said from Aristotle) is called <term>entelecheia</term> <note>original: "ἐντελέχεια"; a philosophical term for the actualization or "complete reality" of a being</note>, that is, a constant movement, or the life and essential shape of man, which forms him and gives him his shape and essence so that he is and is called a human being. Now, as far as those natural powers are concerned, it is not true that they are changed or entirely destroyed in witches. For we perceive, as has already been said, that they are just as strong, as healthy, and as capable and ready for all human works as they were before. For such naturally inborn qualities were not lost to man through the Fall of Adam, just as Satan did not lose his own, although his sin is much greater than the sin of man; for the former willfully and entirely abandoned God his Creator, while the latter only through the seduction of Satan, and out of hope of attaining more good, angered God, and was therefore reconciled again with God in Christ the Mediator, whereas the former can never come to reconciliation.

<margin>The Fall of Man and the Apostasy of Satan.</margin>
But as for the internal essential or substantial form (for it is to be noted that he intends this to be understood here, because he opposes and contrasts the substance of the Devil to it), this is no differently corrupted and changed in witches than in other sinful people. Although one sin is greater and heavier than another, some are not esteemed to be more or less human

<column-break/>

than others because of it. For if that were true, what would one then say of the Mamluks <note>A reference to Christians who converted to Islam to serve the Ottoman Empire</note> who defect to the Turks? Should these also have their internal form and human substance changed, and have received the substance of Satan in its place? Who has ever heard such monstrous talk? Is the God of the Turks then better than Satan? Or do the godless apostate Christians sin less than the seduced, straying witches? What shall one say? If the witches have entirely and utterly lost their previous internal form, and have taken on the substance of the Devil and become partakers of the same—so that henceforth they can no longer be esteemed as the previous humans, nor even as humans at all, other than how one regards dead men, or forest-devils, or werewolves (although these lose more the external than the internal shape, as some hold)—dear me, how does it happen then that one witch does not give birth to another? I do not think he believes that, and yet according to his opinion, it would have to happen. Likewise, why does he demand that witches do penance and improve themselves? For the will for this is not in the devils, but in humans, although they are often powerfully restrained and hindered by the Devil. And if they can no longer think or do anything good at all, how then shall they be converted? But if this is to be understood of them no differently than of other sinners—of whom the Scripture likewise speaks, saying they are not capable (namely, of their own power) of thinking anything good—why then should one invent such a wondrous transformation of witches, as if they had cast off all human form and nature and become entirely "bedeviled" or turned into devils? For penance is nothing else than remorse for the previous life, or as the Greek word sounds, a conversion of the heart to a better life, with a new essential birth. For although the Scripture speaks in this manner of Nebuchadnezzar, the Babylonian king,

<margin>Repentance <note>original: "Metanoia"</note></margin>

# Concerning Witches

<margin>
Jerome, 4th of August.
*The City of God* <note>original: "de ciuitate D." referring to St. Augustine's work</note>
Book 18.
</margin>
...as if he had been changed into a wild beast; yet this must not be understood according to the literal letter. Otherwise, he would not have been spiritually reborn, but would have become a new man according to his substance (for nothing rises again that has not previously fallen, as Tertullian says). And thus one would have to judge all sinners—indeed, all people, since all people are sinners—in the same way, which is entirely absurd.

Furthermore, there has never been a pagan philosopher or naturalist whose opinion was that the internal corruption of man was a discarding of his substance, or that improvement was a new substantial birth.

<margin>
Sin is no
substance.
</margin>
Likewise, theologians and scholars of the Scripture have never been so mad—excepting the legacy of Flacius Illyricus, that follower of the old heretic Manichaeus—as to hold that sin is a substantial being. They did not believe that when sin enters a man, the man's essence perishes; or that when sin is destroyed, a new substance or essence is created. For from that it would follow that there would never be any true humans, because sin is always in man; and that no humans would ever be reborn, because sin always remains in man. Or else, that all humans should always have two kinds of substance or essence within them, namely a human one and a devilish one (which is much more terrible to say than if one said they were all possessed by the devil). Thus they would be gruesome monsters and unnatural beasts, or like the fables tell of *Melusina* <note>original: "Melefinæ", likely referring to the folklore water-spirit Melusine</note>, the feminized devil (for some hold that the devil can transform himself into the image of a woman or a man), and perhaps a man's children, just as the pagans held their heroes to be half-human and half-god. Not far from these two opinions and superstitions are those who demand an "essential righteousness" (which is as a part of Christ) within man. Likewise, those who [treat] original sin through

<margin>
Osiander. <note>Andreas Osiander (1498–1552), a reformer who argued that justification was the indwelling of Christ's divine nature, rather than a legal declaration.</note>
</margin>

<column-break/>

words (as if sin and the devil were one and the same, and could be coerced with words) and wish to drive and banish it out of man. But sin and the devil are widely different things: the latter is a creature of God, the former a corruption in the creatures—just as a sickness and the sick body in which the sickness dwells are different. Indeed, the sickness is not to be driven away with words, but through the finger of God and healing medicine, as is to be understood below.

Therefore, since this is so, it is manifest how intolerable this Manichaean doctrine is within the church of God—both regarding the essential change of man and the essential fellowship with the substance of the devil on account of present sin. For according to the opinion of the very best theologians, sin is (as has been said) a corruption of the substance only insofar as it concerns the *quality*—such as purity, uprightness, perfection, constancy, and dignity—or to put it more briefly (in which also the Image of God, according to which man was first created, consists): righteousness and honor. It does not concern the essence or the substance itself. And Satan, who brought about such corruption in man, is not mixed with man in an essential way, or through the pouring out of his essence like a seed. Rather, through false inspiration and with deceitful counsel, he seduced and corrupted the first humans. Otherwise, Eve would have had to be possessed by the devil; indeed, after the fall, she would have become a *Melusina*, which is terrifying to think, let alone to write or speak of. And all of us together (as previously mentioned) who descend from Eve would be gruesome monsters, indeed mere Merlins <note>likely referring to changelings or demonic offspring</note> or Satyrs. Fie upon such shameful talk! Such godless philosophers and heretical theologians should be sent to the Turks, not tolerated in Reformed academies and cities, and much less in the school of Christ.

# On Witches

...given to understand: that the aforementioned figure <note>referring to a magical sigil or talisman mentioned on the previous page</note> cannot, by its own nature or use, perform such things. Whoever ascribes such power to it must consider that this power comes from elsewhere: namely from God, from the Devil, or from men. It cannot come from God, because His order and institution do not operate in this way. Nor can human art bring such things to pass. From this it follows that either there is no special power within it, or it must have entered through Satan. Now consider what one should think of the "barbaric" words of sorcerers <note>original: "Barbarischen... worten," referring to *voces magicae* or nonsensical incantations</note>, or the misuse of other words; likewise of artificial and invented signs, or the improper use of other symbols. From where do they derive their power when they seem to accomplish something extraordinary beyond their nature? Namely, from the master Satan. This could be further proven if our current purpose allowed it. But since Satan is a liar, a deceiver, and a destroyer and corrupter of all things, he must not be trusted at all when he offers us such misuses of words and signs and boasts of them with false miracles.

<margin>Imagination or fantasy.</margin>
Regarding "Imagination" or fantasy—to which Avicenna <note>A famous Persian philosopher and physician (c. 980–1037)</note>, along with the poets and the common rabble, ascribes many wonderful powers, such as the ability to change the elements, turn rain into ice, pull the moon from the sky, transplant crops, or turn humans into wolves, cats, or other animals (indeed, what not?)—it is all either gross lies or devilish phantoms. For human imagination can only move the body in which it resides, just as animals are guided by their own imagination, not by that of another. Because the soul of man—of which imagination or fantasy is a specific power and work—is in man as the <term>Forma</term> <note>The "form" or animating principle in Aristotelian philosophy</note> is in its matter, it acts only therein. It cannot move a foreign, distant thing without intermediate means, nor can it change anything outside its own body or subject, for such power is given to no creature.

<margin>Petrus Pomponatius.</margin>
To this belongs the story told of Petrus Pomponatius <note>Pietro Pomponazzi (1462–1525), an Italian philosopher who sought natural explanations for "miracles"</note>, who was once an excellent physician in Italy. As he was once traveling across the countryside, he saw to one side in a pasture a crowd of peasants who had begun to flay and skin a poor, senseless <term>Lycanthropum</term> <note>A person suffering from lycanthropy, the delusion of being a wolf</note> (that is, one who held himself to be a wolf). They wanted to see if he was <term>versipellis</term> <note>Latin for "turn-skin," a werewolf whose fur grows on the inside</note>, that is, if he had "turned hair." For the sick man himself said he was a "bear-wolf" <note>original: "Beerwolff," an archaic term for werewolf</note> and told the peasants to get away from him, otherwise he would tear them all apart and eat them. For it was an old, false delusion of theirs that humans could be changed in this way. But Pomponatius, who understood the matter better, informed them otherwise; he took the sick man to himself and healed him through good medicine.

<column-break/>

The inexperienced rabble is still possessed by the same error, believing that witches are sometimes transformed into cats and perform wonderful dances and other foolish acts in such transformed or invisible forms; yet these are mostly dreams or devilish phantoms. Furthermore, Satan suggests many things to witches in their sleep and persuades them that they have done this or that, which in truth never happened. He who cannot believe this gives sufficient proof that he is entirely inexperienced in the great confusion found among witches and those who are meant to punish them.

All of this is not to say that witches are not guilty of many great sins. For even if they had no others, this sin would be far too great: that they knowingly and willingly (which no one can deny) renounce God their Creator and give themselves over to Satan. But that people ascribe many things to them as if they had done what they cannot even do—that I consider improper. Likewise, that which they have done, and which they have in common with several other sinners, is regarded and punished so harshly in them as if it were a mortal sin, while in others it is counted as a minor thing—who could approve of that?

-># Doctor Johann Ewich.<-

**To the Doctors of Medicine**, who daily deal with the sick and hear the unlearned opinions regarding the causes and remedies of diseases, this cannot seem strange. For how many are there among the common rabble and peasants who, when some harm befalls their own bodies, their cattle, their households, or their goods, do not immediately suspect some old crone? And against such sorcery (God forbid), do they not use various blessings and the signing of the cross as customary and permitted means (as they believe)? Indeed, they are not ashamed even to ask the Doctors whether they cannot perceive such ailments from the urine—O luxurious, irrational, miserable people, indeed not at all unlike the witches themselves. But because they have once imagined this false opinion regarding certain secret and suddenly occurring violent illnesses, for which they perceive no other preceding cause, it must be to them nothing but witchcraft. This is so even though the Physicians <note>original: "Medici"</note> better understand the true causes: namely, that those who have accumulated more blood and moisture than before, and are well-formed and strong, are often prone to fall suddenly into heavy bodily weakness. Of this, the old Hippocrates is a sufficient witness, where he says in his aphorisms that the well-conditioned bodies of athletes, when they have reached their highest point, cannot remain there and are not without danger. And yet we will never deny that many ailments can occur of which we have no certain knowledge, nor can have; but such things are then to be commended more to the omniscience of God than to be judged according to our mad thoughts, putting others in mortal danger over them—but no more of this.

Just as God is a Creator and sustainer of all His creatures, and especially desires to preserve the human race, so on the contrary Satan (who for that reason is rightly called Abaddon by St. John, and Zabolus by Cyprian) seeks nothing else than to destroy the same, and uses for that purpose all those he can bring about as servants and helpers. But he especially envies and is hostile to the faith, love, and unity of the God-fearing, and sees nothing more gladly than their persecution and downfall.

# Of Witches

<margin>Note.</margin>
There are many and various ways by which he <note>the Devil</note> appears to keep his faith and promises to his witches, so that they do not labor in vain. For he does not always desire to lie, but indeed always to deceive and to harm. In short, he is accustomed to hide and adorn his villainy—as has been said—with his art of jugglery; thus he also trains his disciples, the witches, and teaches them likewise to decorate their godless acts with all kinds of juggling ceremonies. For this reason, the excellently learned and experienced man Dr. Johann Weyer <note>original: "D. Iohan. Vvier"</note>—the principal personal physician to the most illustrious and high-born Prince and Lord, Lord William, Duke of Jülich and Cleves, etc.—rightly and aptly titled and named his books which he wrote about witches, *On the Deceptions of Demons* <note>original Latin: "De præstigiis dæmonum"</note>, that is, of the juggling-works of the devil. But if perhaps there is no space nor time for the witch to perform such juggling ceremonies, then there is no lack of terrible wishes and curses, either poured out with unspeakable words or secretly conceived in the heart without words. Which, although they can do nothing to the matter (for such things return to where they came from), they nevertheless give to understand what cruel and great malice exists in the witches, and how powerfully Satan works within them.

This then is what has been briefly said so far regarding the first part of this treatise, which was spent almost entirely on the interpretation and explanation of the description, and which shows the nature, power, art, and deeds of witches in a reasonable manner. Therefore, the second part follows now, concerning the marks and testimonies by which they are to be recognized and through which they are to be convicted of guilt, so that we may deal more certainly with the punishment in the third part. But yet, I must first append here several special rules and maxims drawn from the first part, so that the most important points may be better kept in memory.

### Maxims and Rules of the First Part.

<column-break/>

THERE are many different opinions concerning witches.

Many different opinions make the matter obscure and difficult to understand.

On account of manifold and mixed names, one should not mix the things themselves nor judge them without distinction.

Sin, just like virtue, are related to one another, but are not to be mixed.

Witches are human beings, and they retain their previous form and their unaltered essence or substance, as well as natural affection toward their children.

Neither sin nor righteousness are essences or substances in man.

Sin is not built out of, nor is the sickness of the body driven away with words. For words, as well as signs, can do no more than indicate and signify.

Witches have no power beyond their nature, nor does Satan. For both have their determined power, which God nevertheless governs according to His pleasure.

Satan, properly speaking, can create nothing, but can only destroy what is created, insofar as it is granted to him by God.

Satan is an enemy of God, and desires that all sinners whom he seduces should also be so. Yet he cannot lead all sinners equally far away from God.

Neither Satan nor witches can perform true miracles. For such is the attribute of God alone, as is being Almighty and the Knower of Hearts.

Satan is a juggler <note>or "illusionist"</note>, and the master and prince of all jugglers.

Many things appear to blinded or deluded people as if they were happening, which nevertheless truly do not happen.

God has commanded to avoid the company and counsel of sorcerers just as much as sorcery itself.

Satan deceives, and is also sometimes deceived, and his schemes do not always succeed for him.

Wishes, curses, and imagination work only within those in whom they reside, unless God allows something to happen by way of a miracle, or works some wonder Himself therein.

<summary>This page concludes the first part of the treatise by defining the devil as a "juggler" who uses illusions to deceive, and provides a list of theological maxims regarding the limitations of witchcraft and satanic power.</summary>
